KEP-361.title: Local Ephemeral Storage Capacity Isolation
KEP-361.summary: This KEP introduces capacity isolation for local ephemeral storage on a node, allowing pods and containers to request and limit the amount of shared local disk space they consume. It adds support for tracking, scheduling, and evicting pods based on the new 'ephemeral-storage' resource similar to CPU and memory, enabling better resource guarantees and management for scratch space, caching, and logs.

KEP-557.title: CSI Volume Topology
KEP-557.summary: This KEP adds support for CSI volume topology by introducing the storage/v1 CSINode API object, enabling Kubernetes to understand and propagate topology information from CSI drivers. It allows topology-aware volume provisioning, scheduling, and spreading, improving placement of stateful workloads across zones and nodes.

KEP-121.title: Local Persistent Volumes
KEP-121.summary: The KEP adds support for PersistentLocalVolumes, a new in‑tree volume plugin that exposes local disks, partitions, or directories as PersistentVolumes with node affinity, enabling pods to use high‑performance local storage as a persistent resource. This provides better performance and cost efficiency for stateful workloads such as databases and caches, while integrating with existing Kubernetes storage primitives like StorageClass and PVCs.

KEP-2924.title: In-tree Storage Plugin to CSI Migration - Ceph Cephfs
KEP-2924.summary: This KEP adds feature gates to migrate the in‑tree CephFS volume plugin to the external CephFS CSI driver. When enabled alongside the generic CSIMigration gate, Kubernetes redirects all CephFS volume operations to the CSI driver, simplifying management and aligning with the CSI migration strategy.

KEP-5381.title: Mutable PersistentVolume Node Affinity
KEP-5381.summary: This KEP proposes to make PersistentVolume.spec.nodeAffinity mutable, allowing the node affinity of a volume to be changed after creation. This enables users to migrate data or adopt new storage features without disrupting workloads, improving scheduling reliability.

KEP-177.title: CSI Snapshot
KEP-177.summary: This KEP implements CSI volume snapshot support in Kubernetes, introducing new VolumeSnapshot, VolumeSnapshotContent, and VolumeSnapshotClass APIs with required fields for snapshot source, deletion policies, and binding status. It also adds controller architecture changes, secret handling, leader election, and metrics to enable creating, deleting, and restoring snapshots via CSI drivers.

KEP-3762.title: PersistentVolume last phase transition time
KEP-3762.summary: This KEP proposes adding a new status field `lastPhaseTransitionTime` to PersistentVolumes, recording the timestamp of the most recent phase transition. The field enables administrators to sort, clean up, and monitor volumes based on how long they have been in a particular phase, improving observability and operational safety.

KEP-531.title: Online Growing Persistent Volume Size
KEP-531.summary: This KEP adds online file system resizing for PersistentVolumeClaims, allowing users to increase a PVC's size while it remains mounted by editing the PVC without restarting the pod. It improves availability by eliminating downtime associated with offline resizing.

KEP-1790.title: Recover from volume expansion failure
KEP-1790.summary: This KEP introduces a recovery mechanism for failed PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) expansions by allowing users to reduce the requested size and retry expansion. It adds new status fields (AllocatedResources, ResizeStatus/AllocatedResourceStatus) to accurately track allocated resources and expansion state, while updating quota calculations to prevent abuse.

KEP-556.title: Support for CSI volume resizing
KEP-556.summary: This KEP adds support for resizing CSI volumes, bringing CSI drivers to feature parity with in‑tree volume expansion. It introduces an external resize controller and extends kubelet behavior, and adds new CSIPersistentVolumeSource fields for per‑PVC secret references required by controller and node expansion RPCs.

KEP-1432.title: Volume Health Monitor
KEP-1432.summary: The Volume Health Monitor KEP adds a mechanism for CSI drivers and Kubelet to report health status of Persistent Volumes. It introduces a new VolumeHealthStats field in Kubelet's VolumeStats metrics and defines new CSI RPCs and capabilities to surface volume condition information, enabling early detection of storage issues via events and metrics.

KEP-3107.title: SecretRef field addition to NodeExpandVolume request
KEP-3107.summary: This KEP adds a `nodeExpandSecretRef` field to the CSI PersistentVolumeSource, allowing a secret to be passed from the kubelet to CSI drivers during the NodeExpandVolume RPC. The change enables per‑PVC secrets for volume resizing operations such as encrypted device expansion or backend size verification.

KEP-2644.title: Honor Persistent Volume Reclaim Policy
KEP-2644.summary: This KEP introduces the HonorPVReclaimPolicy feature gate to ensure that PersistentVolume reclaim policies (especially Delete) are honored even when a bound PV is deleted before its PVC. It adds finalizers to PVs for both CSI driver volumes and in-tree plugins to prevent premature removal of the PV object and guarantee proper deletion of the underlying storage asset, preventing volume leaks.

KEP-284.title: Growing Persistent Volume size
KEP-284.summary: This KEP adds support for dynamically expanding the size of a PersistentVolume by allowing users to modify the storage request in a bound PersistentVolumeClaim. It introduces a new volume_expand_controller to coordinate cloud‑provider volume resize and optional filesystem resize on the node, and updates PVC status conditions to reflect the resize progress. The feature is gated by ExpandPersistentVolumes and requires API changes to make pvc.spec.resources.requests.storage mutable and to expose new resize‑related status conditions.

KEP-1845.title: Prioritization on Volume Capacity
KEP-1845.summary: This KEP introduces a scheduler priority plugin that scores nodes based on how closely their statically provisioned PersistentVolumes match the capacity requested by PVCs, reducing waste of storage resources. By configuring utilization shape points and optional storage class weights, the scheduler can favor nodes with the best-fitting volume capacities across any topology domain.

KEP-2589.title: In-tree Storage Plugin to CSI Migration - Portworx
KEP-2589.summary: This KEP adds vendor‑specific feature gates to migrate the Portworx in‑tree storage plugin to the Portworx CSI driver. Enabling CSIMigrationPortworx (and related flags) redirects volume operations from the in‑tree driver to CSI, aligning with the broader CSI migration effort and simplifying storage provisioning for users of Portworx.

KEP-2923.title: In-tree Storage Plugin to CSI Migration - Ceph RBD
KEP-2923.summary: The KEP adds support for migrating the in‑tree Ceph RBD storage plugin to the external CSI driver. It introduces the CSIMigrationRbd and InTreePluginRbdUnregister feature gates, allowing RBD volume operations to be transparently redirected to the CSI driver when enabled alongside CSIMigration, simplifying operations for users and preparing the in‑tree plugin for eventual removal.

KEP-1488.title: In-tree Storage Plugin to CSI Migration - GCE PD
KEP-1488.summary: This KEP defines the migration of the in‑tree GCE Persistent Disk (gce‑pd) storage plugin to its CSI driver by introducing the CSIMigrationGCE feature gate (and optionally InTreePluginGCEUnregister). When enabled together with the generic CSIMigration gate, all GCE PD operations are transparently redirected to the CSI driver, simplifying the storage stack and preparing Kubernetes for GA of the CSI migration.

KEP-5538.title: CSI driver opt-in for service account tokens via secrets field
KEP-5538.summary: This KEP introduces an opt‑in mechanism for CSI drivers to receive service account tokens via the dedicated `secrets` field in `NodePublishVolumeRequest` instead of the less secure `volume_context`. A new boolean field `serviceAccountTokenInSecrets` is added to the `CSIDriver` spec, controlled by the `CSIServiceAccountTokenSecrets` feature gate, allowing drivers to improve token handling security while maintaining backward compatibility.

KEP-2317.title: Provide fsgroup of pod to CSI driver on mount
KEP-2317.summary: This KEP introduces a feature gate that enables kubelet to pass a pod's fsGroup to CSI drivers via a new CSI RPC field (volume_mount_group) on NodeStageVolume and NodePublishVolume calls. By delegating fsGroup handling to the driver, it eliminates the need for kubelet to recursively chown/chmod volumes, which is essential for drivers that cannot perform these operations, such as AzureFile.

KEP-351.title: Raw Block Volumes
KEP-351.summary: The KEP introduces support for raw block volumes in Kubernetes by extending the volume API to allow pods to consume unformatted block devices directly. This enables high‑performance, low‑latency storage use cases such as databases, providing a consistent security model and non‑privileged access to block storage.

KEP-989.title: Extend usage of Volume DataSource to allow PVCs for Cloning
KEP-989.summary: This KEP adds support for specifying an existing PersistentVolumeClaim as the DataSource of a new PVC, enabling direct volume cloning via CSI provisioners. It allows users to request a duplicate of a volume within the same namespace and storage class, simplifying workflows for testing, backup, and data templating.

KEP-1489.title: In-tree Storage Plugin to CSI Migration - Cinder
KEP-1489.summary: This KEP adds vendor‑specific support for migrating the in‑tree OpenStack Cinder storage plugin to its CSI driver. It introduces two feature gates, CSIMigrationOpenStack and InTreePluginOpenStackUnregister, which when enabled (along with CSIMigration) redirect all Cinder operations to the CSI driver, simplifying migration for users.

KEP-1855.title: Service Account Token for CSI Driver
KEP-1855.summary: This KEP introduces a mechanism for CSI drivers to obtain audience-bound service account tokens for the pods they serve, via kubelet, and optionally request a republish (remount) of the volume to refresh short-lived tokens. It addresses security and permission limitations of the existing approach where CSI drivers read token files directly, improving isolation and token lifecycle management.

KEP-4049.title: Storage Capacity Scoring of Nodes for Dynamic Provisioning
KEP-4049.summary: This KEP adds a storage capacity based scoring mechanism for nodes used by the scheduler's VolumeBinding plugin during dynamic provisioning. Administrators can configure the scheduler to prefer nodes with either the most or the least free allocatable storage, improving placement decisions for local storage and cost optimization.

KEP-2263.title: Volume scale testing
KEP-2263.summary: This KEP proposes a comprehensive testing plan to evaluate the scalability and performance of Kubernetes storage components, focusing on volume controllers, kubelet volume manager, and CSI sidecars. The tests aim to establish baseline performance limits (e.g., max volumes per pod, node, cluster) and define SLOs for pod startup latency with volumes, providing a framework vendors can use for their drivers.

KEP-2451.title: Service Account Token Volumes
KEP-2451.summary: This KEP introduces a ServiceAccountToken volume projection that allows pods to receive automatically rotated service account tokens via the TokenRequest API, eliminating the need for secret-based token distribution. It also defines file permission heuristics to improve security while maintaining compatibility.

KEP-3333.title: Retroactive default StorageClass assignment
KEP-3333.summary: This KEP introduces retroactive default StorageClass assignment, allowing the PV controller to automatically assign the current default StorageClass to existing unbound PersistentVolumeClaims that have no storageClassName set. This change reduces the ordering dependencies between PVC creation and default StorageClass availability, simplifying cluster administration and installation workflows.

KEP-2261.title: Move mount library to staging
KEP-2261.summary: This KEP proposes moving the mount library from k8s/utils/mount into a staging repository under k/k. The relocation enables shared use by in‑tree volume plugins and external CSI drivers, leverages existing Kubernetes e2e test infrastructure, and simplifies back‑porting fixes without pulling unrelated changes.

KEP-770.title: Skip attach for non-attachable CSI volumes
KEP-770.summary: This KEP introduces the ability for Kubernetes to skip the attach/detach flow for CSI drivers that do not support volume attachment. By detecting non‑attachable CSI plugins, the control plane avoids creating VolumeAttachment objects and the external‑attacher is not required, simplifying volume mounting for such drivers.

KEP-2268.title: non graceful shutdown
KEP-2268.summary: This KEP introduces a mechanism to handle non‑graceful node shutdowns by allowing operators to manually taint a node as out‑of‑service, causing the Pod GC controller to force‑delete pods on that node and the attach‑detach controller to immediately detach volumes. This enables stateful workloads to fail‑over to other nodes, improving availability when a node is powered off, has a hardware failure, or cannot be detected by the graceful shutdown process.

KEP-1490.title: In-tree Storage Plugin to CSI Migration - Azuredisk
KEP-1490.summary: This KEP enables migration of the in-tree Azure Disk volume plugin to its CSI driver by introducing the CSIMigrationAzureDisk feature gate (and optionally InTreePluginAzureDiskUnregister). When enabled together with the generic CSIMigration gate, all Azure Disk volume operations are transparently handled by the CSI driver, simplifying management and aligning with the CSI migration strategy.

KEP-1495.title: Volume Populators
KEP-1495.summary: This KEP introduces a new `DataSourceRef` field on PersistentVolumeClaims to replace the existing `DataSource` field, enabling arbitrary objects (including custom resources) to be used as volume data sources. It also adds a `VolumePopulator` CRD and a data-source-validator controller to register and validate these new data sources, allowing generic volume populators for use cases like VM images and backup/restore.

KEP-1885.title: In-tree Storage Plugin to CSI Migration - Azurefile
KEP-1885.summary: This KEP enables migration of the in‑tree Azure File volume plugin to its CSI driver by introducing the CSIMigrationAzureFile feature gate (and an auxiliary InTreePluginAzurefileUnregister gate). When enabled alongside CSIMigration, all Azure File volume operations are redirected to the CSI driver transparently, allowing gradual deprecation of the in‑tree plugin.

KEP-554.title: Volume Scheduling Limits
KEP-554.summary: This KEP introduces per‑node configurable attachable volume limits, moving volume limit tracking from global Node capacity to the CSINode object. It adds a unified predicate that handles both in‑tree and CSI volumes, allowing CSI drivers to share limits with their corresponding in‑tree plugins and making volume limits configurable per node type.

KEP-4958.title: CSI Sidecars All in one
KEP-4958.summary: This KEP proposes consolidating all CSI sidecar components (external-attacher, provisioner, resizer, etc.) into a single monorepo with unified entrypoints. The change aims to simplify release management, reduce maintenance overhead, and lower resource usage by sharing common code and informers across sidecars.

KEP-3476.title: Volume Group Snapshot
KEP-3476.summary: The KEP adds a new group snapshot API that lets users take a crash‑consistent snapshot of multiple PersistentVolumeClaims at once by selecting them with a label selector. It introduces VolumeGroupSnapshot, VolumeGroupSnapshotClass, and VolumeGroupSnapshotContent resources and integrates with CSI drivers that support group snapshot capabilities, simplifying consistent backup and restore of multi‑volume applications.

KEP-3756.title: Robust VolumeManager reconstruction after kubelet restart
KEP-3756.summary: This KEP introduces a robust reconstruction of the kubelet VolumeManager after a kubelet restart by rapidly rebuilding the ActualStateOfWorld from the host OS and then populating the DesiredStateOfWorld from the API server. The change improves volume cleanup, provides accurate mount information for downstream features like SELinux relabeling, and resolves known bugs where volumes were not properly unmounted after restarts.

KEP-625.title: In-tree Storage Plugin to CSI Migration
KEP-625.summary: This KEP defines the design and implementation of migrating in‑tree storage plugins to the Container Storage Interface (CSI) by introducing an opt‑in feature gate that redirects in‑tree plugin operations to corresponding CSI drivers. It enables a seamless transition to CSI while preserving existing API contracts and allowing upgrade/downgrade paths.

KEP-3294.title: Provision volumes from cross-namespace snapshots
KEP-3294.summary: This KEP adds the ability to provision PersistentVolumeClaims from VolumeSnapshots that reside in a different namespace. It extends the PVC API to reference a cross‑namespace snapshot and leverages the ReferenceGrant resource for permission control, enabling shared snapshot use cases such as testing and golden images.

KEP-695.title: Skip Volume Ownership Change
KEP-695.summary: Adds a new optional field pod.Spec.SecurityContext.FSGroupChangePolicy that lets users control how volume ownership and permission changes for an FSGroup are applied. It enables skipping the recursive chown/chmod on large volumes or applying it only when the root directory permissions differ, reducing pod startup time while maintaining security semantics.

KEP-3314.title: CSI Changed Block Tracking
KEP-3314.summary: This KEP adds a new optional CSI SnapshotMetadata gRPC service that allows CSI drivers to expose changed block tracking (CBT) information for volume snapshots. It introduces a custom resource to advertise the sidecar service, enabling backup applications to efficiently retrieve allocated and changed block metadata directly via gRPC without overloading the Kubernetes API server.

KEP-2485.title: ReadWriteOncePod PersistentVolume AccessMode
KEP-2485.summary: This KEP adds a new ReadWriteOncePod (RWOP) access mode for PersistentVolumes that restricts volume usage to a single pod on a single node, addressing scenarios where the existing ReadWriteOnce mode is too permissive. It also defines the required changes to the CSI specification, drivers, and sidecars to support the new mode while preserving compatibility with the current RWO mode.

KEP-1487.title: In-tree Storage Plugin to CSI Migration - AWS
KEP-1487.summary: This KEP introduces vendor‑specific feature gates to migrate the built‑in AWS EBS in‑tree volume plugin to its CSI driver. Enabling CSIMigrationAWS (along with the generic CSIMigration flag) redirects volume operations from the legacy plugin to the CSI driver transparently, improving maintainability and allowing deprecation of the in‑tree implementation.

KEP-1710.title: Skip SELinux relabeling of volumes
KEP-1710.summary: This KEP introduces a mechanism to avoid costly recursive SELinux relabeling of volumes by using the mount option `-o context=XYZ`. It adds feature gates and API fields to allow default mount‑with‑context for ReadWriteOncePod volumes and provides an opt‑out via a new SELinuxChangePolicy field for workloads that require recursive relabeling.

KEP-1979.title: Object Storage Support
KEP-1979.summary: The KEP introduces the Container Object Storage Interface (COSI), a standardized Kubernetes API for provisioning, accessing, and managing object storage buckets. It enables automated bucket lifecycle operations, credential generation, and bucket sharing across namespaces, bringing object storage to the same level of first‑class treatment as CSI volumes.

KEP-1900.title: CSI Snapshot Webhook
KEP-1900.summary: This KEP introduces stricter validation for VolumeSnapshot and VolumeSnapshotContent objects by updating their CRD schemas and deploying a validating admission webhook that enforces immutability and additional field constraints. The phased rollout ensures backward compatibility while preventing invalid snapshot objects from being created or updated, improving reliability of the CSI snapshot feature.

KEP-603.title: CSI Pod Info on Mount
KEP-603.summary: This KEP extends the kubelet to include pod metadata such as the pod name and namespace in the CSI NodePublishVolume call, allowing CSI drivers to receive per‑pod context during volume mounts. The capability enables drivers that need pod‑level information for access control, logging, or other custom behavior, improving integration between Kubernetes and storage providers.

KEP-5040.title: Remove gitRepo volumes driver.
KEP-5040.summary: This KEP proposes removing the in‑tree gitRepo volume driver by disabling it with a new feature gate (GitRepoVolumeDriver) while keeping the gitRepo volume type in the API. Pods with gitRepo volumes will still be admitted, but kubelet will reject them, addressing a security risk (CVE-2024-10220) and completing the deprecation of an unmaintained storage plugin.

KEP-565.title: CSI Raw Block Volumes
KEP-565.summary: This KEP adds support for raw block volumes to the CSI volume plugin in kubelet, enabling CSI drivers to create, stage, and publish block devices directly to pods. It introduces the CSIBlockVolume feature gate and modifies the CSI mounter to handle block devices without a filesystem, improving CSI integration for block storage use cases.

KEP-962.title: ExecutionHook
KEP-962.summary: The KEP introduces a new API (ExecutionHook) and associated controller to allow on‑demand execution of user‑specified commands inside pods/containers, enabling use cases such as application‑consistent volume snapshots, upgrades, debugging, and other lifecycle actions. A reusable HookAction resource stores the command definition, while ExecutionHook objects select target pods/containers and track execution status.

KEP-2264.title: Kubernetes CSI release and CI process
KEP-2264.summary: This KEP defines a standardized release and CI process for the Kubernetes CSI components maintained under the kubernetes-csi organization. It introduces automated Prow jobs for building, unit testing, and end‑to‑end testing of each component, along with a versioning and tagging strategy to produce reproducible container images, improving reliability and predictability for CSI driver deployments.

KEP-3141.title: Prevent unauthorised volume mode conversion
KEP-3141.summary: This KEP adds validation to prevent unauthorized conversion of volume mode when restoring a PersistentVolumeClaim from a VolumeSnapshot. It introduces a new immutable field `spec.sourceVolumeMode` in the VolumeSnapshotContent API and an annotation to allow trusted users to explicitly permit volume mode changes, leveraging RBAC to enforce the rule.

KEP-1682.title: Skip Volume Ownership Change
KEP-1682.summary: This KEP introduces a new field `CSIDriver.Spec.FSGroupPolicy` that allows CSI drivers to explicitly opt‑in to volume ownership and permission changes via fsGroup. By eliminating fragile heuristics, it prevents errors when drivers (e.g., NFS) do not support such operations, improving reliability of volume mounts.

KEP-596.title: Ephemeral Inline CSI Volumes
KEP-596.summary: This KEP adds support for defining CSI volumes directly inside a Pod spec as ephemeral inline volumes, allowing CSI drivers to create and mount short‑lived volumes without PersistentVolume and PersistentVolumeClaim objects. It introduces new API fields for inline CSI volume specifications and a driver capability flag, enabling drivers to handle mount/unmount lifecycle only.

KEP-1491.title: In-tree Storage Plugin to CSI Migration - vSphere
KEP-1491.summary: This KEP implements the migration of the in‑tree vSphere volume plugin to the vSphere CSI driver by introducing two feature gates, CSIMigrationvSphere and InTreePluginvSphereUnregister. When enabled alongside the core CSIMigration gate, all operations for kubernetes.io/vsphere-volume are transparently redirected to the CSI driver, simplifying upgrades and preparing the in‑tree plugin for eventual removal.

KEP-1412.title: Immutable Secrets and ConfigMaps
KEP-1412.summary: This KEP adds an `immutable` boolean field to Secret and ConfigMap resources, allowing users to mark their contents as read‑only for the object's lifetime. When set, the API server rejects any data changes and kubelet stops watching these objects, reducing watch traffic and protecting against accidental updates that could cause application outages.

KEP-1698.title: generic ephemeral inline volumes
KEP-1698.summary: This KEP introduces a generic mechanism for specifying inline, ephemeral volumes directly in a pod spec by embedding a PersistentVolumeClaimTemplate. The controller automatically creates and deletes a PVC for each pod, allowing any storage driver that supports dynamic provisioning to be used without driver modifications, and supporting standard volume operations such as snapshotting and resizing.

KEP-4876.title: Mutable CSINode Allocatable Property
KEP-4876.summary: This KEP makes the CSINode.Spec.Drivers[*].Allocatable.Count field mutable and adds a mechanism for CSI drivers to dynamically update the allocatable count on nodes. By introducing a per‑driver update interval and reactive updates on capacity‑related failures, it ensures the scheduler has an accurate view of attachment capacity, improving reliability of stateful pod scheduling.

KEP-1472.title: Storage Capacity Constraints for Pod Scheduling
KEP-1472.summary: This KEP introduces a new built‑in API object, CSIStorageCapacity, and a CSIDriver spec field to expose the remaining storage capacity of CSI drivers per topology segment. The scheduler consumes this information to avoid placing pods on nodes where volume creation would fail due to insufficient storage, improving pod scheduling reliability for both local and network‑attached storage.

KEP-3751.title: Kubernetes VolumeAttributesClass and ModifyVolume
KEP-3751.summary: This KEP introduces a new VolumeAttributesClass API resource and modifies the PersistentVolume and PersistentVolumeClaim APIs to allow dynamic specification and modification of volume performance attributes (e.g., IOPS, throughput). It adds a ControllerModifyVolume CSI RPC and related status fields so that volume attributes can be changed on‑line without recreating volumes, with quota enforcement and admission control.

KEP-1733.title: Release Notes Improvements
KEP-1733.summary: This KEP proposes a new, streamlined release notes process for Kubernetes, including consolidation of tooling, removal of legacy scripts, and the creation of a dedicated website to present release notes in a searchable, filterable format. It also adds automation to generate JSON release notes, publish them to a Google Cloud bucket, and classify changes with additional labels, improving efficiency for the release team and the end‑user experience.

KEP-1731.title: Publishing Kubernetes packages on community infrastructure
KEP-1731.summary: This KEP proposes using the Open Build Service (OBS) to automatically build, sign, and publish Kubernetes deb and rpm packages on community‑owned infrastructure, removing the reliance on Google‑owned resources and manual steps. By integrating package generation into the release pipeline, it enables stable, dev, and nightly channels to be published automatically for each release, improving speed, transparency, and community ownership.

KEP-559.title: Volume Subpath Env Expansion
KEP-559.summary: This KEP introduces a new API field `subPathExpr` allowing volume mount subpaths to be specified using environment variable expansion (e.g., $(POD_NAME)). It enables unique per‑pod log directories without complex initContainer workarounds, improving usability and security of volume subpaths.

KEP-5008.title: Move Headlamp to the SIG UI
KEP-5008.summary: This KEP proposes moving the Headlamp project under the SIG UI umbrella in the kubernetes-sigs organization, making it an official Kubernetes UI component. By doing so it aims to improve the out‑of‑the‑box UI experience, provide an extensible platform for vendors and CNCF projects, and strengthen community integration.

KEP-3031.title: Signing release artifacts
KEP-3031.summary: This KEP defines a standard process and tooling for signing all Kubernetes release artifacts using sigstore's cosign. By providing cryptographic signatures for binaries, container images, documentation, SBOMs, and other consumable artifacts, it enables users to verify integrity and authenticity, strengthening the software supply chain security for Kubernetes releases.

KEP-2818.title: Reducing Build Maintenance in CIP
KEP-2818.summary: Deprecate Bazel in the k8s-container-image-promoter (CIP) and replace it with native Go tooling and Docker commands. This reduces build maintenance, removes Bazel dependencies, and preserves deterministic image digests for e2e tests by using static tarball archives.

KEP-1729.title: Rebase Kubernetes Main Master and Node Images to Distroless/static
KEP-1729.summary: This KEP proposes rebasing the core Kubernetes master and node container images to use gcr.io/distroless/static as the base, making the images thinner, more secure, and reducing vulnerability churn. It establishes policies, testing, and documentation to ensure compatibility and a smooth transition, targeting the v1.15 release.

KEP-3000.title: Artifact Distribution Policy
KEP-3000.summary: The KEP defines a policy and procedure for promoting and mirroring Kubernetes container images across multiple registries and cloud providers, enabling a redirecting OCI proxy (registry.k8s.io) that routes traffic to the nearest mirror (e.g., AWS S3). This reduces egress costs and ensures global accessibility of images, especially for users behind restrictive firewalls.

KEP-3027.title: SLSA Compliance in the Kubernetes Release Process
KEP-3027.summary: This KEP proposes to harden the Kubernetes release process by adopting the SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts) framework, aiming for Level 3 (and eventually Level 4) compliance. By doing so, it will provide downstream consumers with strong guarantees of artifact integrity, provenance, and traceability, enhancing overall supply‑chain security.

KEP-1498.title: Kubernetes Yearly Support Period
KEP-1498.summary: This KEP proposes extending Kubernetes' patch‑fix support window from the current nine months to a twelve‑month support period plus a two‑month grace period (total 14 months). The change aligns support cycles with typical annual business planning cycles and updates related version‑skew, deprecation, and dependency support policies.

KEP-1734.title: Image Promoter
KEP-1734.summary: The Image Promoter KEP defines a GitOps‑style workflow for securely publishing container images to the official Kubernetes GCR. It introduces a staging registry for testing and scanning images, and a promotion process via pull‑request review that automatically copies approved images to the production registry, optionally signing them.

KEP-2853.title: Changing kubernetes/kubernetes default branch name to main
KEP-2853.summary: This KEP proposes renaming the default branch of the primary Kubernetes repository (kubernetes/kubernetes) from "master" to "main" to adopt more inclusive terminology. The change includes a coordinated plan for communication, migration, and updating CI jobs to minimize impact on downstream consumers.

KEP-3720.title: Freezing `k8s.gcr.io` image registry
KEP-3720.summary: The KEP proposes to freeze the legacy k8s.gcr.io image registry by stopping all new image pushes after the v1.27 release, directing all future images exclusively to the community‑run registry.k8s.io. This reduces infrastructure costs and encourages users to migrate to the newer, faster, and cheaper registry.

KEP-1732.title: Kubernetes Community Artifact Serving
KEP-1732.summary: The KEP proposes a standardized process and infrastructure for serving official Kubernetes artifacts (container images and binaries) via a global HTTP redirector (artifacts.k8s.io) that routes requests to geo‑located mirrors. This ensures consistent, fast, and cost‑efficient access for the community while allowing authorized contributors to promote and manage artifacts through a staged staging‑to‑production workflow.

KEP-3744.title: Stay on supported go versions
KEP-3744.summary: This KEP defines a process for Kubernetes release branches to adopt newer minor versions of the Go compiler while preserving compatibility and stability of patch releases. By tracking prerequisite changes, backporting them, and updating branches after thorough testing, Kubernetes can stay on supported Go versions and benefit from security fixes without introducing regressions.

KEP-2572.title: Defining the Kubernetes Release Cadence
KEP-2572.summary: This KEP formalizes a change to the Kubernetes release cadence, reducing the number of minor releases per year from four to three and establishing a 15‑week release cycle. It defines a lightweight policy for creating release schedules, improving predictability, reducing risk, and giving contributors and users more time to plan and adapt.

KEP-3178.title: Cleaning up IPTables Chain Ownership
KEP-3178.summary: This KEP proposes cleaning up IPTables chain ownership by removing unnecessary IPTables chain creation from kubelet and shifting responsibility to kube-proxy. It introduces a new hint chain for iptables mode detection and eliminates duplicate or unused chains such as KUBE-MARK-MASQ, KUBE-MARK-DROP, and related rules, improving security and reducing external component reliance on Kubernetes internal IPTables chains.

KEP-2829.title: Migrate Gateway API to k8s.io Group
KEP-2829.summary: This KEP tracks the migration of the Gateway API from the experimental x-k8s.io API group to the official k8s.io group as part of the v1alpha2 release. The move subjects the API, still represented as CRDs, to the standard Kubernetes API review process, improving quality, stability, and community governance.

KEP-2079.title: Network Policy to support Port Ranges
KEP-2079.summary: This KEP introduces an optional `endPort` field to NetworkPolicyPort, allowing users to specify a range of ports instead of enumerating each port individually. The change simplifies creation of NetworkPolicies for port ranges, enhancing usability and aligning with common use cases such as NodePort ranges and passive FTP server requirements.

KEP-2593.title: Enhanced NodeIPAM to support Discontiguous Cluster CIDR
KEP-2593.summary: This KEP introduces a new built-in API resource, ClusterCIDR, and a MultiCIDRRangeAllocator controller to enable discontiguous and sized pod CIDR allocation per node. It allows dynamic addition of CIDR blocks, node‑specific CIDR selection, and flexible per‑node pod IP capacity without requiring control‑plane restarts.

KEP-2449.title: Move ExternalDNS out of Kubernetes incubator
KEP-2449.summary: This KEP proposes moving the ExternalDNS project out of the Kubernetes incubator into the main Kubernetes organization or the kubernetes-sigs repository under sig-network sponsorship. The move ensures continued community support, neutral governance, and access to Kubernetes infrastructure for CI/CD and releases.

KEP-1435.title: Different protocols in the same service definition with type=loadbalancer
KEP-1435.summary: This KEP proposes to relax Service validation to allow LoadBalancer Services to define multiple ports with different L4 protocols (e.g., TCP and UDP) in a single Service. Enabling this feature allows users to expose applications like DNS or SIP on the same IP address using mixed protocols, while providing a feature gate for cloud providers that may not support it.

KEP-4444.title: Traffic Distribution for Services
KEP-4444.summary: This KEP adds a new field, spec.trafficDistribution, to the Service API to let users express routing preferences such as PreferClose, superseding the deprecated topology-mode annotation and topologyKeys. Implementations like kube-proxy can use this hint to prioritize same‑zone endpoints, giving users more control while remaining extensible for future heuristics.

KEP-3705.title: Cloud Dual-Stack --node-ip Handling
KEP-3705.summary: This KEP adds support for specifying dual‑stack IP addresses via the kubelet --node-ip flag in clusters that use external cloud providers. It introduces handling of comma‑separated IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, propagates them through the existing provided-node-ip annotation, and implements the behavior behind the CloudDualStackNodeIPs feature gate.

KEP-580.title: Pod Ready++
KEP-580.summary: This KEP introduces a new extensibility point for pod readiness called ReadinessGates, allowing external signals to be injected via custom pod conditions that influence the pod's Ready status. By adding the spec.readinessGates field, workloads can make deployment and traffic routing decisions based on richer readiness information, improving reliability during rolling updates and other transitions.

KEP-3458.title: Remove transient node predicates from KCCM's service controller
KEP-3458.summary: This KEP introduces the StableLoadBalancerNodeSet feature gate to stop the cloud controller manager's service controller from adding or removing nodes from load balancer node sets when nodes experience transient readiness changes or receive the ToBeDeletedByClusterAutoscaler taint. By avoiding these syncs, connection draining is preserved, cloud provider API calls are reduced, and large clusters experience fewer rate‑limiting issues.

KEP-2681.title: Field status.hostIPs added for Pod
KEP-2681.summary: This KEP introduces a new status field, `status.hostIPs`, to the Pod API that records all IP addresses (IPv4 and IPv6) assigned to the node hosting the pod. The change enables applications to retrieve multiple host IPs via the Downward API, facilitating smoother dual‑stack migrations and improved visibility of node networking information.

KEP-3070.title: Reserve Service IP Range For Dynamic and Static IP Allocation
KEP-3070.summary: This KEP introduces a configurable sub‑range within the Service ClusterIP CIDR to separate static and dynamic IP allocations. By reserving a lower band of IPs for static assignments and preferring the upper band for dynamic allocations, it reduces the risk of IP conflicts for services that require well‑known static IPs.

KEP-3668.title: Reserve Nodeport Ranges For Dynamic And Static Port Allocation
KEP-3668.summary: This KEP introduces a reservation sub‑range within the Service NodePort range, separating ports used for static assignments from those allocated dynamically. By allocating static ports from a lower band and dynamic ports from an upper band, it reduces the risk of port conflicts without changing the existing allocation mechanism.

KEP-1672.title: Tracking Terminating Endpoints in EndpointSlice
KEP-1672.summary: This KEP adds new fields to the EndpointSlice API to expose the terminating state of endpoints. By introducing `terminating` and `serving` conditions, consumers such as kube-proxy can differentiate between ready, serving, and terminating endpoints without watching pods directly, enabling more efficient and graceful termination handling.

KEP-3866.title: Add an nftables-based kube-proxy backend
KEP-3866.summary: This KEP proposes adding an official nftables-based backend for kube-proxy, replacing the legacy iptables and ipvs modes with a more performant and future‑proof implementation. It aims to address iptables' performance and deprecation issues while providing a cleaner code base and potential for becoming the default Linux proxy mode.

KEP-2438.title: Dual Stack API Server
KEP-2438.summary: This KEP enables the kube-apiserver to listen on and advertise both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in dual‑stack clusters. It adds command‑line support for dual‑stack bind and advertise addresses, updates the kubernetes Service and EndpointSlice handling to be dual‑stack aware, and enhances InClusterConfig to prefer reachable dual‑stack IPs.

KEP-563.title: Kubernetes Dual-stack Support
KEP-563.summary: This KEP adds IPv4/IPv6 dual‑stack support to Kubernetes clusters, enabling pods and services to have both an IPv4 and an IPv6 address and allowing native IPv4‑to‑IPv4 and IPv6‑to‑IPv6 communication throughout the cluster. It updates the API, CRI, kube‑proxy, kubeadm and related components to be aware of multiple IPs per pod, node, and service, providing full dual‑stack functionality while preserving compatibility with IPv4‑only and IPv6‑only clusters.

KEP-4427.title: Relaxed DNS search string validation
KEP-4427.summary: This KEP introduces a RelaxedDNSSearchValidation feature gate that relaxes the validation of DNS search strings in pod dnsConfig.searches, allowing underscores and a single dot as valid entries. It enables legacy workloads and use cases that require such search strings while maintaining safety through a ratcheting validation approach and optional enablement.

KEP-2943.title: Network Policy status subresource
KEP-2943.summary: This KEP introduces a status subresource for NetworkPolicy objects, allowing network policy providers to report parsing and implementation feedback via conditions. Adding this field gives users visibility into why a policy may not be effective, improving debugging and operational clarity.

KEP-1864.title: Optionally Disable Node Ports for Service Type=LoadBalancer
KEP-1864.summary: This KEP adds an optional boolean field `spec.allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts` to Service objects, allowing users to opt out of automatic node‑port allocation for Services of type LoadBalancer. It enables clusters that use load‑balancer implementations that do not require node ports to conserve node‑port resources and avoid unnecessary exposure.

KEP-752.title: EndpointSlice API
KEP-752.summary: The EndpointSlice KEP introduces a new Discovery API resource called EndpointSlice to replace the monolithic Core/V1 Endpoints API. By partitioning service endpoints into smaller slices, it eliminates the scalability and performance bottlenecks of large endpoint sets and enables future extensions such as multiple IPs per pod and richer endpoint state.

KEP-2447.title: Make kube-proxy service abstraction optional
KEP-2447.summary: This KEP introduces an optional mechanism to disable kube-proxy's service abstraction for Services that are handled exclusively by a service mesh. By adding the label `service.kubernetes.io/service-proxy-name` to a Service (and its Endpoints), kube-proxy will ignore those objects, reducing CPU and iptables/ipvs processing load in large clusters.

KEP-4004.title: Deprecate status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion field
KEP-4004.summary: This KEP proposes to deprecate the status.nodeInfo.kubeProxyVersion field on the v1.Node object because it is inaccurate and not set by kube-proxy. A feature gate (DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion) is introduced to stop kubelet from populating the field, allowing a gradual migration for components that may rely on it.

KEP-2450.title: Remove knowledge of pod cluster CIDR from iptables rules
KEP-2450.summary: This KEP proposes removing the dependency on the pod cluster CIDR in kube-proxy's iptables and ipvs rules, replacing it with node‑local traffic identification methods (node CIDR, interface prefixes, or physdev). The change decouples pod IP allocation strategies from service routing, allowing more flexible IP management such as disjoint or expanding CIDR ranges.

KEP-2448.title: Remove kube-proxy's automatic clean up logic
KEP-2448.summary: This KEP removes kube-proxy's implicit clean‑up of proxy rules, requiring the explicit `--cleanup` flag for any rule removal. By eliminating automatic clean‑up on start‑up, it avoids bugs caused by overlapping iptables and IPVS rules and makes kube-proxy behavior more predictable and safer.

KEP-4762.title: Allows setting arbitrary FQDN as the pod's hostname
KEP-4762.summary: This KEP introduces a new podSpec field `hostnameOverride` that allows users to set an arbitrary Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) as a pod's hostname. When the feature gate `HostnameOverride` is enabled, the kubelet will respect this field, write the FQDN to /etc/hosts, and ignore the existing hostname, subdomain, and setHostnameAsFQDN fields.

KEP-1669.title: Proxy Terminating Endpoints
KEP-1669.summary: This KEP enhances kube-proxy to route traffic to terminating pods that are still Ready when they are the only available endpoints for a Service, reducing traffic loss during rolling updates. It leverages the Terminating and Serving conditions added to EndpointSlice (KEP-1672) and adds feature-gated behavior to improve reliability for Services with externalTrafficPolicy or internalTrafficPolicy settings.

KEP-2595.title: Expanded DNS Configuration
KEP-2595.summary: This KEP introduces the ExpandedDNSConfig feature gate to allow Kubernetes to accept larger DNS configurations, increasing the maximum number of DNS search paths to 32 and the total character length to 2048. It updates validation in kube-apiserver and kubelet so pods and pod templates can use expanded DNS search lists, aligning Kubernetes with modern resolver capabilities.

KEP-5495.title: Deprecate ipvs mode in kube-proxy
KEP-5495.summary: This KEP proposes deprecating the ipvs mode of kube-proxy, adding a deprecation warning and updating documentation to encourage migration to the nftables backend. It matters because the SIG network lacks maintainers for ipvs, and nftables provides comparable performance with better maintainability.

KEP-758.title: Graduate Ingress to GA
KEP-758.summary: This KEP graduates the Ingress API to General Availability by moving it from the deprecated extensions/v1beta1 group to networking/v1beta1, cleaning up the API, and adding GA‑ready features. It introduces explicit path type handling, hostname wildcard support, formal IngressClass fields, and alternative backend types, providing a stable, well‑specified Ingress experience for users and operators.

KEP-566.title: Switch CoreDNS to the default DNS
KEP-566.summary: This KEP proposes making CoreDNS the default DNS service in Kubernetes, replacing kube-dns across all installation tools such as kube-up, kops, minikube, and continuing its default status in kubeadm. By standardizing on CoreDNS, clusters gain a more modern, extensible DNS implementation that is already GA and maintained as part of the Kubernetes ecosystem.

KEP-784.title: Kube Proxy component configuration updates and graduation
KEP-784.summary: This KEP proposes restructuring and graduating kube-proxy's component configuration from a flat v1alpha1 schema to a well‑structured, platform‑aware v1alpha2 (and eventually v1beta1). The changes introduce separate platform sections, add new fields, adjust defaults, and drop obsolete options, making the configuration easier to understand, maintain, and extend across Linux, Windows, and multiple proxy backends.

KEP-1024.title: NodeLocal DNS Cache
KEP-1024.summary: The NodeLocal DNS Cache KEP proposes running a DNS caching agent as a DaemonSet on every node, allowing pods to resolve DNS queries via a local cache instead of the kube-dns Service IP. This reduces latency, avoids iptables DNAT and conntrack overhead, and provides per‑node DNS metrics.

KEP-1453.title: Graduate Ingress API to GA
KEP-1453.summary: This KEP migrates the Ingress resource from the deprecated extensions/v1beta1 API group to the stable networking/v1beta1 group and graduates the API to GA. It introduces API refinements such as a dedicated pathType field, defaultBackend renaming, hostname wildcard support, an explicit IngressClass field, and support for non-Service backend types.

KEP-536.title: Topology-aware service routing
KEP-536.summary: This KEP adds a topologyKeys field to the Service API, enabling users to specify preferred topological domains (e.g., node, zone, region) for routing service traffic. It also introduces a PodLocator resource to efficiently map pods to topology labels for scalable implementation of topology‑aware routing in kube‑proxy and DNS components.

KEP-3726.title: standard-application-protocols
KEP-3726.summary: This KEP proposes to standardize the values used in the Service and Endpoint `appProtocol` field by defining a set of Kubernetes‑prefixed protocol names (e.g., kubernetes.io/h2c, kubernetes.io/ws, kubernetes.io/wss). The aim is to improve interoperability between implementations by providing a clear, shared naming scheme for common non‑IANA application protocols.

KEP-1507.title: Adding AppProtocol to Services and Endpoints
KEP-1507.summary: This KEP introduces an optional AppProtocol field for ServicePort and EndpointPort objects, allowing users to specify the application protocol for each port directly in Service and Endpoints resources. The change standardizes protocol specification, replaces ad‑hoc annotations, and aligns Service/Endpoints with the existing EndpointSlice AppProtocol support.

KEP-3685.title: Move EndpointSlice Reconciler into Staging
KEP-3685.summary: This KEP moves the in-tree EndpointSlice reconciler and its dependencies into the staging repository, making the reconciling logic available as a reusable library for out-of-tree EndpointSlice controllers. By exposing a stable API, it simplifies custom controller development and aids migration from Endpoints to EndpointSlices.

KEP-1880.title: Multiple Service CIDRs
KEP-1880.summary: This KEP introduces a new allocation model that adds ServiceCIDR and IPAddress API objects, enabling clusters to dynamically expand the pool of Service IP addresses by creating additional CIDR ranges. It improves scalability, supports IPv6 best‑practice /64 prefixes, and remains backwards compatible with existing Service semantics.

KEP-980.title: Finalizer Protection for Service LoadBalancers
KEP-980.summary: This KEP adds a finalizer to Service objects of type LoadBalancer to ensure they are not fully deleted until the associated cloud load balancer resources are cleaned up. The mechanism protects against orphaned load balancers and supports safe upgrade/downgrade paths.

KEP-3015.title: PreferSameZone and PreferSameNode Traffic Distribution
KEP-3015.summary: This KEP deprecates the ambiguous `PreferClose` traffic distribution mode, renames it to `PreferSameZone`, and introduces a new `PreferSameNode` mode that routes service traffic to endpoints on the same node when possible. To support the new mode, a `forNodes` field is added to `discoveryv1.EndpointHints`, allowing EndpointSlices to convey node‑specific hints to service proxies. These changes make traffic distribution semantics clearer and enable more locality‑aware routing for services.

KEP-427.title: Graduate CoreDNS to GA
KEP-427.summary: This KEP proposes graduating CoreDNS, the flexible and extensible DNS server used for cluster service discovery, from Beta to GA in Kubernetes. The graduation includes making CoreDNS the default DNS implementation, providing upgrade paths in kubeadm, and ensuring compatibility and performance parity with kube-dns.

KEP-1138.title: Graduate IPv6 to beta
KEP-1138.summary: This KEP graduates IPv6 support from Alpha to Beta, making IPv6‑only Kubernetes clusters stable and production‑ready. It adds CI e2e testing on kind and at least one cloud provider, ensuring feature parity with IPv4 and full documentation.

KEP-3836.title: Kube-proxy improved ingress connectivity reliability
KEP-3836.summary: This KEP enhances kube-proxy health handling to improve ingress connectivity reliability. It makes kube-proxy fail its /healthz endpoint when a node is being terminated (via the ToBeDeletedByClusterAutoscaler taint) so load balancers can drain connections, adds a new /livez endpoint that reflects only proxy health, and provides guidance documentation for cloud providers. The changes aim to ensure graceful connection draining for eTP:Cluster services and give operators observable metrics.

KEP-2200.title: Block ExternalIPs via Admission Control
KEP-2200.summary: This KEP adds a built-in admission controller, DenyServiceExternalIPs, that rejects creation or update of Service objects that add new entries to spec.externalIPs, mitigating the CVE-2020-8554 MITM vulnerability. It allows existing externalIPs to remain but prevents unprivileged users from introducing insecure external IPs, and is opt‑in via the apiserver admission‑plugins flag.

KEP-2365.title: IngressClass Namespaced Params
KEP-2365.summary: This KEP adds Scope and Namespace fields to the IngressClass ParametersRef, enabling IngressClass objects to reference namespace‑scoped parameter resources in addition to cluster‑scoped ones. The change is guarded by the IngressClassNamespacedParams feature gate and introduces a new IngressClassParametersReference type.

KEP-265.title: IPVS Load Balancing Mode in Kubernetes
KEP-265.summary: This KEP introduces an IPVS‑based mode for kube‑proxy, allowing services to be load‑balanced using the IP Virtual Server kernel module instead of iptables. By leveraging IPVS’s efficient data structures and load‑balancing algorithms, the proposal aims to improve the scalability and performance of Kubernetes service routing.

KEP-614.title: SCTP support
KEP-614.summary: This KEP adds native SCTP protocol support to Kubernetes Service, NetworkPolicy, and Pod ContainerPort definitions, extending the corev1.Protocol enumeration with a new SCTP value. It enables telecommunication workloads to use SCTP for service discovery, load balancing, and network policy enforcement, while also addressing compatibility with userspace SCTP stacks.

KEP-2091.title: Add support for AdminNetworkPolicy resources
KEP-2091.summary: This KEP introduces two new cluster‑scoped resources, AdminNetworkPolicy and BaselineAdminNetworkPolicy, enabling administrators to express explicit allow, deny, and pass actions for intra‑cluster traffic. The APIs add priority ordering, rule naming, and the ability to enforce immutable guardrails that cannot be overridden by namespace‑scoped NetworkPolicies.

KEP-1611.title: Rearchitecting NetworkPolicy tests with a DSL for better upstream test coverage
KEP-1611.summary: This KEP proposes rearchitecting the Kubernetes NetworkPolicy test suite by introducing a domain‑specific language (DSL) and a reachability matrix to define pod connectivity scenarios. The goal is to improve test readability, performance, coverage, and scalability, enabling faster and more comprehensive CI verification of NetworkPolicy behavior across CNIs.

KEP-3453.title: Minimize iptables-restore input size
KEP-3453.summary: This KEP introduces an optimization to kube-proxy's iptables mode by minimizing the size of the input to iptables-restore. It tracks changes to Service and EndpointSlice objects and only regenerates the iptables chains that actually changed, reducing CPU usage and latency in large clusters while preserving correctness.

KEP-4974.title: Deprecate v1.Endpoints and Associated Controllers
KEP-4974.summary: This KEP formally deprecates the v1.Endpoints API and its associated controllers, encouraging users to transition to EndpointSlice. It adds deprecation warnings, metrics, documentation updates, and test suite changes to support disabling the Endpoints controller in clusters.

KEP-2086.title: Service Internal Traffic Policy
KEP-2086.summary: This KEP adds a new field `spec.internalTrafficPolicy` to Service resources, enabling node‑local or topology‑aware routing of internal cluster traffic. With the ServiceInternalTrafficPolicy feature gate, users can choose between the default "Cluster" behavior (traffic to any endpoint) and "Local" behavior (traffic only to endpoints on the same node), improving use‑cases such as per‑node logging or metrics agents.

KEP-504.title: Configurable Pod DNS
KEP-504.summary: This KEP introduces a new PodSpec field `dnsConfig` that allows users to overlay custom DNS settings on top of the existing `dnsPolicy`. It enables adding or overriding nameservers, search paths, and resolver options, and adds a `Custom` dnsPolicy for fully custom resolv.conf configurations, reducing unnecessary DNS query amplification and giving finer control over pod DNS behavior.

KEP-1860.title: Make Kubernetes aware of the load balancer behaviour
KEP-1860.summary: This KEP introduces a new optional field `ipMode` in the Service status loadBalancer ingress to allow cloud providers to control whether kube-proxy binds the LoadBalancer IP directly on nodes. By toggling between `VIP` (default) and `Proxy`, it enables or disables the shortcut that bypasses the external load balancer, improving compatibility with cloud provider LB behaviors and features.

KEP-2433.title: Topology Aware Hints
KEP-2433.summary: This KEP introduces a new `hints` field in the EndpointSlice API to enable topology‑aware routing by allowing EndpointSlice producers to indicate the preferred zones for consuming each endpoint. When the TopologyAwareHints feature gate is enabled, kube‑proxy can use these hints to keep traffic within the same zone, reducing cross‑zone latency and cost.

KEP-5311.title: Relaxed validation for Services names
KEP-5311.summary: This KEP proposes to relax Service name validation by switching from DNS1035Label to DNSLabel, allowing Service names to start with digits and align with validation used for other resources. The change is gated behind the RelaxedServiceNameValidation feature gate and includes updates to Ingress validation to remain compatible.

KEP-4858.title: IP/CIDR Validation Improvements
KEP-4858.summary: This KEP introduces stricter validation for all IP and CIDR typed fields in core Kubernetes APIs, rejecting ambiguous or unsafe representations such as leading zeros, IPv4‑mapped IPv6 addresses, non‑canonical forms, and CIDR strings with host bits set. The changes improve security and consistency, initially gated behind the StrictIPCIDRValidation feature gate and later graduated through warning, ratcheting, and full enforcement phases.

KEP-2021.title: HPA supports scaling to/from zero pods for object/external metrics
KEP-2021.summary: This KEP extends the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) to support scaling workloads from zero to many replicas and back to zero when using object or external metrics. It introduces a new ScaledToZero condition in the HPA status, allowing automated scaling to zero for cost‑efficient workloads such as GPU‑intensive or idle queue consumers.
affectedFields: status.conditions[].status (new condition ScaledToZero can be True/False)

KEP-5325.title: Improve pod selection accuracy across workload types
KEP-5325.summary: This KEP introduces a new optional field, SelectionStrategy, to the HorizontalPodAutoscaler spec, allowing users to control how pods are selected for metrics collection—either by label selector (default) or by owner reference. This improves scaling accuracy by ensuring only pods owned by the target workload are considered, preventing unrelated pods from influencing HPA decisions.

KEP-4951.title: Configurable tolerance for HPA
KEP-4951.summary: This KEP adds a configurable tolerance field to the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) API, allowing users to set per‑HPA scaling tolerance values that override the cluster‑wide --horizontal-pod-autoscaler-tolerance flag. By specifying tolerance in the HPAScalingRules of an HPA, operators can fine‑tune how sensitive scaling decisions are to metric fluctuations, reducing unnecessary scaling actions and improving responsiveness for individual workloads.

KEP-117.title: Enhance HPA Metrics Specificity
KEP-117.summary: This KEP extends the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) by adding label selector support to the Object and Pods metric source types and introducing a targetAverageValue field, aligning them with the External metric source. These changes make metric selection more granular and flexible, improving autoscaling based on custom metrics without requiring external pipeline modifications.

KEP-2702.title: Graduate HPA v2beta2 API to GA
KEP-2702.summary: This KEP proposes graduating the autoscaling/v2beta2 Horizontal Pod Autoscaler API to General Availability (GA). The graduation includes promoting the API to stable, adding required end‑to‑end tests, and renaming several fields for clarity, while deprecating the older v2beta1 version.

KEP-5030.title: Integrate CSI Volume attach limits with cluster autoscaler
KEP-5030.summary: This KEP updates the Cluster Autoscaler to consider CSI volume attach limits when scaling nodes, ensuring the correct number of nodes are provisioned. It also enhances the built‑in scheduler’s NodeVolumeLimits plugin to avoid placing pods on nodes that lack the required CSI driver, closing a gap that could lead to scheduling failures.

KEP-2225.title: Contributor Site
KEP-2225.summary: The KEP proposes creating a dedicated, static contributor site (hosted at kubernetes.dev) to centralize and publish documentation aimed at Kubernetes contributors. By consolidating markdown files from various repos and providing easy navigation and discoverability, it helps scale the contributor community and reduces fragmentation and outdated information.

KEP-853.title: Configurable scale up/down velocity for HPA
KEP-853.summary: This KEP introduces a configurable `behavior` field for the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) that allows users to control scaling velocity in both directions via stabilization windows, select policies, and scaling policies. By exposing these settings per‑HPA, users can fine‑tune how quickly pods are added or removed to match application requirements and reduce unwanted scaling jitter.

KEP-1553.title: Issue Triage Workflow and Automation
KEP-1553.summary: The KEP introduces a standardized issue triage workflow for the kubernetes/kubernetes repository by automatically applying a `needs-triage` label to new issues and PRs and allowing triage decisions via `triage/accepted` and other triage labels. It also renames the `triage/support` label to `kind/support` to better reflect its purpose, reducing triage overhead for SIG/area reviewers and improving routing of community contributions.

KEP-1610.title: Container Resource based Autoscaling
KEP-1610.summary: This KEP introduces a new ContainerResource metric source for the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, allowing scaling decisions to be based on individual container resource usage rather than summed pod usage. It adds a container field to specify which container's metrics to consider, enabling finer‑grained autoscaling for multi‑container pods.

KEP-4706.title: Deprecate and remove kustomize from kubectl
KEP-4706.summary: This KEP proposes deprecating and ultimately removing the built‑in kustomize functionality from kubectl, allowing kustomize to be maintained and released independently. The change introduces deprecation warnings, an environment variable to toggle legacy behavior, and migration guidance toward using a standalone kustomize binary or a kubectl plugin.

KEP-3104.title: Introduce kuberc
KEP-3104.summary: This KEP introduces an optional `kuberc` file that separates user preferences, default options, and command aliases from cluster credentials stored in kubeconfig. By versioning and managing this file via a new `kubectl kuberc` command, users can opt‑in to new client behaviors without breaking existing CI pipelines or scripts.

KEP-491.title: kubectl-diff
KEP-491.summary: kubectl diff provides a simple user experience to preview how configuration changes will affect the cluster by comparing the live state to the hypothetical state after applying changes. It leverages server-side dry-run to safely generate a merged object without persisting changes, enabling both manual and automated validation of configuration updates.

KEP-993.title: Kustomize Generators and Transformers
KEP-993.summary: This KEP introduces exec‑based plugins for Kustomize that allow users to add custom Generators and Transformers via two new fields (`generators` and `transformers`) in kustomization.yaml. Plugins receive configuration through STDIN and emit resources through STDOUT, enabling ecosystem tools and organization‑specific solutions to be declaratively integrated with kubectl and Kustomize.

KEP-2953.title: Kustomize Plugin Graduation
KEP-2953.summary: This KEP proposes graduating Kustomize's alpha plugin mechanisms into a unified, KRM-driven extension model with a robust distribution, discovery, and trust framework. It aims to make Kustomize plugins first‑class, supported in kubectl, by converging legacy exec/Go plugins and KRM function plugins under a single, secure runtime model.

KEP-2386.title: Kustomize Subcommand Integration
KEP-2386.summary: This KEP proposes adding a new kubectl subcommand, `kubectl kustomize`, which exposes the existing Kustomize `build` functionality through the kubectl CLI. By doing so, users can generate and transform declarative resource configurations directly with kubectl, improving the workflow for applying, diffing, and managing resources without requiring a separate Kustomize binary.

KEP-4292.title: Custom profiling support in kubectl debug command
KEP-4292.summary: Introduces a `custom` flag to the `kubectl debug` command, allowing users to supply a JSON file that customizes container specifications (e.g., env vars, resources, ports) on top of predefined debug profiles. This enables flexible, per‑debug-session configuration without proliferating new flags, improving usability and maintainability.

KEP-2551.title: kubectl return code normalization
KEP-2551.summary: This KEP proposes to standardize and normalize the exit codes returned by kubectl for both successful and failed commands. By defining a set of distinct error codes and providing a common utility for exit code handling, it improves automation reliability and enables pipelines to react to specific failure types.

KEP-2229.title: xdg-base-dir
KEP-2229.summary: This KEP proposes that kubectl adopt the XDG Base Directory Specification, switching the default configuration location from $HOME/.kube to $HOME/.config/kube. It includes automatic migration of existing configs and maintains compatibility with the legacy location during the transition.

KEP-2380.title: Data Driven Commands for Kubectl
KEP-2380.summary: This KEP proposes a data‑driven approach for kubectl commands, allowing the server to publish command definitions (including request endpoints, body templates, flags, and output formats) that the client can consume at runtime. By decoupling command implementations from the kubectl binary, it improves support for extension APIs and mitigates version‑skew issues between clients and servers.

KEP-2381.title: future-of-kubectl-cp
KEP-2381.summary: This KEP proposes simplifying kubectl cp to provide only basic file and directory copying between local environments and pods, dropping advanced features like symlink handling and permission changes due to recurring security vulnerabilities. It recommends using kubectl exec with tar as a more transparent and secure alternative for complex copy scenarios, and aims to reduce maintenance risk while still covering the majority of use cases.

KEP-3659.title: ApplySet: kubectl apply --prune redesign and graduation strategy
KEP-3659.summary: This KEP redesigns the kubectl apply --prune functionality by introducing a low‑level grouping concept called ApplySet. The new design provides a safer, more performant pruning mechanism that works across namespaced and cluster‑scoped resources, including custom resources, and serves as a foundation for higher‑level tooling.

KEP-2384.title: Kustomize File Processing Integration
KEP-2384.summary: This KEP integrates Kustomize directly into kubectl's cli-runtime file processing libraries, adding a new -k/--kustomize flag to kubectl commands for handling kustomization.yaml directories. It simplifies the user experience by removing the need to pipe kustomize output and improves error handling and messaging.

KEP-2985.title: Public KRM Functions Registry
KEP-2985.summary: This KEP proposes creating a public, vendor‑neutral registry for KRM functions, enabling the community to discover, publish, and trust functions across a centralized index and website. By standardizing publication via publishers and leveraging existing tooling (OWNERS files, verified commits), it improves Day 0 and Day 2 experiences for users of Kustomize, Kpt, and other orchestrators that run KRM functions.

KEP-2299.title: Kustomize Plugin Composition API
KEP-2299.summary: This KEP introduces a new Kustomize API kind called Composition that treats plugins as first-class components of a configuration bundle. It enables users to declaratively compose, import, override, and reorder plugin transformers alongside built-in transformers, providing a more flexible and expressive workflow for plugin-centric configurations.

KEP-5295.title: KYAML
KEP-5295.summary: This KEP introduces KYAML, a new output format for kubectl that emits a strict subset of YAML designed to avoid common YAML pitfalls such as whitespace sensitivity and ambiguous scalar typing. By providing a deterministic, flow‑style encoding and making it the standard for documentation and examples, KYAML aims to reduce user errors and improve tooling compatibility while remaining fully parsable by existing YAML parsers.

KEP-3895.title: Interactive(-i) flag to kubectl delete for user confirmation
KEP-3895.summary: Adds an optional interactive (-i) flag to the kubectl delete command that displays a preview of resources to be deleted and prompts the user for confirmation before proceeding. This helps prevent accidental deletions and protects administrators from irreversible actions.

KEP-2906.title: Kustomize Function Catalog
KEP-2906.summary: This KEP introduces a new Catalog API kind that centralizes discovery and distribution of Kustomize functions, allowing Kustomization, Component, and Composition resources to reference functions via a standard catalog rather than explicit container references. The catalog can be sourced locally, via HTTP(S), or as OCI artifacts, simplifying function installation and enabling official extensions to be distributed as containers.

KEP-3805.title: Kubectl Server-Side Apply by default
KEP-3805.summary: This KEP proposes making Server-Side Apply the default behavior for kubectl apply (and kubectl diff) by introducing an "auto" value for the --server-side flag, gradually transitioning to true. The change aims to increase adoption of Server-Side Apply, simplify kubectl maintenance, and reduce confusion between client-side and server-side apply mechanisms while providing a smooth migration path for existing users.

KEP-2257.title: Kui Graphical Terminal Enhancements
KEP-2257.summary: This KEP introduces a kubectl plugin framework that integrates the Kui project to provide graphical pop‑ups directly from terminal commands. It enables developers to create rich, Electron‑based UI extensions for kubectl and distribute them via krew, enhancing user experience without replacing existing textual plugins.

KEP-1802.title: Kustomize Components
KEP-1802.summary: This KEP introduces a new Kustomize kind called Component and a new kustomization field named components, enabling reusable, composable configuration pieces that can be mixed into higher-level overlays. By evaluating components sequentially after resource accumulation, it solves conflicts inherent in the traditional overlay inheritance model and supports modular application deployments with optional features.

KEP-2383.title: Extend Kustomize Patches to Multiple Targets
KEP-2383.summary: This KEP introduces a new `patches` field to Kustomization, allowing a single strategic merge or JSON patch to be applied to multiple resources selected via label selectors, annotations, GVKN, or name regex. It simplifies common use‑cases such as adding sidecars, modifying container arguments, or overriding fields across many objects, and paves the way to deprecate the older `patchesStrategicMerge` and `patchesJson6902` fields.

KEP-1441.title: kubectl debug
KEP-1441.summary: This KEP adds a new `kubectl debug` command that enables users to create ephemeral debug containers, copy pods with modified images, or launch privileged containers on nodes for interactive troubleshooting. The feature provides a first‑class, Kubernetes‑native debugging experience without requiring pre‑installed tools or administrative node access.

KEP-1020.title: Move Kubectl Code into Staging
KEP-1020.summary: This KEP proposes moving the k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/kubectl code into the staging repository (k8s.io/kubernetes/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl). The move decouples kubectl from internal Kubernetes dependencies, facilitates reuse by external projects, and is a prerequisite for the eventual migration of the kubectl binary into its own repository.

KEP-3515.title: Kubectl Explain OpenAPIv3
KEP-3515.summary: This KEP enhances kubectl explain by switching its data source from OpenAPI v2 to the richer OpenAPI v3 spec and replacing the hand‑written printer with a go/template based implementation. The change provides richer type information (e.g., nullable, defaults, validation) and new output formats while gracefully falling back when v3 is unavailable.

KEP-2382.title: Kustomize Exec Secret Generator
KEP-2382.summary: This KEP reintroduces the ability for Kustomize to generate Secrets via exec plugins, allowing users to fetch or decrypt secret data at build time without storing it on disk. It adds explicit opt‑in flags and restricted plugin paths to mitigate security risks associated with executing arbitrary commands.

KEP-2379.title: Kubectl Plugins
KEP-2379.summary: This KEP defines a git‑style plugin mechanism for kubectl where any executable on the user's PATH prefixed with `kubectl-` is automatically discovered and invoked as a kubectl subcommand. It enables users to extend kubectl functionality without additional installation steps, allowing custom commands and subcommands to be added directly via standard executables and optional shell‑completion support.

KEP-2206.title: OpenAPI Features in Kustomize
KEP-2206.summary: This KEP introduces an `openapi` field in kustomization files allowing users to specify a custom OpenAPI schema for Kustomize, and adds a `kustomize openapi fetch` command to retrieve the OpenAPI schema from the current cluster. By enabling custom schemas, Kustomize can correctly apply strategic merge patches for custom resources, improving flexibility and reducing the need to recompile Kustomize for schema updates.

KEP-2377.title: Kustomize
KEP-2377.summary: This KEP proposes Kustomize, a declarative configuration tool that enables users to reference, generate, and transform Kubernetes manifests using a kustomization.yaml file. It brings imperative kubectl capabilities (e.g., configmap/secret creation, labeling, patching) into a declarative workflow, improving GitOps and reducing the need for custom scripting.

KEP-859.title: Kubectl Commands In Headers
KEP-859.summary: This KEP introduces optional HTTP request headers (Kubectl-Command and Kubectl-Session) that kubectl sends to the kube-apiserver, providing context about the originating kubectl command and a session identifier. The headers enable cluster operators to debug request origins and gather telemetry on kubectl usage without altering server behavior.

KEP-2227.title: kubectl default container
KEP-2227.summary: This KEP introduces a well‑known optional annotation (kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-container) that allows pod creators to specify which container should be used by default for kubectl commands such as exec, attach, cp, and logs. It improves operator experience by removing reliance on container order, especially in multi‑container pods with sidecars.

KEP-1440.title: Kubectl events
KEP-1440.summary: This KEP introduces a new `kubectl events` subcommand to provide dedicated, extensible event handling separate from `kubectl get events`. It adds richer watch, sorting, filtering, and timeline capabilities, addressing long‑standing usability limitations without altering existing `kubectl get` behavior.

KEP-2385.title: Kustomize Secret Generator Plugins
KEP-2385.summary: This KEP adds a plugin framework to Kustomize’s SecretGenerator, allowing users to generate secret key/value pairs via pluggable sources. The initial implementation supports Go plugins, enabling integration with external secret management tools and replacing insecure file‑based value sourcing. The design is extensible to other plugin types such as exec‑style plugins.

KEP-3638.title: Improve kubectl plugin resolution for non-shadowing subcommands
KEP-3638.summary: This KEP enhances kubectl by allowing external plugins to act as subcommands of built-in commands when the subcommand does not already exist. By searching for matching plugins (e.g., kubectl-create-foo) and executing them, it reduces the need to add new static subcommands to the binary, easing maintenance and supporting custom resources. An opt‑in environment variable KUBECTL_ENABLE_CMD_SHADOW controls the feature during the alpha and beta phases.

KEP-2590.title: Kubectl Subresource Support
KEP-2590.summary: This KEP proposes adding a new `--subresource` flag to the kubectl commands `get`, `patch`, `edit`, `apply`, and `replace`. The flag enables users to fetch and update common subresources such as `status`, `scale`, and `resize` directly through kubectl, eliminating the need for raw API calls via curl and improving the debugging and management workflow.

KEP-1326.title: doc-policies-for-third-party-content
KEP-1326.summary: This KEP establishes policies for Kubernetes documentation to limit and manage third‑party and dual‑sourced content. It defines when third‑party material may be included (only when required for Kubernetes to function in‑project) and requires linking to external sources wherever possible, thereby improving consistency, maintainability, and reducing vendor advertising in the docs.

KEP-3299.title: KMS v2 Improvements
KEP-3299.summary: KEP-3299 introduces a KMS v2 service contract that adds key rotation without API server restarts, improves health checks, and enhances observability of envelope operations. It adds a new KMS API version, DEK seed reuse, key_id handling, status RPC, and hot‑reload of EncryptionConfiguration to reduce latency and rate‑limit impacts in large clusters.

KEP-2718.title: Client Executable Proxy
KEP-2718.summary: The Client Executable Proxy KEP adds a client‑side exec‑proxy mechanism that forwards Kubernetes API requests to an external process for arbitrary modification, such as request signing or header injection, before they reach the API server. This enables secure, configurable authentication methods like AWS Signature V4 or hardware‑protected TLS signing without relying on traditional HTTP proxy setups.

KEP-600.title: Dynamic Audit Configuration
KEP-600.summary: This KEP introduces a cluster‑scoped AuditConfiguration custom resource that allows advanced audit settings (policy and webhook backend) to be changed dynamically at runtime without restarting the API server. It adds a new dynamic audit backend, feature gate, and supporting API types to let administrators and extensions configure audit policies and webhook destinations on the fly, improving flexibility and operability.

KEP-2799.title: Reduction of Secret-based Service Account Tokens
