KEP-2799.summary: This KEP reduces the surface area of secret-based service account tokens by disabling their auto-generation, adding tracking for legacy tokens via a configmap, and eventually cleaning up unused auto-generated tokens. It introduces feature gates to control these behaviors, encouraging the use of the TokenRequest API and improving cluster security.

KEP-789.title: Harden Default RBAC Discovery ClusterRole(Binding)s
KEP-789.summary: This KEP hardens the default RBAC discovery permissions by removing the system:unauthenticated group from the system:discovery and system:basic-user ClusterRoleBindings, while preserving unauthenticated access to a minimal public info role (system:public-info-viewer). The change improves the default security and privacy posture of new clusters by limiting unauthenticated discovery of API resources.

KEP-4193.title: bound service account token improvements
KEP-4193.summary: This KEP enhances bound service account tokens by embedding the Pod's Node name and UID into the JWT, adding a unique JTI claim for each token, and extending the TokenRequest API to allow tokens to be bound directly to Node objects. These changes improve replay‑attack resistance, enable stronger identity verification across node boundaries, and provide better audit traceability of token usage.

KEP-4317.title: Pod Certificates
KEP-4317.summary: The Pod Certificates KEP introduces a new PodCertificateRequest API type and a corresponding projected volume source that enable pods to securely obtain X.509 certificates without using bearer tokens. This mechanism automates key and certificate provisioning directly via the kubelet, improving security and simplifying integration of third‑party signers.

KEP-3221.title: Structured Authorization Configuration
KEP-3221.summary: This KEP introduces a structured configuration file (AuthorizationConfiguration) for the kube-apiserver to declaratively define the authorization chain, enabling multiple ordered webhooks, fine‑grained control, CEL‑based request filtering, failure policies, and dynamic reload. It provides administrators with more flexibility and safety when configuring authorizers compared to the existing flat flag‑based approach.

KEP-1687.title: Hierarchical Namespace Controller As A Subproject
KEP-1687.summary: This KEP proposes establishing the Hierarchical Namespace Controller (HNC) as its own subproject under sig-auth with a dedicated repository. Moving HNC from the Multi-Tenancy Working Group to a sig-owned subproject provides a permanent home, clearer governance, and avoids future migration pain as it approaches MVP status.

KEP-2579.title: PSP Replacement Policy
KEP-2579.summary: The KEP replaces the deprecated PodSecurityPolicy with a built-in PodSecurity admission controller that enforces the Pod Security Standards via namespace labels. It introduces enforce, audit, and warn modes, versioned policies, and dry‑run checks to provide secure, flexible, and backward‑compatible pod security enforcement.

KEP-4872.title: Harden Kubelet Serving Certificate Validation in Kube-API server
KEP-4872.summary: This KEP introduces validation of the kubelet serving certificate's Common Name (CN) by the kube-apiserver to ensure it matches the expected node name (system:node:<nodename>). The feature, gated by KubeletCertCNValidation, prevents compromised nodes from impersonating other nodes by using certificates issued for IPs they do not own, enhancing cluster security.

KEP-3331.title: Structured authentication config
KEP-3331.summary: This KEP introduces a new structured authentication configuration API object for the kube-apiserver, allowing JWT/OIDC authentication to be defined via a versioned config file instead of flag-based settings. It adds support for multiple providers, claim validation and mapping using CEL expressions, and dynamic reloading of authentication settings.

KEP-740.title: Support external signing of service account tokens
KEP-740.summary: Adds support for external signing of Kubernetes service account JWT tokens by introducing a new gRPC ExternalJWTSigner API and a kube-apiserver flag to point to an external signer (e.g., HSM or cloud KMS). This enables key rotation without restarting the apiserver and improves security by keeping private signing material out of the cluster control plane.

KEP-5018.title: DRA Admin Access
KEP-5018.summary: The KEP introduces a privileged admin mode for Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) by adding an optional `adminAccess` flag to DeviceRequests in ResourceClaim and ResourceClaimTemplate objects. This enables cluster administrators to access devices already in use for monitoring or troubleshooting, while restricting the capability to namespaces labeled for admin access and guarded by the DRAAdminAccess feature gate.

KEP-4940.title: Add Pod Security Admission (PSA) to block setting `.host` field from ProbeHandler and LifecycleHandler
KEP-4940.summary: This KEP adds a Pod Security Admission (PSA) policy that blocks the use of the `.host` field in ProbeHandler and LifecycleHandler configurations for containers and initContainers. By preventing users from setting arbitrary hosts in probes, it mitigates potential SSRF attacks and improves cluster security.

KEP-1393.title: Service Account signing key retrieval
KEP-1393.summary: This KEP adds a non‑resource API exposing an OpenID Connect discovery document and a JWKS endpoint that contain the issuer URL and the public keys used to sign Kubernetes Service Account tokens. By making the signing keys discoverable, external relying parties can verify service account tokens directly, reducing load on the API server and enabling token use across clusters and external services.

KEP-5284.title: Constrained Impersonation
KEP-5284.summary: Constrained Impersonation introduces fine‑grained RBAC verbs that restrict impersonation to specific resource types, modes, and verbs. It requires an impersonator to hold both a constrained impersonation permission and explicit impersonate‑on:<mode>:<verb> permissions, enabling safer controller impersonation while preserving existing client semantics.

KEP-1314.title: Extended NodeRestrictions for Pods
KEP-1314.summary: This KEP extends the NodeRestriction admission controller to add additional safeguards for pods created by nodes, including whitelisting allowed label keys per namespace, prohibiting label changes via the pod/status subresource, and limiting mirror pod OwnerReferences to reference only the node. These restrictions mitigate confused‑deputy attacks where a compromised node could manipulate pod metadata to affect other controllers.

KEP-2784.title: CSR Duration
KEP-2784.summary: This KEP extends the CertificateSigningRequest API by adding an optional spec.expirationSeconds field, allowing clients to request a specific certificate validity duration. It enhances security by enabling short-lived certificates and gives signers a way to honor requested lifetimes while remaining optional for backward compatibility.

KEP-541.title: External credential providers
KEP-541.summary: External credential providers enable Kubernetes clients to obtain authentication credentials via out-of-tree executables, allowing dynamic retrieval of bearer tokens or client certificates. This mechanism supports credential rotation without restarts, integration with external key management systems, and vendor-neutral authentication flows.

KEP-4601.title: Authorize with Selectors
KEP-4601.summary: This KEP extends the authorization attributes to include field and label selectors for List, Watch, and DeleteCollection verbs, and propagates those selectors into SubjectAccessReview, SelfSubjectAccessReview, and LocalSubjectAccessReview objects. By exposing selectors to authorizers, including webhook and CEL authorizers, it enables finer-grained, selector‑based access control for per‑node workloads and other use‑cases.

KEP-4412.title: Projected Service Account Tokens for Kubelet Image Credential Providers
KEP-4412.summary: This KEP introduces projected Service Account tokens for Kubelet image credential providers, allowing pods to use short‑lived, audience‑bound service account tokens to authenticate image pulls. It eliminates the need for long‑lived image pull secrets, improving security and reducing secret management overhead.

KEP-2907.title: Secrets Store CSI Driver
KEP-2907.summary: The Secrets Store CSI Driver KEP introduces a new CSI driver and associated Custom Resource Definitions (SecretProviderClass and SecretProviderClassPodStatus) to enable pods to fetch secrets from external secret stores via a filesystem mount. This makes the core driver functionality generally available (GA), providing a portable, secure way to consume external secrets without extending the native Kubernetes Secret object.

KEP-266.title: Kubelet client certificate bootstrap and rotation
KEP-266.summary: This KEP introduces a kubelet client certificate bootstrap and rotation mechanism that allows a node to obtain its initial client certificate via a short‑lived bootstrap credential and automatically rotate it as it approaches expiration. The design leverages CertificateSigningRequests, a CertificateManager within the kubelet, and a feature gate to provide secure, hands‑free credential management for nodes.

KEP-1513.title: Certificates API
KEP-1513.summary: The Certificates API provides a programmatic interface for requesting and obtaining X.509 certificates from a Certificate Authority within Kubernetes. It introduces a generic, asynchronous workflow with distinct approver and signer controllers, enabling automated and secure certificate provisioning for both core components and user workloads.

KEP-279.title: Bounding Self-Labeling Kubelets
KEP-279.summary: This KEP tightens node self‑labeling by updating the NodeRestriction admission plugin to block kubelets from setting arbitrary labels in the kubernetes.io and k8s.io namespaces, allowing only a predefined safe set and reserving a new prefix for cluster‑admin labels. The change improves cluster security by preventing compromised nodes from spoofing labels used for workload isolation and scheduling.

KEP-4633.title: Only allow anonymous auth for configured endpoints
KEP-4633.summary: This KEP introduces configurable anonymous authentication for the kube-apiserver, allowing administrators to enable, disable, or restrict anonymous access to specific API endpoints via the AuthenticationConfiguration. It mitigates security risks from misconfigured RoleBindings while preserving necessary unauthenticated health checks and bootstrap operations.

KEP-3325.title: Review attibutes of a current user
KEP-3325.summary: The KEP adds a new SelfSubjectReview API endpoint in the authentication.k8s.io group that returns the attributes of the currently authenticated user (UserInfo). It also introduces a corresponding kubectl command (kubectl auth whoami) to help operators debug and inspect authentication results.

KEP-3257.title: Cluster Trust Bundles
KEP-3257.summary: This KEP introduces a new cluster-scoped API object, ClusterTrustBundle, to distribute X.509 trust anchors from in‑cluster certificate signers to workloads. It also adds a new kubelet projected volume source, clusterTrustBundle, allowing pods to mount these trust bundles directly from the API, simplifying trust anchor distribution and rotation.

KEP-3130.title: KMS Observability
KEP-3130.summary: This KEP introduces a transaction ID (UID) for each envelope encryption/decryption operation, adding the UID field to the kms-plugin API and logging it in the kube-apiserver. The UID enables correlation of logs across kube-apiserver, kms-plugin, and external KMS, improving observability of secret encryption processes.

KEP-3926.title: Handling undecryptable resources
KEP-3926.summary: This KEP adds the ability to identify resources that cannot be decrypted or decoded due to encryption-at-rest failures and introduces a new DeleteOption (gateable via the AllowUnsafeMalformedObjectDeletion feature gate) that lets administrators delete such malformed objects through the Kubernetes API. It also defines a new status reason (StatusReasonStoreReadError) to surface storage read errors, improving observability and recovery of corrupted resources.

KEP-1205.title: Bound Service Account Tokens
KEP-1205.summary: This KEP introduces the TokenRequest API to allow workloads to request JWTs that are audience, time, and optionally object bound, improving security over the existing service account token model. It also adds token projection for pods via a ServiceAccountTokenProjection volume source and updates TokenReview to validate audience bindings, enabling a migration to bound service account tokens.

KEP-3077.title: Contextual logging
KEP-3077.summary: Contextual logging replaces the global klog logger with a logr.Logger passed via context.Context or an explicit parameter, enabling callers to attach key/value pairs, names, and control verbosity for log messages. This change removes the hard dependency on klog, improves testability by allowing per‑test loggers, and integrates with structured logging and log/slog while being gated behind a feature flag.

KEP-3766.title: Move ReferenceGrant to sig-auth API Group
KEP-3766.summary: This KEP proposes moving the ReferenceGrant resource from the gateway.networking.k8s.io API group to the neutral authorization.k8s.io API group managed by SIG Auth. By doing so, ReferenceGrant becomes the canonical API for enabling safe cross‑namespace object references across multiple SIGs such as Gateway API and SIG Storage.

KEP-1753.title: Kubernetes system components logs sanitization
KEP-1753.summary: This KEP introduces a dynamic logging filter for Kubernetes system components that redacts sensitive information such as passwords, tokens, and security keys from log entries. By tagging struct fields with datapolicy tags and integrating a verification library with klog, the feature aims to prevent accidental exposure of secrets while keeping performance impact acceptable.

KEP-3498.title: Extending Metrics Stability
KEP-3498.summary: This KEP extends the existing metric stability framework by introducing additional stability classes—beta and internal—along with refined semantics for alpha metrics, enabling finer-grained stability guarantees aligned with the feature release cycle. It also enhances the static analysis tooling that validates metric definitions, improving reliability and documentation of Kubernetes metrics.

KEP-2845.title: Deprecate klog specific flags in Kubernetes components
KEP-2845.summary: This KEP proposes deprecating and eventually removing a subset of klog-specific command‑line flags from core Kubernetes components, keeping only -v and --vmodule (and log-flush-frequency). The change simplifies logging configuration, aligns with 12‑factor app principles, and reduces maintenance complexity while enabling alternative logging formats like JSON.

KEP-1748.title: Expose Pod Resource Request Metrics
KEP-1748.summary: This KEP proposes adding a new multi-dimensional Prometheus metric, pod_resources, to expose pod resource request information such as requests, limits, and lifecycle state. The metric enables administrators to more easily monitor cluster capacity, plan resources, and detect contention without relying on high-cardinality kube-state-metrics data.

KEP-4785.title: Resource State Metrics
KEP-4785.summary: Resource State Metrics introduces a new Kubernetes controller and CRD (ResourceMetricsMonitor) that generates metrics for custom resources based on configurable schemas. It replaces the Custom Resource State API in kube-state-metrics, improving maintainability, scalability, and isolation of custom resource metric generation.

KEP-1206.title: Kubernetes Metrics Overhaul
KEP-1206.summary: This KEP proposes a comprehensive overhaul of all metrics instrumented in the Kubernetes codebase to align with the official instrumentation guidelines and Prometheus best practices. It introduces consistent labeling, converts summary metrics to histograms where appropriate, and updates metric names and units across core components such as kubelet, apiserver, scheduler, proxy, and client-go, facilitating easier aggregation, querying, and migration for users.

KEP-4827.title: Component Statusz
KEP-4827.summary: The KEP introduces a new /statusz endpoint on all core Kubernetes components, providing standardized real-time information about the component's build version, Go version, compatibility, and uptime. This enhances observability and debugging by exposing essential component details via both human‑readable text and a versioned JSON API, secured behind a feature gate and RBAC.

KEP-1209.title: Metrics Stability Framework
KEP-1209.summary: The Metrics Stability Framework KEP consolidates previous documents to define a lifecycle for control‑plane metrics, introducing stability annotations and validation tooling to ensure metric APIs remain stable across releases. It improves reliability for operators and users by preventing breaking changes to metrics and promoting stable metrics to GA.

KEP-3466.title: Kubernetes Component Health SLIs
KEP-3466.summary: The KEP adds a new `/metrics/slis` endpoint to Kubernetes components that emits health‑check data as structured Prometheus metrics, enabling monitoring agents to collect Service Level Indicator (SLI) data at higher scrape intervals and build Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and alerts. This provides a uniform, low‑cardinality health‑checking interface without requiring specialized parsing logic.

KEP-2305.title: Dynamic Cardinality Enforcement
KEP-2305.summary: This KEP introduces a runtime-configurable allowlist for metric label values, enabling components to enforce bounded cardinality for Prometheus metrics. By adding a command‑line flag that ingests allowlists during component startup, it prevents memory leaks caused by unbounded label dimensions without requiring code changes or binary releases.

KEP-1013.title: Watch support for metrics APIs
KEP-1013.summary: This KEP adds watch support to the existing metrics APIs (metrics.k8s.io, custom.metrics.k8s.io, and external.metrics.k8s.io), enabling clients to subscribe to a stream of metric updates instead of polling. By exposing a `watch` query parameter, metric consumers such as the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler can receive new data points as soon as they become available, reducing latency and load on the metrics backend.

KEP-383.title: New Event API GA Graduation
KEP-383.summary: This KEP graduates the new Event API to GA, introducing a richer, more structured Event object with first‑class fields such as eventTime, action, regarding, related, reportingController and series information. The changes reduce performance impact and improve observability by enabling better deduplication, querying, and backoff handling for cluster events.

KEP-2831.title: Kubelet OpenTelemetry Tracing
KEP-2831.summary: This KEP enhances the kubelet to generate and export OpenTelemetry spans for its gRPC and HTTP interactions, including CRI, CNI, and CSI calls. By adding tracing configuration to the kubelet, operators can collect distributed trace data to diagnose node‑level latency and failures, improving observability of Kubernetes clusters.

KEP-647.title: APIServer Tracing
KEP-647.summary: The KEP adds native OpenTelemetry-based tracing to the Kubernetes API server, enabling it to generate, propagate, and export spans for incoming and outgoing requests. This provides observability through distributed tracing, helping operators debug control-plane issues and integrate with existing tracing backends.

KEP-1602.title: Structured Logging
KEP-1602.summary: This KEP defines a standard structure for Kubernetes log messages, adds new klog methods (InfoS, ErrorS) to enforce that structure, and introduces an optional JSON logging output format. It aims to make logs more queryable, simplify ingestion by third‑party logging solutions, and provide a migration path toward structured logging in the control plane.

KEP-4828.title: Component Flagz
KEP-4828.summary: The KEP adds a /flagz endpoint to core Kubernetes components, exposing the command‑line flags each component was started with. This improves observability and debugging by allowing administrators and developers to view active flag values in plain‑text or a versioned JSON format.

KEP-2314.title: Custom endpoints support for AWS Cloud Provider
KEP-2314.summary: The KEP adds support for configuring custom AWS service endpoints in the Kubernetes AWS Cloud Provider, enabling use of alternative implementations such as Eucalyptus and private AWS endpoints via AWS PrivateLink. This allows both the cloud controller and kubelet to communicate with non‑standard AWS endpoints, improving security and flexibility for clusters running on AWS.

KEP-2313.title: aws-k8s-tester
KEP-2313.summary: The KEP proposes aws-k8s-tester, a kubetest plugin that creates and tears down AWS resources such as EKS clusters to run Kubernetes end‑to‑end tests. It aims to improve test coverage of EKS, ensure feature parity with upstream Kubernetes, and provide transparent, automated testing for AWS‑specific components.

KEP-423.title: graduate-aws-nlb-to-beta
KEP-423.summary: This KEP proposes graduating AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) support from Alpha to Beta in Kubernetes. The graduation stabilizes the NLB integration, enabling users to reliably create Services of type LoadBalancer that provision AWS NLBs with features like cross‑zone load balancing and TLS termination.

KEP-2315.title: AWS LoadBalancer Prefix
KEP-2315.summary: This KEP adds a Service annotation that lets users specify a prefix for the AWS ELB name generated for LoadBalancer services. The predictable naming enables integration with existing AWS IAM policies that depend on resource name prefixes, allowing separate teams to manage security and provisioning. It addresses the current limitation where ELB names are derived from unpredictable UIDs.

KEP-629.title: AWS ALB Ingress Controller
KEP-629.summary: This KEP proposes adopting the AWS ALB Ingress Controller as a native Ingress controller for Kubernetes clusters on AWS, enabling Ingress resources to be backed by Amazon Application Load Balancers. It leverages ALB features like host/path routing, TLS termination, HTTP/2, and integrates with AWS services such as WAF and Cognito, improving security and functionality for workloads on AWS.

KEP-630.title: aws-ebs-csi-driver
KEP-630.summary: The AWS EBS CSI Driver implements the Container Storage Interface to provide out‑of‑tree support for AWS Elastic Block Store volumes in Kubernetes. It offers static and dynamic provisioning, volume scheduling, mount options, raw block access, and offline volume resizing, enabling seamless migration from the in‑tree EBS plugin while allowing independent release cycles.

KEP-4743.title: Kubernetes-etcd interface
KEP-4743.summary: This KEP defines a formal etcd‑Kubernetes interface that will be added to the etcd client and adopted by Kubernetes, codifying the existing contract between the two projects. The interface improves testability, prevents misuse, and provides a clear, backward‑compatible pathway for backporting etcd client updates and adopting new etcd functionality.

KEP-4331.title: Livez readyz
KEP-4331.summary: This KEP introduces separate /livez and /readyz HTTP endpoints for etcd, providing distinct liveness and readiness probes that align with Kubernetes probe semantics. The new probes allow more granular health checking, enabling kubelet or load balancers to restart unhealthy nodes or stop sending traffic to nodes that are not ready to serve KV and watch operations.

KEP-1659.title: Standard Topology Labels
KEP-1659.summary: This KEP formalizes the existing topology.kubernetes.io/region and topology.kubernetes.io/zone node labels as standard labels with well‑defined semantics, providing clear documentation for their hierarchical relationship and immutability. It also evaluates the need for a potential third topology level, aiming to improve consistency for components that rely on topology information without introducing code changes.

KEP-4578.title: Feature Gate in etcd
KEP-4578.summary: This KEP proposes adding a Kubernetes‑style feature gate framework to the etcd server, allowing features to be enabled or disabled via a unified `--feature-gates` flag and to be queried at runtime. It codifies feature lifecycles (Alpha, Beta, GA, Deprecated), replaces the existing experimental flag mechanism, and provides metrics for observability.

KEP-3935.title: Support Oldest Node And Newest Control Plane
KEP-3935.summary: This KEP proposes expanding the supported version skew between node components (kubelet and kube-proxy) and control‑plane components from the current n‑2 to n‑3, allowing the oldest supported node version to communicate with the newest supported control‑plane version. By doing so, upgrade paths are streamlined, reducing the number of disruptive node upgrades required during multi‑version upgrades and better aligning the skew policy with the yearly support period.

KEP-4326.title: Downgrade support
KEP-4326.summary: This KEP introduces a storage version (SV) stored within the etcd DB file to indicate the compatibility version of etcd data, enabling safe upgrades and downgrades of the data. It also adds an offline tool, etcdutl migrate, to upgrade or downgrade data directories, simplifying the upgrade process and improving reliability of etcd clusters.

KEP-1618.title: Conformance Profiles
KEP-1618.summary: This KEP introduces the concept of conformance profiles, allowing optional Kubernetes features to be grouped into defined sets of behaviors. By enabling profile-specific conformance testing, vendors and users can verify that clusters meet the required functionality for specific workloads, improving portability and certification clarity.

KEP-1194.title: Production Readiness Review Process
KEP-1194.summary: The KEP introduces a Production Readiness Review (PRR) process for features entering alpha, beta, or GA stages, ensuring they are observable, supportable, and can be safely rolled back in production. It establishes criteria, questionnaires, and CI enforcement via Prow to embed operational considerations into the Kubernetes feature lifecycle.

KEP-1333.title: Ensure Conformance Tests Do Not Require Beta APIs or Features
KEP-1333.summary: This KEP defines a process to ensure that Kubernetes components and conformance tests do not depend on beta REST APIs or feature gates. It introduces CI jobs and runtime-config flags to disable alpha/beta APIs and feature gates, and outlines a phased plan to identify, block, and remove existing beta dependencies, improving the reliability of conformance for production distributions.

KEP-917.title: go modules
KEP-917.summary: This KEP migrates the Kubernetes codebase to use Go modules for managing the vendor directory and introduces go.mod files for staging components such as client-go and api. It also defines a publishing and versioning strategy for these components, removes the legacy Godeps workflow, and improves build speed and reproducibility.

KEP-1635.title: Require Transition from Beta
KEP-1635.summary: This KEP enforces that any Kubernetes REST API that reaches beta must transition to GA or a new beta within nine months (three releases), otherwise it is deprecated with intent to remove. The policy ensures beta APIs do not remain in a perpetual beta state, improving stability and encouraging timely graduation.

KEP-4330.title: Compatibility Versions
KEP-4330.summary: This KEP proposes adding `--emulation-version` and `--min-compatibility-version` flags to Kubernetes control‑plane components, allowing a binary to emulate the behavior of an earlier release and to define the minimum version it must remain compatible with. The goal is to make upgrades safer and more granular by controlling API, feature, and storage version exposure, thereby improving upgrade reliability, rollback capabilities, and version skew handling.

KEP-5241.title: Beta Feature Gate Promotion Requirements
KEP-5241.summary: This KEP defines strict promotion requirements for Kubernetes feature gates moving from Beta to GA, requiring that all functional, security, monitoring, and testing issues identified during Beta be resolved before default enablement. It establishes clear criteria and processes to ensure feature gates are stable and safe for production clusters, preventing incomplete or unstable features from being enabled by default.

KEP-1143.title: Appropriate use of node-role labels
KEP-1143.summary: This KEP clarifies that the node-role.kubernetes.io/* label namespace is reserved for end‑users and external tooling and must not be used by Kubernetes components to change behavior. It defines a migration path for internal consumers to replace reliance on these labels with new, feature‑gated node labels and removes legacy behavior across upcoming releases.

KEP-3136.title: Beta APIs Are Off by Default
KEP-3136.summary: Starting with the release that introduces this change, beta APIs will be disabled by default in new clusters. Existing beta APIs and new versions of already-enabled beta APIs remain enabled, while enabling additional beta APIs requires explicit --runtime-config flags, allowing cluster admins to opt‑in selectively.

KEP-617.title: Enhance KEP implementation
KEP-617.summary: This KEP proposes enhancements to the KEP implementation process, including standardized markers for unresolved sections, renaming and restructuring KEP files into directories, splitting metadata into a separate YAML file, and improving GitHub tooling. These changes aim to make KEPs easier to navigate, reference, and automate for both humans and tooling, thereby improving the overall KEP adoption and management.

KEP-960.title: Behavior-driven Conformance Testing
KEP-960.summary: This KEP proposes a behavior‑driven approach to Kubernetes conformance testing, where expected cluster behaviors are defined, approved, and tracked separately from the tests that validate them. Tooling would generate behavior lists from API schemas, create test scaffolding, and produce coverage reports, improving visibility and review efficiency for conformance validation.

KEP-4402.title: Go workspaces for k/k
KEP-4402.summary: This KEP proposes adopting Go workspaces in the main Kubernetes repository to replace legacy GOPATH-based tooling, modernize the build and code generation processes, and simplify multi-module development. By introducing a go.work file and updating tools like gengo and kube-openapi, it removes GOPATH hackery, enabling upstream tooling such as gopls and improving developer experience without impacting cluster users.

KEP-2527.title: Clarify if/how controllers can use status to track non-observable state
KEP-2527.summary: This KEP clarifies and relaxes the long‑standing rule that status fields must be fully reconstructable from observation, allowing controllers to store allocation or acknowledgment information in status. It also provides guidance on when to use separate objects versus status for controller‑owned data and how the spec/status split can be leveraged for access control.

KEP-4885.title: Windows CPU and Memory Affinity
KEP-4885.summary: This KEP adds support for the CPU, Memory, and Topology managers on Windows nodes by extending the kubelet to understand Windows processor groups and NUMA topology, and by introducing a new Windows-only memory policy (BestEffort). It enables CPU and memory affinity for Windows pods, providing isolation and performance improvements similar to existing Linux functionality.

KEP-4802.title: Windows Graceful Node Shutdown
KEP-4802.summary: This KEP adds support for graceful node shutdown on Windows nodes by making the kubelet aware of Windows shutdown events and triggering pod termination with appropriate grace periods. It enables pods to execute pre‑stop hooks and terminate cleanly during node shutdown, aligning Windows behavior with the existing Linux graceful shutdown feature.

KEP-1981.title: Windows Privileged Container Support
KEP-1981.summary: This KEP adds support for privileged containers on Windows by introducing a HostProcess flag in the Windows security context and enabling host network mode for privileged pods. This allows Windows workloads to run with host-level access similar to Linux privileged containers, simplifying deployment of networking, storage, and administrative daemons.

KEP-689.title: Windows Group Managed Service Accounts for Container Identity
KEP-689.summary: This KEP adds support for Windows Group Managed Service Accounts (GMSA) as container identities, allowing pods on Windows nodes to run with an Active Directory identity without additional files or registry keys. It introduces a cluster‑scoped GMSACredentialSpec custom resource and new securityContext fields for pods and containers to reference GMSA credentials, integrating with Kubelet, the CRI and admission/webhook mechanisms.

KEP-2258.title: Node log query
KEP-2258.summary: This KEP adds a node log query feature that exposes a `/proxy/logs/` endpoint on the kubelet, allowing cluster administrators to retrieve logs from node services (systemd/journald on Linux, /var/log/, and Windows Event logs) via the API or a kubectl plugin without needing to SSH into the node. The feature is gated by the `NodeLogQuery` feature gate and requires enabling `enableSystemLogQuery` (alongside `enableSystemLogHandler`) in the KubeletConfiguration, providing secure, streaming access to node logs for troubleshooting.

KEP-2578.title: Windows Conformance
KEP-2578.summary: The KEP defines an operational readiness specification for Kubernetes clusters that run Windows workloads, establishing a set of core and feature‑specific conformance tests that Windows clusters must pass alongside Linux conformance. It standardizes how these tests are expressed (via Ginkgo tags) and executed (e.g., through Sonobuoy), providing a clear certification path for vendors and users to verify production‑ready Windows Kubernetes deployments.

KEP-1122.title: Support for CSI Plugins on Windows Nodes
KEP-1122.summary: This KEP adds support for CSI Node Plugins on Windows nodes by introducing a new privileged proxy (csi-proxy.exe) that executes host‑level storage operations via gRPC over named pipes, and updates kubelet, CSI driver registrar, and related components to handle Windows paths and containers. The changes enable Windows workloads to use modern CSI plugins for provisioning, attaching, and managing persistent storage using standard Kubernetes constructs like DaemonSets.

KEP-5100.title: DSR and Overlay support in Windows kube-proxy
KEP-5100.summary: This KEP documents and promotes existing Direct Server Return (DSR) and overlay networking mode support in the Windows implementation of kube-proxy to GA. Enabling DSR reduces load‑balancer overhead and latency, while overlay mode allows Windows nodes to work with CNI plugins that require overlay networks, such as Calico.

KEP-1301.title: Windows RuntimeClass Support
KEP-1301.summary: This KEP introduces support for Windows RuntimeClass, enabling Pods to be scheduled onto Windows nodes based on OS version via a new node label (node.kubernetes.io/windows-build) and RuntimeHandler integration with the CRI. It facilitates selection of Windows Server releases, forward compatibility using Hyper‑V isolation, and targeting specific multi‑arch images, simplifying configuration compared to node selectors and tolerations.

KEP-2802.title: Identify Pod's OS during API Server admission
KEP-2802.summary: This KEP adds an optional OS field to the Pod spec, allowing users to declare the operating system (linux or windows) a pod is intended to run on. Admission plugins and the kubelet can then enforce OS‑specific security constraints and reject pods that cannot be scheduled on the host OS, improving security and correctness for mixed‑OS clusters.

KEP-3503.title: Host Network Support for Windows Pods
KEP-3503.summary: This KEP adds support for Windows pods to use the node's network namespace by introducing Windows-specific CRI API fields (WindowsNamespaceOption) and updating the Kubelet to set them when hostNetwork=true. It provides feature parity with Linux hostNetwork and enables scenarios like high port density and pre‑CNI daemons on Windows nodes.

KEP-1001.title: Supporting CRI-containerD on Windows
KEP-1001.summary: This KEP proposes adding support for CRI-ContainerD on Windows, enabling Kubernetes to leverage the newer Windows Server container platform (HCS v2) and upcoming ContainerD Windows support. By doing so, Windows clusters can gain improved feature compatibility, hypervisor-based isolation, resource control, and a path away from Docker EE, aligning with future dockershim deprecation.

KEP-116.title: Windows node support
KEP-116.summary: This KEP adds support for Windows compute nodes in Kubernetes, enabling the scheduling and execution of Windows Server containers alongside Linux workloads. It outlines the current capabilities, limitations, and roadmap for Windows node functionality, including networking, storage, and security considerations.

KEP-668.title: Support Out-of-Tree GCE Cloud Provider
KEP-668.summary: This KEP adds support for an out-of-tree GCE cloud provider by developing a well‑tested GCE cloud‑controller‑manager that matches the feature set of the in‑tree controller. It enables Kubernetes clusters running on GCE to use the cloud‑controller‑manager architecture, improving modularity and future maintenance.

KEP-1043.title: Windows security context API changes
KEP-1043.summary: This KEP adds Windows-specific security fields to the PodSecurityContext and Container SecurityContext APIs by introducing a WindowsOptions struct. The new fields allow native specification of GMSA credential specs and a Windows RunAsUserName, improving support for Windows workload identity without relying on annotations.

KEP-2436.title: Controller Manager Leader Migration
KEP-2436.summary: This KEP introduces a leader migration mechanism that enables highly available clusters to safely transition cloud-specific controllers from the in‑tree kube‑controller‑manager to the out‑of‑tree cloud‑controller‑manager. It adds configurable migration locks and a feature gate to coordinate controller leadership across the two components during upgrades, minimizing downtime.

KEP-1959.title: Service Type=LoadBalancer Class Field
KEP-1959.summary: This KEP introduces a new optional field `spec.loadBalancerClass` to Service objects, allowing clusters to run multiple LoadBalancer implementations side‑by‑side. The feature is gated by `ServiceLoadBalancerClass` and enables users to select or opt‑out of the default cloud‑provider load balancer without relying on provider‑specific annotations.

KEP-2025.title: Extending Apiserver Network Proxy to handle traffic originated from Node network
KEP-2025.summary: This KEP extends the apiserver network proxy (Konnectivity) to allow traffic originating from the node network to reach the Kubernetes API server without exposing the API server publicly. It introduces a bidirectional tunnel mechanism with new agent flags and feature gates, enhancing security and simplifying network isolation between node and master networks.

KEP-669.title: Support Out-of-Tree OpenStack Cloud Provider
KEP-669.summary: This KEP adds support for an out-of-tree OpenStack cloud provider by delivering a fully tested cloud-controller-manager that matches the functionality of the in-tree provider. It enables Kubernetes clusters on OpenStack to use the external cloud-controller-manager, facilitating migration and future maintenance without altering the core Kubernetes codebase.

KEP-1771.title: Versioning Policy for External Cloud Providers
KEP-1771.summary: This KEP standardizes the semantic versioning policy for external (out-of-tree) cloud providers, requiring that their releases track the major and minor version of the Kubernetes control plane they support. By aligning cloud-controller-manager versions with Kubernetes releases, it improves discoverability of supported versions, reduces version skew, and mitigates incompatibility issues.

KEP-5237.title: Watch-based route controller reconciliation
KEP-5237.summary: This KEP switches the route controller in the cloud-controller-manager from a fixed‑interval reconciliation loop to a watch‑based, event‑driven approach using informers. By reconciling on node add/update/delete events and filtering relevant fields, it reduces unnecessary API calls to infrastructure providers and shortens the time to provision routes for new nodes.

KEP-2394.title: Support Out-of-Tree AWS Cloud Provider
KEP-2394.summary: This KEP adds support for an out-of-tree AWS cloud provider by developing, testing, and releasing an AWS cloud-controller-manager that matches the feature set of the in-tree kube-controller-manager. It enables Kubernetes clusters on AWS to run the cloud-controller-manager, improving modularity and maintenance of cloud-specific controller logic.

KEP-2393.title: Cloud Provider Documentation
KEP-2393.summary: This KEP establishes documentation standards for both in-tree and out-of-tree Kubernetes cloud providers, defining required example manifests and up-to-date resource annotation/label listings. By enforcing a consistent documentation format, it improves discoverability and reduces the burden on SIG Docs, benefiting users and operators integrating cloud providers with Kubernetes.

KEP-2395.title: Removing In-Tree Cloud Providers
KEP-2395.summary: This KEP proposes a phased removal of in‑tree cloud provider code from the Kubernetes core repository, moving it to staging and eventually to external provider repositories, and replacing it with out‑of‑tree Cloud Controller Managers. It introduces feature gates to disable in‑tree providers, enabling a more modular and independently versioned cloud provider ecosystem while reducing core binary size and security surface.

KEP-2390.title: Reporting Conformance Test Results to Testgrid
KEP-2390.summary: This KEP describes a process for Kubernetes cloud providers to periodically run E2E conformance tests and upload the results to Testgrid. By standardizing result collection, sig-release can more easily detect critical bugs across providers and improve overall conformance visibility.

KEP-2133.title: Kubelet Credential Providers
KEP-2133.summary: This KEP adds an extensible plugin mechanism to the kubelet that allows dynamic fetching of image registry credentials via exec plugins. By configuring credential provider plugins through a config file and binary directory, kubelet can obtain credentials for any cloud provider without built‑in logic, improving extensibility and reducing vendor lock‑in.

KEP-837.title: Promoting Cloud Provider Labels to GA
KEP-837.summary: This KEP promotes cloud provider specific node and volume labels from their beta (beta.kubernetes.io/…) form to GA label keys (node.kubernetes.io/instance-type, topology.kubernetes.io/zone, topology.kubernetes.io/region). It adds the GA labels alongside the existing beta labels during a transition period, then deprecates and eventually removes the beta labels, improving consistency for scheduling and topology features while preserving compatibility.

KEP-670.title: Support Out-of-Tree vSphere Cloud Provider
KEP-670.summary: This KEP adds support for an out-of-tree vSphere cloud provider by delivering a fully featured cloud-controller-manager that matches the in‑tree functionality. It enables Kubernetes clusters on vSphere to run the external provider while maintaining compatibility with existing in‑tree configurations, facilitating migration and future feature development.

KEP-1179.title: Building Kubernetes Without In-Tree Cloud Providers
KEP-1179.summary: This KEP introduces a build-time option to exclude in‑tree cloud provider code from Kubernetes binaries using a synthetic Go build tag (nolegacyproviders). It enables developers to compile and test Kubernetes without bundled cloud providers, facilitating preparation for their eventual removal and allowing smaller, provider‑less binaries.

KEP-2699.title: Add webhook hosting to CCM.
KEP-2699.summary: This KEP proposes extending the Cloud Controller Manager (CCM) framework to host cloud‑provider‑specific admission webhooks. It adds extension hooks, command‑line flags, and a builder pattern so providers can run mutating webhooks (such as PersistentVolumeLabel) in‑line with API server request handling, simplifying deployment and integration while preserving flexibility to run controllers and webhooks separately.

KEP-671.title: Support Out-of-Tree IBM Cloud Provider
KEP-671.summary: This KEP adds support for an out-of-tree IBM cloud provider by developing, testing, and releasing an IBM-specific cloud-controller-manager that matches the functionality of the built‑in kube‑controller‑manager. It enables Kubernetes clusters on IBM cloud to run the external cloud‑controller‑manager, aligning with the broader move to out‑of‑tree cloud providers.

KEP-2392.title: Cloud Controller Manager
KEP-2392.summary: This KEP defines the architectural changes to split the controller manager into a cloud‑independent kube‑controller‑manager and a separate Cloud Controller Manager (CCM). It moves all cloud‑provider‑specific controller loops out of core components (controller manager, kubelet, API server) so cloud provider code can reside out‑of‑tree while preserving feature parity.

KEP-2214.title: Indexed Job
KEP-2214.summary: The Indexed Job KEP adds a CompletionMode field to Job spec, enabling jobs with a fixed number of completions to assign each pod a unique ordered index. This index is exposed via an annotation and environment variable, allowing pods to have stable hostnames and communicate via headless Services, simplifying embarrassingly parallel workloads.

KEP-3939.title: Allow Replacement of Pods in a Job when fully terminating
KEP-3939.summary: This KEP adds an optional Job API field to control whether replacement Pods are created only after previous Pods have fully terminated, rather than when they are merely marked for deletion. It also adds a status field to track the number of terminating Pods, giving users and queueing controllers better visibility and resource management.

KEP-3998.title: Job success/completion policy
KEP-3998.summary: This KEP extends the Job API with a SuccessPolicy field that lets Indexed Jobs be declared succeeded based on custom criteria such as specific succeeded indexes or a minimum count of succeeded indexes. When a rule is satisfied, a new SuccessCriteriaMet condition is added and any lingering pods are terminated. The change enables workloads like MPI or PyTorch to consider only a subset of pod successes when determining overall job success.

KEP-1591.title: Allow DaemonSets to surge during update like Deployments
KEP-1591.summary: This KEP adds a MaxSurge field to DaemonSet RollingUpdate strategy, allowing DaemonSets to create surge pods during updates similar to Deployments. The feature enables zero‑downtime upgrades for node‑level components such as CNI, CSI, and other per‑node integrations, improving availability during rollouts.

KEP-3329.title: Retriable and non-retriable Pod failures for Jobs
KEP-3329.summary: This KEP adds a policy to Kubernetes Jobs that distinguishes between retriable (infrastructure) and non-retriable (software bug) Pod failures. It introduces new Pod and Job conditions as well as JobSpec fields so that infra‑related failures do not count toward backoffLimit, while failures deemed non‑retriable can terminate the Job early, saving compute resources.

KEP-3335.title: StatefulSet Slice
KEP-3335.summary: This KEP introduces the ability for a StatefulSet to start its pod ordinals at an arbitrary number, enabling the creation of StatefulSet slices. By allowing the first ordinal to be set via a new field, operators can migrate StatefulSets across namespaces or clusters without downtime, supporting gradual migration and scaling of subsets of replicas.

KEP-3973.title: Consider Terminating Pods in Deployments
KEP-3973.summary: This KEP adds a new .spec.podReplacementPolicy field to Deployments, allowing users to control how terminating pods are handled during rollouts and scaling—either waiting for termination to complete or creating new pods immediately. It also introduces status fields to track terminating replicas in Deployments and ReplicaSets, improving resource accounting and predictability.

KEP-961.title: Implement maxUnavailable for StatefulSets
KEP-961.summary: This KEP adds a `maxUnavailable` field to the StatefulSet RollingUpdate strategy, allowing more than one pod to be updated concurrently during a rollout. The feature enables faster rollouts for stateful applications that can tolerate multiple pods being down while preserving the existing one‑pod‑at‑a‑time behavior as the default.

KEP-2185.title: Random Pod Selection on ReplicaSet Downscale
KEP-2185.summary: This KEP introduces a randomized pod victim selection algorithm for ReplicaSet downscaling, using a logarithmic scale of pod age to break the existing bias toward deleting the newest pods. The change aims to improve high‑availability by reducing imbalance across failure domains while still preferring newer pods when possible.

KEP-2879.title: Track ready Pods in Job status
KEP-2879.summary: This KEP adds a new `status.ready` field to the Job API that counts the number of Job Pods whose Ready condition is true. The field gives users and controllers a more accurate view of Job progress by distinguishing ready pods from those only pending or running, reducing the need to watch individual Pod updates.

KEP-85.title: Graduate PodDisruptionBudget to stable
KEP-85.summary: This KEP proposes graduating the PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) API to GA (stable) and promotes the Eviction subresource to policy/v1. It also introduces mutable PDB fields, adds status conditions, fixes empty selector semantics, and improves the disruption controller’s scalability and handling of non‑ready pods, providing a more reliable and long‑term‑supported API for workload availability.

KEP-3017.title: Pod Healthy Policy for PDB
KEP-3017.summary: This KEP adds a new field `unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` to the PodDisruptionBudget API, allowing users to control how pods that are Running but not Ready are treated during eviction. It enables either preserving availability by only evicting such pods when the budget is healthy, or always allowing eviction to avoid deadlocks and aid node drain and autoscaling.

KEP-981.title: pdb-support-for-custom-resources-with-scale-subresource
KEP-981.summary: This KEP extends the Pod Disruption Budget (PDB) controller to use the generic scale subresource, enabling PDB support for any custom resource that implements the scale subresource. By falling back to the scale endpoint when a controller is not one of the built‑in workloads, it allows custom controllers/operators to benefit from PDBs without changing existing APIs.

KEP-706.title: Portable Service Definitions
KEP-706.summary: Portable Service Definitions introduce a set of custom resources and a standardized secret schema that allow applications to declaratively request external services (e.g., databases, DNS, SMTP) in a cloud‑agnostic way. By using the same Kubernetes objects across environments, the proposal improves workload portability and simplifies service discovery and credential management.

KEP-2255.title: ReplicaSet Pod Deletion Cost
KEP-2255.summary: Introduces the pod-deletion-cost annotation (controller.kubernetes.io/pod-deletion-cost) that allows applications to hint the ReplicaSet controller about which pods should be deleted first during scale‑down. By exposing a cost value, controllers can prioritize pod eviction based on custom criteria such as utilization or node cost, improving control over scaling behavior without guaranteeing deletion order.

KEP-592.title: TTL After Finished
KEP-592.summary: The TTL After Finished KEP introduces a TTL mechanism for finished Jobs (and eventually Pods) that automatically deletes the resource after a user-specified time interval once it reaches a terminal state. This helps prevent accumulation of completed Jobs, reducing etcd load and cluster resource consumption.

KEP-1847.title: Auto delete PVCs created by StatefulSet
KEP-1847.summary: This KEP introduces a PersistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy field in the StatefulSet spec, allowing PVCs created from volumeClaimTemplates to be automatically deleted on StatefulSet deletion or scale‑down based on user‑defined policies. The feature is gated by StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC and defaults to retain, giving users opt‑in control over PVC lifecycle, which simplifies cleanup for short‑lived StatefulSets while preserving data safety.

KEP-5440.title: Mutable Pod Resources for Suspended Jobs
KEP-5440.summary: This KEP proposes to relax update validation on suspended Jobs, allowing the CPU, memory, GPU, and other extended resource requests and limits in the pod template to be mutated while the Job is suspended. This enables higher‑level queue controllers to dynamically optimize resource allocations based on current cluster capacity before unsuspending the Job, improving utilization and scheduling of expensive resources.

KEP-2599.title: minReadySeconds for StatefulSets
KEP-2599.summary: This KEP adds an optional minReadySeconds field to the StatefulSet spec and an AvailableReplicas field to its status. The feature ensures that a StatefulSet pod must remain ready for a configurable period before being considered available, aligning StatefulSet behavior with other workload controllers.

KEP-2804.title: Consolidate Workload controllers life cycle status
KEP-2804.summary: This KEP introduces a unified set of status conditions (Progressing, Complete, Failed, Available, Waiting, Running) across major workload controllers (Deployment, DaemonSet, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet, ReplicationController, Job) to provide consistent lifecycle visibility. It also adds a feature gate (ExtendedWorkloadConditions) and proposes a new .spec.progressDeadlineSeconds field for DaemonSet and StatefulSet to support failure detection.

KEP-4017.title: Pod Index Label
KEP-4017.summary: The Pod Index Label KEP adds a label containing the pod index to pods created by StatefulSets and Indexed Jobs. This enables users to select pods by index, filter metrics and logs, and route traffic to specific pod instances without parsing pod names. The feature is gated by PodIndexLabel and is designed to be non‑disruptive to existing workloads.

KEP-2307.title: Job tracking without lingering Pods
KEP-2307.summary: This KEP introduces a new Job tracking mechanism that uses Pod finalizers instead of relying on lingering completed Pods. It adds a new status field to Jobs to record uncounted terminated Pods, allowing finished Pods to be garbage collected earlier while still accurately tracking Job completions and failures.

KEP-2360.title: Optional Service Environment Variables
KEP-2360.summary: This KEP introduces an optional `enableServiceLinks` boolean field in PodSpec that lets developers disable the automatic injection of service environment variables into Pods. By default the behavior remains unchanged, but pods can opt out to avoid compatibility, performance, or scalability issues caused by large numbers of injected variables.

KEP-3715.title: Elastic Indexed Job
KEP-3715.summary: This KEP makes the `spec.completions` field mutable for Indexed Jobs when it remains equal to `spec.parallelism`, allowing elastic scaling of indexed batch workloads while preserving stable pod identities. This enables use cases like MPI, Ray, and PyTorch training that need dynamic scaling without switching to StatefulSets.

KEP-4368.title: Job API managed-by label
KEP-4368.summary: This KEP introduces a new `managedBy` field in the Job spec that allows an external controller to take exclusive responsibility for synchronizing the Job's status. By delegating control, it enables workloads like MultiKueue to mirror Jobs across clusters and disables the built‑in Job controller when appropriate.

KEP-3850.title: Backoff Limits Per Index For Indexed Jobs
KEP-3850.summary: This KEP adds per-index backoff limits to indexed Jobs, allowing each index to have its own retry count and continue execution despite failures. It introduces new spec fields and status tracking to support independent failure handling and a new FailIndex action in PodFailurePolicy.

KEP-2232.title: Suspend Job
KEP-2232.summary: This KEP adds a `suspend` field to the Job API, allowing users to pause and later resume Jobs. When a Job is suspended, the controller deletes active Pods and refrains from creating new ones until resumed, enabling cost‑saving and job‑queueing use cases.

KEP-19.title: CronJobs (previously ScheduledJobs)
KEP-19.summary: This KEP proposes promoting CronJob to GA by introducing a second‑generation controller that uses informers, workqueues, and multiple workers to improve scalability and performance. It also adds a new status field, .status.lastSuccessfulTime, providing visibility into the most recent successful execution of a CronJob.

KEP-4026.title: Add job creation timestamp to job annotations
KEP-4026.summary: This KEP adds a cronjob-scheduled timestamp annotation to Job objects created by a CronJob, allowing users to see the original scheduled time for each job. The annotation is added by the CronJob controller behind the CronJobCreationAnnotation feature gate, providing visibility without impacting existing workloads.

KEP-4222.title: CBOR Serializer
KEP-4222.summary: The KEP introduces a Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) serializer for Kubernetes API servers and clients, offering an alternative to JSON for request/response bodies and superseding JSON for custom resource storage. By using a self‑describing binary format, it aims to reduce CPU usage and heap allocations during encode/decode operations, especially for custom resources that cannot use Protobuf.

KEP-4443.title: More granular Job failure reasons for PodFailurePolicy
KEP-4443.summary: This KEP adds an optional `name` field to each `PodFailurePolicyRule` in the Job API, defaulting to the rule's index when unset. The rule name is appended to the `JobFailed` condition reason (as `PodFailurePolicy_{ruleName}`), enabling higher‑level controllers like JobSet to distinguish which specific pod failure caused a job failure.

KEP-3140.title: TimeZone support in CronJob
KEP-3140.summary: This KEP introduces a new .spec.timeZone field to the CronJob API, allowing users to specify the time zone for job scheduling. By doing so, it decouples CronJob execution times from the kube‑controller‑manager's host time zone, providing more predictable and portable scheduling across clusters.

KEP-492.title: Graduate Admission Webhooks to GA
KEP-492.summary: This KEP graduates admission webhooks to GA by adding several new configuration fields such as object selectors, scope restriction, timeout and port settings, and a reinvocation policy, improving flexibility, performance, and safety of webhook usage. The changes affect the webhook configuration API and make the feature stable for production use.

KEP-95.title: Graduate CustomResourceDefinitions to GA
KEP-95.summary: This KEP outlines the steps required to graduate CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs) from beta to General Availability (GA). It defines the necessary feature completions, tests, and scalability targets to ensure CRDs meet production quality and are ready for GA deployment.

KEP-1281.title: API Server Network Proxy
KEP-1281.summary: This KEP introduces an extensible API Server Network Proxy system that routes outbound traffic from the Kubernetes API server through configurable egress proxies (konnectivity servers) using NetworkContext. It replaces deprecated SSH tunnels, enabling control plane and cluster network isolation, auditability, and custom proxy implementations.

KEP-2343.title: Automated Storage Version Migration with Storage Version Hash
KEP-2343.summary: This KEP introduces a StorageState custom resource that tracks persisted and current storage version hashes for each API resource, enabling automatic storage version migration when the hash changes in the discovery document. It adds a controller to monitor the discovery document, trigger migrations, and keep StorageState up‑to‑date, simplifying upgrade and rollback workflows for cluster operators.

KEP-598.title: CustomResourceDefinition Conversion Webhook
KEP-598.summary: This KEP introduces support for version conversion of Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) by adding a conversion webhook mechanism. It extends the CRD API to include a conversion section and per-version schema, enabling seamless upgrading, downgrading, and serving of multiple API versions for custom resources.

KEP-5504.title: Comparable Resource Version
KEP-5504.summary: This KEP introduces a comparable integer semantics for Kubernetes resource versions, allowing clients to perform ordering comparisons (greater than, less than) rather than only equality. It adds a helper function in client-go for comparing resource versions, updates documentation, and adds conformance tests to ensure clusters enforce monotonic integer resource versions.

KEP-5589.title: Remove gogo protobuf dependency
KEP-5589.summary: This KEP proposes a multi‑step plan to eliminate both runtime and generation‑time dependencies on the unmaintained gogo/protobuf library from Kubernetes API types, while preserving the existing protobuf serialization behavior. By defining minimal interfaces and adjusting code generation tooling, the change removes gogo references from API modules and enables future updates to protobuf handling without reliance on an abandoned codebase.

KEP-1040.title: Priority and Fairness for API Server Requests
KEP-1040.summary: This KEP replaces the simple max‑in‑flight request handler in the API server with a configurable priority and fairness system that categorizes requests into priority levels and queues, providing overload protection, fairness across tenants and request types, and improved throughput. It introduces new API objects to configure flow control, enabling operators to protect CPU and memory resources while ensuring critical system requests are served promptly.

KEP-2334.title: Graduate Server-side Get and Partial Objects to GA
KEP-2334.summary: This KEP graduates the server‑side columnar formatting (Table) and PartialObjectMetadata APIs from beta to GA by moving them to meta.k8s.io/v1, adding protobuf support, and updating core controllers to use the new types. Graduating these APIs enables stable, efficient metadata retrieval for kubectl and internal controllers, improving performance and removing the need for legacy printers.

KEP-4006.title: Transition from SPDY to Websockets
KEP-4006.summary: This KEP replaces the SPDY/3.1 bi-directional streaming protocol used by kubectl exec, attach, cp, and port-forward with WebSockets for the client-to-API‑Server communication. The change modernizes the streaming stack, improves compatibility with L7 proxies and load‑balancers, and later extends WebSocket streaming from the API Server to Kubelet.

KEP-692.title: Publish CRD OpenAPI
KEP-692.summary: This KEP proposes generating and publishing OpenAPI v3 documentation for CustomResourceDefinitions, allowing client-side validation, schema explanation, and code generation for custom resources. It introduces aggregation of CRD OpenAPI specs via the apiextensions-apiserver and kube-aggregator, with a feature gate to control rollout.

KEP-2342.title: exposing hashed storage versions via the discovery API
KEP-2342.summary: This KEP adds an opaque hash of the storage version to the discovery API by introducing a new `storageVersionHash` field on the `APIResource` type. The hash enables the storage version migrator to detect when objects are stored with an unexpected version and trigger migrations, improving automated storage version management.

KEP-2330.title: Migrating API objects to latest storage version
KEP-2330.summary: This KEP defines a tool and API to migrate stored Kubernetes objects to the latest storage version, preventing clusters from crashing due to outdated persisted data after upgrades. It introduces a StorageVersionMigration CRD that tracks migration intent, progress, and supports automated and manual workflows for built‑in, custom, and aggregated resources.

KEP-2558.title: Publish versioning information in OpenAPI
KEP-2558.summary: This KEP adds a vendor extension (x-kubernetes-api-lifecycle) to the OpenAPI schema to publish field‑level versioning information, including prerelease status, minimum Kubernetes version, and associated feature gate. By parsing structured comment tags on built‑in API fields, the extension enables tooling, documentation, and IDEs to surface lifecycle metadata without changing the API itself.

KEP-2338.title: API gzip compression support
KEP-2338.summary: This KEP graduates transparent gzip compression for large API responses to GA, enabling the apiserver to automatically compress responses >128KB when the client requests it via Accept-Encoding. It reduces bandwidth and latency for clients syncing large amounts of data while preserving performance for small requests.

KEP-3157.title: Allow informers for getting a stream of data instead of chunking
KEP-3157.summary: The WatchList KEP adds a feature gate that enables informers to retrieve list data as a continuous stream of watch events instead of a traditional bulk LIST request. By using a WATCH request with SendInitialEvents=true, memory consumption on the kube‑apiserver becomes constant and predictable, reducing OOM risk and load on etcd while maintaining consistency and backward compatibility.

KEP-4020.title: Unknown Version Interoperability Proxy
KEP-4020.summary: The Unknown Version Interoperability Proxy (Mixed Version Proxy) adds a server-side proxy that routes client requests for built‑in resources to an API server that actually serves those resources during version skew, and merges discovery data from all peer API servers into a cluster‑wide aggregated discovery document. This eliminates 404 errors and incomplete discovery during upgrades or downgrades, ensuring controllers see a consistent view of available resources and can safely proceed.

KEP-3488.title: CEL for Admission Control
KEP-3488.summary: This KEP proposes adding in‑process, customizable admission validation using the Common Expression Language (CEL) as an alternative to external validating admission webhooks. It introduces a native policy framework that enables clusters to enforce policies with lower latency and operational overhead while leveraging CEL type checking and integration with Kubernetes native types.

KEP-4192.title: Move Storage Version Migrator in-tree
KEP-4192.summary: The KEP proposes moving the Storage Version Migrator (SVM) controller and its REST APIs in‑tree into the kube‑controller‑manager, creating a new API group storagemigration.k8s.io with the StorageVersionMigration kind. This enables cluster administrators to trigger storage version migrations (including encryption‑at‑rest rewrites) via a native API without relying on the out‑of‑tree implementation.

KEP-4080.title: Add generic control plane staging repository(ies)
KEP-4080.summary: This KEP proposes creating one or more new generic control plane staging repositories (e.g., k/generic-controlplane) to factor out the generic functionality of kube-apiserver and kube-controller-manager into a reusable library and sample binary. The refactoring aims to improve layering, reduce complexity in k/k, and enable projects to build customized control planes without vendoring the full Kubernetes codebase.

KEP-365.title: Paginated API Lists
KEP-365.summary: This KEP introduces an opt‑in chunking mechanism for LIST API calls, allowing clients to specify a maximum number of results (limit) and receive a continue token to retrieve subsequent partial results. By breaking large list responses into consistent chunks, it reduces server memory usage and lowers tail latency for large clusters.

KEP-2339.title: StorageVersion API for HA API servers
KEP-2339.summary: The StorageVersion API introduces a new internal resource that records the storage versions used by each API server instance in a highly‑available Kubernetes control plane. By exposing this information, external controllers such as the storage migrator can detect when all API servers agree on a common encoding version before performing storage migrations, preventing data corruption during rolling upgrades.

KEP-3156.title: HTTP3
KEP-3156.summary: This KEP proposes adding HTTP/3 support to the Kubernetes control plane by enabling the kube-apiserver to listen on UDP and providing an opt‑in round‑tripper for client-go. It introduces a feature gate and a configuration flag to allow early adoption and feedback while the protocol matures in the Go ecosystem.

KEP-3716.title: Admission Webhook Match Conditions
KEP-3716.summary: This KEP introduces a new `matchConditions` field for ValidatingWebhook and MutatingWebhook configurations, allowing administrators to specify CEL expressions that must evaluate to true for a request to be sent to the webhook. By enabling fine-grained filtering of admission requests, the feature improves webhook reliability, reduces latency, and enhances supportability for managed clusters.

KEP-3352.title: Aggregated Discovery
KEP-3352.summary: Aggregated Discovery introduces a new aggregated discovery document served via the existing /api and /apis endpoints using a new content‑negotiation type. This reduces the number of individual discovery requests clients must make, lowering latency and throttling while providing ETag support for efficient updates.

KEP-1601.title: Context support in k8s.io/client-go
KEP-1601.summary: This KEP proposes a refactoring of k8s.io/client-go to add support for Go context propagation on all clientset API calls, enabling request timeout, cancellation, and distributed tracing. It also cleans up inconsistent option passing in the clientset's public API, making method signatures more consistent and idiomatic.

KEP-4358.title: Custom Resource Field Selectors
KEP-4358.summary: This KEP introduces a selectableFields allow list in CustomResourceDefinitions, enabling field selector filtering on custom resources. It allows extension authors to expose specific spec or status fields for efficient querying without resorting to labels.

KEP-555.title: Apply
KEP-555.summary: This KEP moves the kubectl apply functionality into the control plane as Server-Side Apply, introducing a field manager that tracks owners for each field and eliminating the client‑side last‑applied‑configuration annotation. It also adds API extensions for list/map semantics, status‑wiping handling, and an audit policy option to omit managed fields from logs.

KEP-1872.title: Manifest based registration of Admission webhooks
KEP-1872.summary: This KEP introduces manifest‑based registration of admission webhooks, allowing webhooks to be loaded from a file specified in the AdmissionConfiguration at kube‑apiserver startup. By doing so it eliminates the enforcement gap between apiserver start and the creation of MutatingWebhookConfiguration/ValidatingWebhookConfiguration objects and protects these registrations from alteration via normal API requests.

KEP-2337.title: k8s.io Group Protection
KEP-2337.summary: This KEP introduces a required `api-approved.kubernetes.io` annotation on CustomResourceDefinitions that use reserved API groups (k8s.io or kubernetes.io). The annotation links to the approval PR and drives a new `KubeAPIApproved` condition, preventing accidental creation of unapproved APIs in community‑owned groups.

KEP-1164.title: Deprecate and remove SelfLink
KEP-1164.summary: This KEP proposes deprecating and ultimately removing the `selfLink` field from `ObjectMeta` and `ListMeta` in all Kubernetes API objects. Removing the field eliminates a performance overhead and simplifies the generic apiserver processing pipeline.

KEP-4153.title: Declarative Validation
KEP-4153.summary: This KEP proposes a declarative approach for defining validation rules for Kubernetes native API types by using IDL tags in Go type definitions. The rules are expressed via JSON Schema, CEL, and merge strategies, and are incorporated into the OpenAPI v3 schema, enabling the kube-apiserver to enforce validation and allowing tools to consume the validation specifications. The change aims to simplify development, maintenance, and tooling around API validation without introducing new API fields.

KEP-4988.title: Snapshottable API server cache
KEP-4988.summary: This KEP enhances the kube-apiserver watch cache by adding B‑tree snapshotting so that LIST requests for historical resourceVersions can be served directly from the cache instead of etcd, reducing memory pressure and improving performance. It also introduces cache compaction aligned with etcd compaction and a DetectCacheInconsistency feature gate that periodically checks cache‑etcd consistency and falls back to etcd on mismatches.

KEP-2155.title: Client-go Apply
KEP-2155.summary: This KEP adds a typesafe, programmatic way to perform server-side Apply using client-go's typed client. It introduces generated apply configuration builder types and Apply functions, along with ApplyOptions, enabling developers to construct apply requests in pure Go without hand‑crafting JSON/YAML.

KEP-1295.title: Insecure Backend Proxy
KEP-1295.summary: This KEP introduces an option to bypass TLS verification when the kube-apiserver proxies log requests to a kubelet with an expired serving certificate. By adding a boolean field InsecureSkipTLSVerifyBackend to PodLogOptions (exposed via a feature gate AllowInsecureBackendProxy and a kubectl flag), cluster admins can retrieve pod logs for debugging self‑hosted clusters while acknowledging the security trade‑off.

KEP-5000.title: API Linting and CRD Schema Change Tooling
KEP-5000.summary: KEP-5000 proposes two new sig‑api‑machinery subprojects: a golangci‑lint plugin (kube‑api‑linter) that checks Go type definitions for adherence to Kubernetes API conventions, and a CLI tool (crdify) that validates changes to CustomResourceDefinition schemas to detect breaking changes, with optional admission controller support. These tools aim to improve the developer experience for both built‑in API development and CRD authoring by providing static analysis and schema transition checks.

KEP-2523.title: consistent-resource-version-semantics
KEP-2523.summary: This KEP introduces a `ResourceVersionMatch` query parameter to ListOptions, allowing callers to specify whether a list request should use “NotOlderThan” or “Exact” semantics for the supplied resourceVersion. The change makes resource version behavior consistent across paginated and non‑paginated list calls, improving predictability and enabling more efficient reads.

KEP-5647.title: Stale Controller Handling
KEP-5647.summary: This KEP proposes a mechanism for Kubernetes controllers to detect when their local cache is stale and to pause reconciliation until the cache catches up, improving consistency and preventing actions based on outdated data. It adds a Bookmark event to informers, exposes resource versions to controllers, and provides an opt‑in feature gate (StaleControllerConsistency) for selective adoption.

KEP-2336.title: OwnerReference Resource Field
KEP-2336.summary: This KEP adds an optional `resource` field to OwnerReference objects, allowing direct specification of the resource name and eliminating the need for expensive discovery lookups to map a kind to a resource. The change improves the efficiency, reliability, and predictability of garbage collection and other components that rely on OwnerReferences while remaining backward compatible.

KEP-2161.title: Immutable label selectors for all namespaces
KEP-2161.summary: This KEP proposes that the API server automatically adds an immutable label "kubernetes.io/metadata.name" to every Namespace, matching its name. The default label enables users to select namespaces by name using standard label selectors in resources such as NetworkPolicy and webhook configurations without needing write permission to add custom labels.

KEP-2333.title: legacyflags
KEP-2333.summary: The KEP introduces a new legacyflags package that wraps the pflag library to simplify flag registration, parsing, and application for core Kubernetes components. It enables safe migration to versioned ComponentConfig by enforcing flag precedence and preventing unwanted third‑party flag registration, reducing complexity and maintenance overhead.

KEP-5366.title: Graceful Leader Transition
KEP-5366.summary: This KEP introduces a graceful leader transition for key HA components (kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, cloud-controller-manager) by modifying the leader election callback to avoid process exit on lease loss. The change, gated by GracefulLeaderTransition, allows components to cleanly release resources and become followers without a full restart, improving latency and resource usage.

KEP-5073.title: Declarative Validation
KEP-5073.summary: This KEP introduces declarative validation for Kubernetes native API types by allowing developers to specify validation rules directly in the Go type definitions using IDL tags. A new tool, validation-gen, generates the corresponding validation code, and feature gates control the rollout of this new validation mechanism.

KEP-4008.title: CRD Validation Ratcheting
KEP-4008.summary: This KEP introduces CRD Validation Ratcheting, a feature that permits updates to custom resources to succeed when validation errors only affect unchanged fields, effectively allowing validation logic to be tightened or widened without breaking existing objects. By shifting validation enforcement from controllers to the API server and handling schema changes safely, it improves the usability and upgrade experience for CRD authors and Kubernetes developers.

KEP-2335.title: Vanilla CRD OpenAPI Subset: Structural Schemas
KEP-2335.summary: This KEP introduces a restricted subset of OpenAPI v3 called structural schemas for CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs). By enforcing structural schema constraints, it enables advanced CRD features such as server‑side pruning, defaulting, server‑side apply, read‑only fields, and future protobuf support while retaining sufficient expressivity for Kubernetes‑like APIs.

KEP-1693.title: Warning mechanism for use of deprecated APIs
KEP-1693.summary: This KEP introduces a warning mechanism that surfaces deprecation notices to API clients via HTTP Warning headers, enabling users to see informative messages when using deprecated APIs. It also provides cluster administrators with metrics and audit annotations to detect and investigate deprecated API usage, and extends support for custom resource definitions and admission webhooks to contribute warnings.

KEP-2885.title: Server Side Unknown Field Validation
KEP-2885.summary: The Server Side Unknown Field Validation KEP introduces a feature gate that allows the API server to reject create, update, and patch requests containing fields not defined in the object's schema. By adding an opt‑in query parameter and adjusting kubectl's --validate flag, it moves unknown‑field validation from the client to the server, improving consistency and reducing client‑side maintenance.

KEP-3962.title: Mutating Admission Policies
