KEP-3962.summary: Mutating Admission Policies introduce a new API allowing users to declare mutations using CEL expressions, replacing many mutating admission webhook use cases. The API defines MutatingAdmissionPolicy and MutatingAdmissionPolicyBinding resources, supporting JSON Patch or Server Side Apply style mutations that are merged in‑process by the API server.

KEP-4595.title: CEL for CRD AdditionalPrinterColumns
KEP-4595.summary: This KEP adds support for defining additional printer columns in CustomResourceDefinitions using CEL expressions instead of only JSONPath. By introducing a new mutually exclusive field `expression` in the `additionalPrinterColumns` definition, users can compute and format column values with greater flexibility, enabling array handling, conditionals, and complex string formatting in `kubectl get` output.

KEP-1929.title: Built-in declarative defaults
KEP-1929.summary: This KEP proposes adding a new `// +default` marker to built-in Kubernetes API Go structs, enabling declarative default values that are reflected in OpenAPI schemas and shared with CRD defaulting. By aligning built-in and CRD default mechanisms, it simplifies type authoring, reduces errors, and improves consistency across the API surface.

KEP-4460.title: Enable per-request Read/Write Deadline
KEP-4460.summary: This KEP introduces a feature gate (PerHandlerReadWriteTimeout) that enables per-request read and write deadlines in the kube-apiserver using Go's net/http ResponseController. By applying request-scoped deadlines and removing the existing timeout filter, it aims to eliminate data race conditions and simplify request handling while preserving observability and error handling.

KEP-2332.title: Pruning for Custom Resources
KEP-2332.summary: This KEP introduces pruning of unknown fields in CustomResources based on the OpenAPI validation schemas defined in CustomResourceDefinitions. By making pruning opt‑in via the preserveUnknownFields flag (default false in v1), it improves data consistency, security, and aligns CRD behavior with native Kubernetes resources.

KEP-576.title: Dry-run
KEP-576.summary: The Dry-run KEP introduces a server‑side dry‑run mode for modifying API requests, allowing clients to validate and see the result of a request without persisting any changes. It adds a dryRun query parameter, updates admission controller handling, storage behavior, and kubectl flag semantics to support this feature, improving safety for declarative workflows and tooling.

KEP-3037.title: Alternative Services
KEP-3037.summary: This KEP proposes extending client-go to support HTTP Alternative Services (Alt‑Svc) and a configurable list of alternative API server endpoints, enabling Kubernetes components to discover and connect to multiple control‑plane nodes without requiring external load balancers or Service resources. By making the feature opt‑in and leveraging HTTP/2 and TLS, clusters can achieve higher resilience and simpler HA bootstrapping.

KEP-1027.title: Union types
KEP-1027.summary: This KEP introduces a standardized mechanism for defining union (oneOf) fields in Kubernetes API objects using a discriminator field and Go markers. The approach provides automatic validation and normalization of union members, improving client‑server semantics and handling of version skew across API versions.

KEP-2887.title: OpenAPI Enum Types
KEP-2887.summary: The KEP introduces a `+enum` marker for Go type aliases that represent enumeration types, allowing the OpenAPI generator to automatically include enum values in the generated schema. This improves API documentation, validation, and tooling by providing explicit enum information rather than plain strings.

KEP-5116.title: Streaming JSON Encoding for LIST Responses
KEP-5116.summary: This KEP introduces streaming JSON and Protocol Buffer encoders for list (collection) responses in the Kubernetes API server, reducing memory consumption by avoiding full response buffering. By encoding items individually and streaming them to the client, the API server can handle large LIST requests more efficiently, improving scalability and cost-efficiency.

KEP-4568.title: Resilient watchcache initialization
KEP-4568.summary: This KEP introduces mechanisms to make kube-apiserver watchcache initialization more resilient by reducing request load, rejecting hanging watch and list requests with HTTP 429, and delegating get and certain list requests directly to etcd. These changes prevent overload and potential control‑plane outages during watchcache startup or reinitialization.

KEP-2876.title: CRD Validation Expression Language
KEP-2876.summary: This KEP introduces an inline expression language based on the Common Expression Language (CEL) to CustomResourceDefinitions, allowing developers to define validation rules directly within the CRD schema via the new x-kubernetes-validations extension. By integrating CEL, CRDs become more self‑contained and declarative, reducing the need for external admission webhooks for many validation use cases while providing compile‑time type checking and safety.

KEP-1623.title: Standardize Conditions
KEP-1623.summary: This KEP introduces a standardized Condition type in k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1 to provide a common schema for .status.conditions across new Kubernetes APIs. It also adds utility methods and recommended defaulting functions to simplify handling of conditions for API authors and consumers.

KEP-2896.title: OpenAPI V3
KEP-2896.summary: This KEP introduces a new /openapi/v3 endpoint that serves OpenAPI v3 specifications for Kubernetes types, providing a lossless representation of schemas and improving transparency compared to the existing OpenAPI v2 endpoint. It also splits the schema per group‑version with etag support to reduce aggregation overhead and enable efficient client caching.

KEP-1152.title: Less object serializations
KEP-1152.summary: This KEP introduces an internal caching mechanism for object serializations in the kube-apiserver to reduce redundant encoding work for multiple watchers and GET/LIST requests. By adding a CacheableObject interface and extending the Encoder with an Identifier, the apiserver can cache and reuse serialized representations, lowering CPU usage and memory allocations, thereby improving scalability and performance.

KEP-1965.title: kube-apiserver identity
KEP-1965.summary: This KEP introduces a mechanism for each kube-apiserver in a HA cluster to publish a unique identity via a Lease object in the kube-system namespace. Controllers can then discover and track live apiserver instances, enabling features like storage version garbage collection and API priority fairness to function correctly even behind load balancers.

KEP-4420.title: Retry Generate Name
KEP-4420.summary: This KEP adds automatic retry logic in the kube‑apiserver for Create requests that use .metadata.generateName and encounter a name conflict. The API server will regenerate a name and retry up to a configurable number of attempts (default 7), reducing the probability of generateName collisions for large numbers of resources and improving reliability without altering the API surface.

KEP-1904.title: Efficient watch resumption after kube-apiserver reboot
KEP-1904.summary: This KEP introduces a mechanism to efficiently resume watches after a kube-apiserver restart by leveraging etcd's progress notify (bookmarks) feature. It updates the watch cache resource version via bookmark events, reducing costly relists during upgrades and preventing watch cache version drift across apiserver instances.

KEP-956.title: Watch Bookmark
KEP-956.summary: The KEP introduces a new watch event type called Bookmark and a boolean option AllowWatchBookmarks in ListOptions, allowing the API server to inform watchers that all events up to a certain resourceVersion have been processed. This reduces unnecessary reprocessing of events after a watch restart, lowering apiserver load and decreasing "resource version too old" errors.

KEP-5080.title: Ordered Namespace Deletion
KEP-5080.summary: This KEP introduces an opinionated, deterministic deletion order for resources within a namespace, ensuring that pods are deleted before other resources such as NetworkPolicies. By enabling the OrderedNamespaceDeletion feature gate, the proposal improves security and predictability during namespace cleanup without changing existing APIs.

KEP-2340.title: Consistent Reads from Cache
KEP-2340.summary: This KEP adds a mechanism for the API server to serve consistent Get and List reads from the watch cache instead of directly from etcd, while preserving the quorum read consistency guarantees. It does so by first performing a quorum read to obtain the latest revision, then ensuring the watch cache has caught up using etcd progress notifications, allowing most reads to be satisfied from cache and addressing the stale read problem.

KEP-4346.title: Add Informer Metrics
KEP-4346.summary: This KEP introduces optional Prometheus metrics for client-go informers, exposing internal reflector, queue, and event handler statistics such as pending notifications, queue size, and processing durations. The metrics help developers and reliability engineers monitor informer health and diagnose performance issues without needing extensive logging.

KEP-2341.title: Enabling clients to tell if resource endpoints serve the same set of objects
KEP-2341.summary: This KEP proposes adding an opaque `ResourceID` field to the discovery API's `APIResource` type so that clients can determine whether different resource endpoints (e.g., across groups or versions) serve the same underlying objects. By exposing a stable identifier, clients can improve correctness (e.g., quota and webhook enforcement) and efficiency (e.g., avoiding duplicate migrations).

KEP-1101.title: Immutable Fields
KEP-1101.summary: This KEP introduces a declarative way to mark API fields as immutable by adding OpenAPI vendor extensions (x-kubernetes-immutable and x-kubernetes-immutable-keys) and a corresponding Go marker (+immutable). It enables built‑in immutability validation for both core types and CustomResourceDefinitions, publishing the immutability information via the OpenAPI schema and reducing the need for custom admission webhooks.

KEP-3386.title: Kubelet Evented PLEG for Better Performance
KEP-3386.summary: The KEP introduces an Evented Pod Lifecycle Event Generator (PLEG) for the Kubelet, enabled via the EventedPLEG feature gate. It replaces frequent polling of container runtimes with a gRPC server‑streaming event API, allowing the Kubelet to react to container state changes in real time. This reduces steady‑state CPU usage and improves scalability of the Kubelet and CRI implementations.

KEP-2862.title: Fine grained Kubelet API authorization
KEP-2862.summary: This KEP introduces fine‑grained authorization subresources for the Kubelet API, adding dedicated subresources for the configz, healthz, and pods endpoints. By separating these from the existing coarse‑grained `proxy` subresource, node monitoring and logging agents can operate with least‑privilege RBAC permissions, improving cluster security.

KEP-4176.title: New CPUManager Static Policy which spread hyperthreads across physical CPUs to better utilize CPU Cache
KEP-4176.summary: This KEP proposes a new static CPU Manager policy option, `distribute-cpus-across-cores`, which prefers allocating CPUs from different physical cores on the same socket rather than packing hyperthreads together. The policy aims to improve application performance by better utilizing L2 cache and reducing self‑noisy‑neighbor effects, and is gated by the CPUManagerPolicyAlphaOptions feature gate.

KEP-575.title: Defaulting for Custom Resources
KEP-575.summary: This KEP adds support for default values in CustomResource definitions by allowing the `default` keyword in OpenAPI v3 validation schemas. The defaults are applied during deserialization, matching native Kubernetes API behavior, eliminating the need for mutating admission webhooks and improving API consistency.

KEP-1029.title: Quotas for Ephemeral Storage
KEP-1029.summary: This KEP introduces the use of filesystem project quotas to monitor (and optionally enforce) local ephemeral storage usage for pods, improving the speed and reliability of storage consumption metrics. By leveraging XFS and ext4 project quotas in a non‑enforcing mode, kubelet can more accurately detect hidden disk usage and reduce latency compared to the current du/find based scanning approach.

KEP-1287.title: In-place Update of Pod Resources
KEP-1287.summary: The KEP introduces in‑place update of Pod resources through a new /resize subresource, allowing CPU and memory requests and limits to be changed without restarting the Pod. It adds status fields to report actual and allocated resources and a ResizePolicy to control whether a container must be restarted on resize, extending CRI APIs to support these operations across runtimes.

KEP-589.title: Efficient Node Heartbeat
KEP-589.summary: This KEP introduces a built-in Lease API in the coordination.k8s.io group to serve as a lightweight node heartbeat mechanism, reducing the size and write load of Node objects in etcd. By having Kubelet update a Lease object independently of the full NodeStatus, cluster scalability and performance are improved, especially in large clusters.

KEP-4216.title: Image pull per runtime class
KEP-4216.summary: This KEP proposes extending the CRI ImageSpec with an optional runtime class field, allowing images to be pulled per runtime class. This enables different runtime classes (e.g., Windows process vs hyperV isolation) to select appropriate image manifests from multi-arch indexes, supporting scenarios where the host OS version differs from the container's required OS version.

KEP-4817.title: Resource Claim Status With Possible Standardized Network Interface Data
KEP-4817.summary: This KEP extends the ResourceClaim API by adding a new `devices` field to `ResourceClaim.Status`, allowing DRA drivers to report per‑device status and driver‑specific data, including standardized network device information such as interface name, IP addresses, and MAC address. The added visibility improves observability, troubleshooting, and enables new use‑cases like integrating network device data with higher‑level network services.

KEP-757.title: Pid Limiting
KEP-757.summary: This KEP proposes adding support for PID resource isolation in Kubernetes by introducing feature gates that enable pod-to-pod and node-to-pod PID limiting. It leverages cgroup enforcement and node allocatable calculations to prevent PID exhaustion caused by rogue pods, improving node stability and workload isolation.

KEP-3673.title: Kubelet limit of Parallel Image Pulls
KEP-3673.summary: This KEP adds a node-level limit on the number of concurrent image pulls by introducing a new `maxParallelImagePulls` field to the Kubelet configuration. It allows operators to control disk I/O and network bandwidth consumption during pod startup, improving cluster stability and performance.

KEP-2413.title: Seccomp by default
KEP-2413.summary: This KEP proposes enabling seccomp profiles by default for all workloads through a new feature gate (SeccompDefault) and kubelet configuration flag. When enabled, pods and containers will automatically receive the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile, improving cluster security without requiring explicit configuration from users.

KEP-166.title: Promote Taint Based Evictions to GA
KEP-166.summary: This KEP promotes the Taint Based Evictions feature, which automatically applies NoExecute taints to nodes that become NotReady or unreachable, from beta to GA and enables it by default. By making this behavior generally available, the scheduler can consistently evict pods from unhealthy nodes, improving cluster reliability and operational simplicity.

KEP-5419.title: In-Place Pod-Level Resources Resize
KEP-5419.summary: This KEP extends the existing In-Place Pod Resize capability to support dynamic adjustments of pod-level CPU and memory resources introduced by pod-level resource specifications. It enables clusters to resize aggregate pod resources without recreating the pod, improving resource utilization and operational efficiency.

KEP-4009.title: Add CDI devices to device plugin API
KEP-4009.summary: This KEP extends the Device Plugin API by adding a repeated CDIDevice field to the ContainerAllocateResponse, allowing device plugins to specify fully‑qualified CDI device names. The CDI device IDs are then forwarded through the CRI to container runtimes, eliminating the need for annotation work‑arounds and enabling standardized device injection via CDI.

KEP-3857.title: Recursive read-only mounts
KEP-3857.summary: Adds support for recursive read‑only (RRO) mounts, enabling a volume mounted as read‑only to also enforce read‑only on all its submounts. This is achieved via a new VolumeMount field that leverages the OCI runtime "rro" bind‑mount option and kernel mount_setattr support.

KEP-4188.title: New kubelet gRPC API with endpoint returning local pods information
KEP-4188.summary: This KEP introduces a new gRPC API exposed by the Kubelet over a local UNIX socket that returns detailed Pod information, including the full PodSpec and status, for pods running on the node. It improves reliability, scalability, and flexibility for node-local workloads by allowing them to obtain pod state directly from the Kubelet without contacting the Kubernetes API server, while restricting access to privileged local users.

KEP-495.title: Shared PID Namespace
KEP-495.summary: This KEP introduces a new boolean field `shareProcessNamespace` in the PodSpec that allows all containers in a pod to share a single PID namespace when set to true. It also extends the CRI to support explicit PID namespace modes (Container, Pod, Node, and Target), adds a feature gate, and deprecates the existing kubelet flag for Docker shared PID handling.

KEP-2411.title: CRI Container Log Rotation
KEP-2411.summary: This KEP graduates the CRIContainerLogRotation feature gate from Beta to Stable, making kubelet the component responsible for managing and rotating container logs for CRI-compliant runtimes. It introduces configurable flags for maximum log file size and retention count, enabling reliable log management and easier integration with logging agents.

KEP-753.title: Sidecar Containers
KEP-753.summary: Sidecar containers introduce a new container type that starts alongside init containers, runs for the entire Pod lifetime, and does not block Pod termination. Kubelet will keep sidecars alive, improving patterns like job sidecars, log forwarding, metrics, and service meshes.

KEP-4205.title: Expose PSI Metrics
KEP-4205.summary: This KEP adds support in the kubelet to read Pressure Stall Information (PSI) metrics for CPU, memory, and I/O from cgroup v2 via cAdvisor and runc, and exposes them in the kubelet Summary API and metrics endpoints. Exposing PSI enables nodes to detect and react to resource pressure more proactively, improving observability and node condition handling.

KEP-4381.title: DRA Structured Parameters
KEP-4381.summary: This KEP introduces a new API for Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) with structured parameters, enabling pods to request specialized hardware devices such as GPUs, FPGAs, or network‑attached accelerators. It adds support for device sharing, partial allocation, optional allocation, and custom configuration parameters, allowing vendors to publish device information via ResourceSlice objects and the scheduler to allocate them via ResourceClaims.

KEP-2570.title: Memory QoS
KEP-2570.summary: This KEP adds memory quality‑of‑service (QoS) support by leveraging cgroups v2 memory controller knobs. It maps pod/container memory requests to memory.min, limits to memory.max, and introduces a memory.high throttle for containers, providing better memory isolation and guarantees for pods, containers, and node resources.

KEP-1769.title: Memory Manager
KEP-1769.summary: The Memory Manager is a new kubelet component that provides guaranteed memory and hugepage allocation for Guaranteed QoS pods, supporting both single‑NUMA and multi‑NUMA strategies. It generates NUMA affinity hints for the Topology Manager, ensuring memory is allocated from the minimum number of NUMA nodes and aligning memory with other resources for performance‑critical workloads.

KEP-2129.title: Disable cAdvisor json Metrics
KEP-2129.summary: This KEP deprecates and removes the cAdvisor JSON metrics endpoints from the kubelet, eliminating the container and machine info JSON APIs. By removing these rarely used, Linux‑only endpoints, the kubelet reduces maintenance overhead and aligns with the long‑term goal of discarding cAdvisor APIs in favor of alternative metrics sources.

KEP-4800.title: Split UnCoreCache Toplogy Awareness in CPU Manager
KEP-4800.summary: This KEP adds a new static CPU Manager policy option, "prefer-align-cpus-by-uncorecache", which attempts to allocate CPUs that share the same uncore cache (last-level cache) to improve performance on processors with split uncore cache architectures. It extends the CPUInfo topology struct with an uncorecacheId field and enables the feature via a policy flag, without altering existing static policies.

KEP-3960.title: Pod lifecycle sleep action
KEP-3960.summary: This KEP adds a new sleep action to the PreStop lifecycle hook, allowing containers to pause for a configurable number of seconds before termination. The feature simplifies graceful shutdowns and enables zero‑downtime updates by giving the Endpoint Controller time to remove terminating pods from service endpoints.

KEP-793.title: Promote Node Operating System & Architecture labels to GA
KEP-793.summary: This KEP promotes the existing beta node operating system and architecture labels (beta.kubernetes.io/os, beta.kubernetes.io/arch) to GA as kubernetes.io/os and kubernetes.io/arch. It introduces a transition period where kubelets emit both beta and GA labels, with the node controller reconciling any mismatches, and eventually removes the beta labels after v1.18.

KEP-693.title: Node Topology Manager
KEP-693.summary: The Node Topology Manager introduces a new kubelet component that coordinates CPU, device, and network resource assignments to respect NUMA topology, providing a two‑phase topology coherence protocol. It collects topology hints from existing managers during pod admission and enforces policies (none, best‑effort, restricted, single‑numa‑node) to improve performance for latency‑critical and high‑throughput workloads.

KEP-213.title: RunAsGroup support in PodSpec and PodSecurityPolicy
KEP-213.summary: This KEP adds a RunAsGroup field to PodSecurityContext, SecurityContext, and PodSecurityPolicy, allowing users to specify the primary group ID for containers and pods. By enabling explicit group IDs, it enhances security isolation and aligns Kubernetes container launch capabilities with Docker's -u option.

KEP-135.title: Seccomp to GA
KEP-135.summary: This KEP upgrades seccomp from an annotation to a dedicated field in the Pod API and marks seccomp as GA. It introduces explicit API objects for seccomp profiles, deprecates the old alpha annotations, and provides a minimal, stable implementation while allowing future enhancements.

KEP-4781.title: Restarting kubelet does not change pod status
KEP-4781.summary: This KEP adds a feature gate, ChangeContainerStatusOnKubeletRestart, that preserves container Started and Ready statuses across kubelet restarts, avoiding the default behavior where all pods are marked NotReady. By retaining the previous pod status, it reduces unnecessary service disruptions while allowing an opt‑in to revert to the old behavior if needed.

KEP-727.title: Kubelet Resource Metrics Endpoint
KEP-727.summary: The KEP proposes a new kubelet endpoint (/metrics/resource) that serves resource metrics in Prometheus text format, providing the minimal metrics required by the cluster-level Resource Metrics API. This dedicated endpoint replaces the dual-purpose Summary API for resource metrics, improving efficiency and reducing CPU/memory overhead for the Metrics Server.

KEP-2033.title: Rootless mode
KEP-2033.summary: This KEP enables running the entire set of Kubernetes node components—including kubelet, kube-proxy, CRI, OCI runtimes, and CNI plugins—inside a non‑root user namespace. By operating in rootless mode, it reduces the attack surface of the node, protecting the host from container‑breakout vulnerabilities and allowing Kubernetes to be deployed on shared or unprivileged environments.

KEP-1884.title: Kubelet endpoint for pod resource assignment
KEP-1884.summary: The KEP introduces a new kubelet gRPC endpoint that exposes pod-to-device assignment information, allowing external agents to list, watch, and query allocatable resources on a node. This provides a standardized way for monitoring, device-aware CNI plugins, and topology-aware scheduling to access device and CPU allocation data, improving observability and decoupling device monitoring from in‑tree kubelet logic.

KEP-3619.title: Fine grained SupplementalGroups control
KEP-3619.summary: This KEP adds a new `SupplementalGroupsPolicy` field to the PodSecurityContext to let users control how supplemental groups are calculated for the first container process, fixing non‑OCI‑compliant behavior and preventing security policy bypasses. It also introduces a `User` object in ContainerStatus and a `NodeFeatures` field in NodeStatus to expose the effective UID, GID, and supplemental groups, providing visibility for administrators.

KEP-1967.title: Size memory backed volumes
KEP-1967.summary: This KEP introduces a feature gate (SizeMemoryBackedVolumes) that allows the kubelet to size memory‑backed emptyDir volumes based on the minimum of node allocatable memory, pod allocatable memory, and any user‑specified size limit. This makes the volume size portable across nodes and aligns it with the pod's actual memory limits, improving predictability for workloads that rely on /dev/shm or other memory‑backed storage.

KEP-4680.title: Add Resource Health Status to the Pod Status for Device Plugin and DRA
KEP-4680.summary: This KEP adds a ResourceHealthStatus feature gate that introduces health information for allocated device resources into Pod status. By exposing per‑resource health (healthy, unhealthy, unknown) via new AllocatedResourcesStatus fields in both ContainerStatus and PodStatus, users and controllers can diagnose device failures and take appropriate remediation actions.

KEP-277.title: Ephemeral Containers
KEP-277.summary: This KEP adds a new EphemeralContainers field to Pod specifications, enabling the creation of temporary containers that run inside an existing pod's namespaces for debugging and troubleshooting. It introduces a dedicated /ephemeralcontainers subresource and associated API changes, allowing users to add, attach to, and view these containers without affecting the pod's primary containers.

KEP-950.title: Add pod-startup liveness-probe holdoff for slow-starting pods
KEP-950.summary: This KEP adds a new startupProbe to the container spec that holds off liveness and readiness probes until a pod has finished starting, preventing slow‑starting containers from being killed prematurely. It also introduces a Started flag in ContainerStatus to track whether the startup probe has succeeded, improving pod lifecycle management.

KEP-2403.title: Extend kubelet pod resource assignment endpoint to return allocatable resources
KEP-2403.summary: This KEP extends the kubelet pod resources gRPC endpoint with a new GetAllocatableResources RPC, allowing consumers to retrieve the allocatable compute resources on a node. It enables node monitoring agents and topology‑aware scheduling components to accurately assess node capacity and utilization.

KEP-1898.title: Hardening exec endpoints against SSRF
KEP-1898.summary: This KEP hardens the exec, attach, and port-forward streaming endpoints against Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks by removing vulnerable GET‑based URL parameters and requiring POST requests with options supplied in the request body. The changes introduce breaking API modifications, including removal of the /run endpoint, UID‑based paths, and addition of a pod reference field to the PodExecOptions type, all gated behind the HardenedExecRequests feature flag.

KEP-127.title: Support User Namespaces
KEP-127.summary: This KEP introduces support for Linux user namespaces in Kubernetes by adding a new pod.spec.hostUsers field that enables pods to run in isolated user namespaces with configurable UID/GID mappings. It enhances node‑to‑pod and pod‑to‑pod isolation, mitigating several high‑severity container escape vulnerabilities.

KEP-5394.title: PSI based Node Conditions
KEP-5394.summary: This KEP introduces the PSINodeCondition feature gate that enables the kubelet to report new node conditions based on Pressure Stall Information (PSI) metrics for memory and I/O. By setting node conditions and corresponding NoSchedule taints when PSI thresholds are exceeded, the system prevents scheduling new pods on nodes under high resource pressure, improving cluster stability and resource management.

KEP-606.title: Kubelet endpoint for device assignment observation details
KEP-606.summary: This KEP adds a node‑local gRPC endpoint served by the kubelet that returns the mapping of devices assigned to pods and containers. By exposing this information, external monitoring agents can associate device usage metrics with the corresponding pod and container, enabling easier observability and decoupling monitoring from device lifecycle management.

KEP-281.title: Dynamic Kubelet Configuration
KEP-281.summary: Dynamic Kubelet Configuration allowed administrators to roll out new Kubelet configurations to live clusters via a dynamic mechanism, simplifying configuration management. The feature was deprecated in v1.22 and removed in later releases due to lack of interest and to improve code reliability.

KEP-1972.title: Kubelet Exec Probe Timeouts
KEP-1972.summary: This KEP introduces the ExecProbeTimeouts feature gate to make kubelet respect the timeout values specified for exec probes, treating timeouts as probe failures. It allows clusters to enable proper timeout handling while preserving existing behavior via a configurable gate.

KEP-24.title: Add AppArmor Support
KEP-24.summary: This KEP adds native AppArmor support to the Kubernetes API by introducing a new AppArmorProfile field in the Pod and container security contexts. It enables users to specify AppArmor confinement profiles for pods and containers, improving security and providing an alternative to SELinux.

KEP-2727.title: Add gRPC probe to Pod.Spec.Container.{Liveness,Readiness,Startup}Probe
KEP-2727.summary: This KEP introduces native gRPC health checking support for containers by adding a new GRPC probe type to Pod.Spec.Container.{liveness,readiness,startup}Probe. It enables the Kubelet to perform health checks over HTTP/2 without requiring users to bundle external binaries, aligning Kubernetes with widespread gRPC usage.

KEP-4639.title: OCI images as VolumeSource
KEP-4639.summary: This KEP introduces a new in‑tree VolumeSource that lets a pod mount an OCI image (or OCI artifact) directly as a filesystem. By using OCI registries for shared data, it reduces container image size, improves security, and simplifies distribution of configuration files, binaries, or model weights across containers.

KEP-34.title: Protomote sysctl annotations to fields
KEP-34.summary: This KEP promotes the usage of sysctl annotations to first‑class API fields, adding a native sysctls list to the Pod securityContext and allowing pod‑level sysctl configuration. It also introduces sysctl support in PodSecurityPolicy and moves the kubelet’s experimental unsafe‑sysctls flag into the KubeletConfiguration API, gating the feature on by default for stability and validation.

KEP-2053.title: Downward API HugePages
KEP-2053.summary: This KEP adds support for exposing hugepages resource requests and limits via the Downward API, allowing pods to discover their hugepage allocations through environment variables or volume files. It introduces a feature gate (DownwardAPIHugePages) to control the API server validation and ensures kubelet support for projecting these values, improving visibility and configurability of hugepage usage in pods.

KEP-585.title: Runtime Class
KEP-585.summary: RuntimeClass introduces a new cluster‑scoped API resource that lets cluster operators expose container runtime properties to the control plane. Pods can select a RuntimeClass via the new spec.runtimeClassName field, which is passed to the CRI as a RuntimeHandler, enabling multiple runtimes (e.g., runc, gvisor, kata) to coexist and be scheduled appropriately.

KEP-5593.title: Configure the max CrashLoopBackOff delay
KEP-5593.summary: This KEP adds a configurable knob for cluster operators to set the maximum CrashLoopBackOff delay on a per-node basis, allowing it to be reduced to as low as 1 second. It also separates the backoff counter reset threshold from the delay, improving pod restart behavior for fast or short-lived workloads.

KEP-4369.title: Allow special characters environment variable
KEP-4369.summary: This KEP introduces a feature gate that relaxes the validation of environment variable names, allowing any printable ASCII character (32-126) except "=". It enables users to set special characters in env var names for Pods, ConfigMaps, and Secrets, improving flexibility for applications that require such naming conventions.

KEP-1797.title: Configure FQDN as Hostname for Pods
KEP-1797.summary: This KEP introduces a new PodSpec boolean field `setHostnameAsFQDN` that, when enabled, configures the Linux kernel hostname inside a pod to its fully qualified domain name (FQDN) instead of the short hostname. It allows legacy applications that rely on the kernel hostname being set to the FQDN to run unchanged within Kubernetes.

KEP-1547.title: Building a Dockerless Kubelet
KEP-1547.summary: This KEP proposes adding a build tag to compile the Kubelet without any Docker-specific code or the docker/docker Go client, enabling a "dockerless" Kubelet binary. The change simplifies the Kubelet's dependency graph, reduces binary size, and prepares the codebase for eventual removal or out-of-tree migration of Docker support.

KEP-4033.title: Discover cgroup driver from CRI
KEP-4033.summary: This enhancement adds the ability for the container runtime to inform kubelet which cgroup driver to use, eliminating the need to configure the cgroup driver separately in the kubelet and preventing mismatched driver configurations. It introduces a RuntimeConfig RPC in the CRI API to convey the driver choice, simplifying node configuration and reducing user errors.

KEP-5328.title: Node Declared Features
KEP-5328.summary: The Node Declared Features KEP adds a DeclaredFeatures field to Node.Status, allowing nodes to advertise which feature-gated Kubernetes features they support. This enables the scheduler and admission controllers to make informed decisions, reducing version skew issues and eliminating manual taints, labels, and tolerations for new feature compatibility.

KEP-2040.title: Kubelet CRI support
KEP-2040.summary: This KEP proposes evolving the Container Runtime Interface (CRI) API through version increments (v1alpha2, v1beta, v1) to mature it to stable, addressing feedback, cleaning up TODOs, and adding missing functionality such as a pinned‑image field for garbage‑collection control. By formalizing the CRI API, Kubernetes signals that CRI‑based runtimes like containerd and CRI‑O are production‑ready and encourages migration away from the deprecated dockershim.

KEP-4265.title: Add ProcMount option
KEP-4265.summary: This KEP introduces a new procMount field in the container securityContext, allowing users to opt out of the default /proc masking performed by container runtimes. By setting procMount to Unmasked, containers can run nested unprivileged containers or build images inside a Kubernetes pod, while remaining subject to privileged PSA controls.

KEP-1539.title: HugePages
KEP-1539.summary: This KEP adds support for pre‑allocated huge pages in Kubernetes, allowing pods to request specific huge page sizes as a resource. The kubelet advertises allocatable huge pages, the scheduler places pods on nodes with sufficient huge pages, and pod containers can consume them via hugetlbfs, shmget, or emptyDir volumes, with proper cgroup enforcement and quota handling.

KEP-5067.title: Pod Generation
KEP-5067.summary: The KEP introduces a pod status field `observedGeneration` and a condition-level `observedGeneration` to let the kubelet indicate which pod spec generation has been observed, while also having the API server increment `metadata.generation` on spec changes. This provides a reliable way for users to know which pod updates have been reflected in the pod status, reducing race conditions and improving status consistency.

KEP-3570.title: CPU Manager
KEP-3570.summary: The CPU Manager adds a new kubelet component that assigns pod containers to specific CPU sets on a node, enabling exclusive CPU allocation and NUMA-aware pinning to improve performance and latency. It introduces new kubelet configuration options and a CRI method to update container resources for enforcing cpuset assignments.

KEP-2221.title: Removing dockershim from kubelet
KEP-2221.summary: This KEP proposes deprecating and ultimately removing the in‑tree Docker shim (dockershim) from the kubelet, making Docker just another external CRI implementation. By decoupling Docker from the kubelet, the maintenance burden is reduced and the platform can focus on generic CRI support and other runtimes.

KEP-2254.title: cgroups v2
KEP-2254.summary: This KEP proposes adding support for Linux cgroups v2 in the Kubernetes Kubelet, allowing nodes to run with either cgroups v1 or v2 and providing parity of functionality. Supporting cgroups v2 is important because the kernel API is now stable, newer kernel features (e.g., PSI) depend on it, and many distributions are moving to cgroups v2 by default, which currently blocks Kubernetes operation.

KEP-4742.title: Node Topologies via Downward API
KEP-4742.summary: This KEP introduces a built‑in admission plugin that copies standard node topology labels (zone, region, hostname) onto Pods, making them accessible via the Downward API. By exposing topology information through Pod labels, workloads can obtain node locality data without custom init containers, improving performance and simplifying topology‑aware applications.

KEP-2625.title: SMT aware cpumanager policy
KEP-2625.summary: The KEP adds a CPUManager policy option `full-pcpus-only` that can be enabled via the new kubelet flag `CPUManagerPolicyOptions`. When enabled, the static CPU manager will only allocate whole physical CPUs, rejecting pods that would cause partial core (SMT) sharing, thereby improving latency predictability and isolation on SMT-enabled nodes.

KEP-2400.title: Node system swap support
KEP-2400.summary: This KEP introduces node-level swap support on Linux by adding a NodeSwap feature gate and a kubelet configuration field (swapBehavior) that can enable swap usage for workloads, initially limited to Burstable QoS pods. It allows administrators to configure node-wide swap utilization while preserving system stability and providing a foundation for future per‑pod swap customizations.

KEP-4569.title: Move cgroup v1 in maintenance mode
KEP-4569.summary: This KEP moves cgroup v1 support in Kubernetes into maintenance mode, encouraging migration to cgroup v2 as the default Linux control group implementation. It introduces a kubelet metric to expose the active cgroup version, emits warnings and events when cgroup v1 is detected, and adds a flag to optionally fail on cgroup v1 usage, while keeping existing cgroup v1 functionality for the foreseeable future.

KEP-4191.title: Split Image Filesystem
KEP-4191.summary: This KEP extends kubelet to understand when a container runtime splits the image filesystem across separate disks, enabling correct garbage collection, eviction, and disk usage reporting. By supporting a configuration where the writable layer shares the node filesystem while images reside on a distinct read‑only filesystem, it improves disk management and performance for clusters with separate storage for images and containers.

KEP-5307.title: Container Restart Policy
KEP-5307.summary: This KEP adds a container-level restartPolicyRules field to the Pod spec, allowing kubelet to restart containers in‑place based on configurable exit‑code conditions even when the Pod restartPolicy is Never. It enables more efficient handling of retriable failures for workloads such as large AI/ML training jobs, reducing costly pod rescheduling.

KEP-3288.title: Split Stdout and Stderr Log Stream of Container
KEP-3288.summary: This KEP introduces a new query parameter and API field `stream` on PodLogOptions, allowing users to request either the stdout, stderr, or combined log streams of a container. It enables kube-apiserver, kubelet, and kubectl to return separate log streams, improving observability for debugging and monitoring.

KEP-5365.title: ImageVolume with an image digest
KEP-5365.summary: This KEP extends the ImageVolume feature by adding an ImageRef field to the pod's status, exposing the digest of the image used for an ImageVolume. The change enables users to monitor, audit, and verify the exact image version used for ImageVolumes, supporting use-cases such as observability, git‑ops workflows, and live migration in Kubevirt.

KEP-3573.title: Device Plugins
KEP-3573.summary: The Device Plugins KEP introduces a vendor‑agnostic gRPC based mechanism that lets hardware vendors (e.g., GPUs, NICs, FPGAs) advertise, health‑check, and allocate devices to pods via the kubelet. This enables consistent, portable access to external devices without requiring per‑vendor code in the core Kubernetes codebase.

KEP-688.title: Pod Overhead
KEP-688.summary: The Pod Overhead KEP introduces a mechanism to account for additional resource consumption imposed by sandbox runtimes, such as Kata containers, by adding an optional Overhead field to PodSpec and RuntimeClass. This enables the scheduler, ResourceQuota, and kubelet to consider runtime-specific overhead in scheduling decisions, quota enforcement, and cgroup sizing.

KEP-1558.title: Cleaning up container streaming requests
KEP-1558.summary: This KEP deprecates and removes the Kubelet flag --redirect-container‑streaming and the feature gates StreamingProxyRedirects and ValidateProxyRedirects, consolidating container streaming (exec, attach, port‑forward) to a single local proxy configuration. The change simplifies configuration, removes reliance on beta features, and reduces the surface for potential SSRF attacks.

KEP-5532.title: Restart All Containers on Container Exits
KEP-5532.summary: This KEP extends the container restart policy API (KEP-5307) by adding a RestartAllContainers action, enabling an in‑place pod restart when a container exits with matching conditions. The kubelet will terminate and restart all containers in the pod while preserving the sandbox, UID, network namespace, and volumes, providing a faster, more efficient alternative to deleting and recreating the pod.

KEP-4210.title: ImageMaximumGCAge in Kubelet
KEP-4210.summary: This KEP introduces a new Kubelet configuration option, ImageMaximumGCAge, that lets cluster administrators define a maximum age after which unused container images are garbage collected, independent of disk usage thresholds. It is gated by the ImageGCMaximumAge feature gate, providing more proactive space management and reducing stale images after upgrades.

KEP-5526.title: Pod-Level Resource Managers
KEP-5526.summary: This KEP extends the Kubelet's Topology, CPU, and Memory managers to understand pod-level resource specifications (pod.spec.resources). By enabling pod-wide NUMA alignment and a partitioning model, it allows mixed-criticality containers within a pod to share a single NUMA-aligned resource pool while providing exclusive allocations for guaranteed containers, improving performance for HPC, AI/ML, and other latency-sensitive workloads.

KEP-4603.title: Tune Crashloop Backoff
KEP-4603.summary: KEP-4603 introduces a tunable CrashLoopBackOff behavior via the ReduceDefaultCrashLoopBackoffDecay feature gate, lowering the default initial backoff to 1 second and the maximum backoff to 1 minute, and adjusting the recovery threshold. This change aims to reduce unnecessary restart delays for containers that exit successfully or have short lifetimes, improving responsiveness for workloads like gaming and AI/ML while maintaining node stability.

KEP-5607.title: Allow HostNetwork Pods to Use User Namespaces
KEP-5607.summary: This KEP adds a new alpha feature gate, UserNamespacesHostNetworkSupport, that relaxes pod validation to allow the combination of hostNetwork:true with user namespaces (hostUsers:false). It enables control‑plane static pods to run with reduced privileges while still using host networking, improving security isolation.

KEP-2902.title: CPUManager Policy Option to Distribute CPUs Across NUMA Nodes Instead of Packing Them
KEP-2902.summary: This KEP adds a new CPUManager policy option `distribute-cpus-across-numa` to the static CPUManager policy, enabling even distribution of allocated CPUs across NUMA nodes instead of packing them onto a single node. It improves performance for parallel applications that benefit from balanced NUMA node usage.

KEP-2000.title: Graceful Node Shutdown
KEP-2000.summary: The Graceful Node Shutdown KEP adds a kubelet configuration that detects node shutdown events and triggers pod termination with a configurable grace period, allowing workloads to shut down cleanly. It uses systemd-logind inhibitor locks via dbus to delay shutdown, improving reliability during power-off or VM stop operations.

KEP-3085.title: Pod networking ready condition
KEP-3085.summary: This KEP introduces a new pod condition, PodReadyToStartContainers, which is set to true when the pod sandbox has been successfully created and the pod is ready for its containers to start. The condition provides a clear observable milestone for operators to monitor sandbox creation latency and improves visibility into multi‑component initialization (CSI, CNI, CRI) in the pod lifecycle.

KEP-2238.title: Liveness Probe Grace Period
KEP-2238.summary: This KEP adds a new field `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` to liveness and startup probes, allowing them to specify a separate grace period that overrides the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds. This enables faster restarts of failing containers without being delayed by a long pod termination grace period, while preserving existing behavior when the field is unset.

KEP-4438.title: Restarting sidecar containers during Pod termination
KEP-4438.summary: This KEP introduces a feature gate, RestartContainerDuringTermination, to allow sidecar containers to be restarted if they exit prematurely during Pod termination. The change ensures sidecars remain running while other containers complete termination, improving reliability of sidecar-dependent workloads.

KEP-3721.title: Support for env files.
KEP-3721.summary: This KEP proposes adding a new EnvVarSource field called fileKeyRef that allows containers to populate environment variables directly from a file stored in an emptyDir volume. It simplifies passing per‑pod configuration or initContainer‑generated values to containers, especially for distroless images that lack a shell.

KEP-2837.title: Pod Level Resource Specifications
KEP-2837.summary: This KEP extends the Pod API to allow users to specify resource requests and limits at the pod level for core resources (CPU, memory, and hugepages). By enabling pod‑level resource specifications, it simplifies resource management for multi‑container pods and improves overall resource utilization by allowing containers to share a common resource pool.

KEP-3327.title: CPUManager policy option to align CPUs by Socket instead of by NUMA node
KEP-3327.summary: This KEP introduces a new CPUManager policy option called `align-by-socket` for the static CPU manager. When enabled, the CPU manager prefers topology hints that are socket‑aligned, allowing the TopologyManager to allocate CPUs within the same socket, which improves performance for latency‑sensitive workloads when NUMA alignment is not possible.

KEP-2371.title: cAdvisor-less, CRI-full Container and Pod Stats
KEP-2371.summary: This KEP extends the CRI API to expose a complete set of container and pod metrics, enabling the Kubelet to populate the /stats/summary and /metrics/cadvisor endpoints without relying on cAdvisor. By moving the metrics collection to the CRI layer, it reduces duplication, clarifies metric origins, and improves performance and observability for Kubernetes clusters.

KEP-4818.title: Allow zero value for Sleep Action of PreStop Hook
KEP-4818.summary: This KEP adds a feature gate (PodLifecycleSleepActionAllowZero) that permits a zero-second duration for the SleepAction in a container's PreStop lifecycle hook. Allowing a zero value enables users to define no-op PreStop hooks for purposes such as admission validation without changing existing behavior.

KEP-2535.title: Ensure Secret Pulled Images
KEP-2535.summary: This KEP introduces kubelet configuration options and a feature gate to ensure that images pulled with authentication credentials are verified before use, even when the image is already present on the node. It adds policies to control when re‑authentication is required for images used with `IfNotPresent` or `Never` pull policies, improving security without forcing always‑pull behavior.

KEP-3545.title: Improved multi-numa alignment in Topology Manager
KEP-3545.summary: This KEP enhances the Kubernetes Topology Manager by adding a policy option to prefer sets of NUMA nodes that are closest to each other when allocating resources. It introduces a new kubelet configuration flag (topology-manager-policy-options) with the option prefer-closest-numa-nodes, allowing existing best‑effort and restricted policies to consider NUMA distance while preserving their other properties.

KEP-4622.title: New TopologyManager Policy which configure the value of maxAllowableNUMANodes
KEP-4622.summary: This KEP introduces a new TopologyManager policy option `max-allowable-numa-nodes` that makes the previously hard‑coded limit of 8 NUMA nodes configurable. It allows clusters with CPUs exposing more than 8 NUMA nodes to enable TopologyManager without crashes, giving operators control over the trade‑off between supported NUMA node count and admission performance.

KEP-1867.title: Disable AcceleratorUsage Metrics
KEP-1867.summary: This KEP deprecates and removes the AcceleratorUsage metrics that Kubelet currently exposes, shifting metric collection to external agents via the PodResources API. A feature gate (DisableAcceleratorUsageMetrics) is introduced to allow users to disable these metrics, reducing resource usage and encouraging migration to the newer API.

KEP-3983.title: Add support for a kubelet drop-in configuration directory
KEP-3983.summary: This KEP adds support for a kubelet drop‑in configuration directory via a new `--config-dir` flag. Users can place multiple `.conf` snippets that are merged in alphanumeric order to build the effective kubelet configuration, simplifying per‑node customization and avoiding configuration races. The feature progresses from an alpha environment variable to a beta flag, eventually becoming enabled by default for easier management of kubelet settings.

KEP-4960.title: Container Stop Signals
KEP-4960.summary: This KEP adds a first‑class StopSignal field to a container's lifecycle in the Pod spec, allowing users to configure which POSIX signal is sent to terminate a container without rebuilding the image. The feature propagates the signal through the CRI to container runtimes and makes the effective signal visible in pod status, with validation against the node OS (Linux or Windows).

KEP-2008.title: Forensic Container Checkpointing
KEP-2008.summary: This KEP adds a new kubelet HTTP endpoint and extends the CRI API with a CheckpointContainer RPC to allow checkpointing of individual containers for forensic analysis. The feature enables operators to capture a running container's state without stopping it, facilitating offline examination of potential security incidents.

KEP-2712.title: Pod Priority Based Graceful Node Shutdown
KEP-2712.summary: This KEP adds a kubelet feature gate to perform graceful node shutdown based on pod priority values, allowing administrators to configure different shutdown grace periods for pods of varying priority. By introducing a new kubelet configuration field, the shutdown order becomes more fine‑grained than the existing critical/regular classification, improving control over pod termination during node shutdown.

KEP-4580.title: Deprecate & remove Kubelet RunOnce mode
KEP-4580.summary: This KEP deprecates and removes the kubelet RunOnce mode, marking the RunOnce field in KubeletConfiguration and the --runonce flag as deprecated before ultimately deleting the flag. The change introduces the LegacyNodeRunOnceMode feature gate to control the deprecation and ensures users migrate to alternative solutions such as podman.

KEP-4540.title: Add CPUManager policy option to restrict reservedSystemCPUs to system daemons and interrupt processing
KEP-4540.summary: This KEP introduces a new CPUManager policy option, `strict-cpu-reservation`, which ensures that CPUs specified in `reservedSystemCPUs` are exclusively used by system daemons and interrupt processing. By removing the reserved cores from the shared pool, burstable and best‑effort pods cannot consume them, improving latency and preventing host services from being starved.

KEP-3063.title: dynamic resource allocation
KEP-3063.summary: The KEP proposes a Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) control plane controller that enables opaque, driver‑managed allocation of ResourceClaims via a PodSchedulingContext object, allowing arbitrary parameters, network‑attached resources, and custom matching policies. It extends the ResourceClaim, ResourceClaimStatus, and DeviceClass APIs with new fields and introduces the PodSchedulingContext kind to coordinate allocation between the scheduler and DRA drivers.

KEP-5573.title: Remove cgroup v1 support
KEP-5573.summary: This KEP deprecates and plans for removal of cgroup v1 support in Kubernetes, changing the kubelet configuration default to fail on cgroup v1 nodes and updating warnings, documentation, and testing. It aligns Kubernetes with the broader ecosystem shift to cgroup v2, giving users clear guidance and a path toward eventual code removal.

KEP-2249.title: Namespace Selector for Pod Affinity
KEP-2249.summary: This KEP adds a NamespaceSelector field to PodAffinityTerm, allowing users to select namespaces for pod affinity/anti-affinity using label selectors instead of a static list. It also introduces a new quota scope, CrossNamespaceAffinity, enabling operators to limit which namespaces can use cross‑namespace affinity, mitigating potential security and performance concerns.

KEP-5598.title: Opportunistic batching
KEP-5598.summary: The KEP introduces opportunistic batching in the Kubernetes scheduler by adding a pod scheduling signature and a batching mechanism that can reuse scheduling results for multiple pods with matching signatures. This improves scheduling performance for large workloads and lays groundwork for future gang scheduling capabilities.

KEP-3695.title: Extend the PodResources API to include resources allocated by DRA
KEP-3695.summary: This KEP extends the kubelet's PodResources gRPC API to expose resources allocated by Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA). It adds a new `dynamic_resources` field to each container's resource description and introduces a `Get` RPC to retrieve resources for a specific pod, enabling node monitoring agents to observe DRA‑allocated resources.

KEP-902.title: Add NonPreempting Option For PriorityClasses
KEP-902.summary: This KEP introduces a boolean Preempting field to PriorityClass and PodSpec, allowing users to create non-preempting PriorityClasses. When set to false, pods of that class will not trigger preemption of lower-priority pods, enabling stable scheduling of batch workloads without discarding in‑progress work.

KEP-3838.title: Pod Mutable Scheduling Directives
KEP-3838.summary: This KEP makes the pod's node selector and node affinity mutable while the pod is blocked by a scheduling readiness gate, allowing external controllers to influence pod placement before scheduling. It enables lightweight custom schedulers to adjust where a pod should run without replacing kube-scheduler.

KEP-5055.title: DRA: device taints and tolerations
KEP-5055.summary: This KEP adds support for device taints and tolerations in the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) framework. DRA drivers can publish taints on devices via ResourceSlices, and administrators can create DeviceTaintRule objects to apply taints to selected devices, preventing new pod scheduling and optionally evicting existing pods unless they tolerate the taint.

KEP-4832.title: Asynchronous Preemption
KEP-4832.summary: This KEP proposes decoupling preemption API calls from the scheduling cycle by making them asynchronous, allowing the scheduler to continue scheduling other pods while preemption actions are performed. The change aims to improve scheduling throughput in failure scenarios without altering functional behavior.

KEP-2926.title: Mutable Node Scheduling Directives for Jobs
KEP-2926.summary: This KEP proposes relaxing the immutability of a Job's pod template scheduling fields (node affinity, node selector, tolerations, annotations, and labels) for jobs that have never been unsuspended. By allowing these fields to be mutated before a job starts, higher‑level queue controllers can dynamically inject placement constraints, enabling more flexible batch job scheduling without altering the core job controller.

KEP-785.title: Scheduler Component Config API
KEP-785.summary: This KEP introduces and graduates the kube-scheduler component configuration API (kubescheduler.config.k8s.io) through multiple versions (v1beta1, v1beta2, v1beta3) to GA v1, allowing cluster operators to declaratively configure the scheduler via API objects instead of command‑line flags. The graduated API provides versioned, validated, and extensible scheduler configuration, improving stability, upgrade safety, and configurability of scheduling plugins and profiles.

KEP-4815.title: DRA Partitionable Devices
KEP-4815.summary: This KEP extends the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) framework to support partitionable devices, enabling the scheduler to allocate dynamic partitions of GPUs (e.g., NVIDIA MIG) and multi‑host devices such as TPUs. By introducing structured parameters that describe overlapping device partitions, vendors can create partitions on‑demand after scheduling, improving resource utilization without changing the user‑facing ResourceClaim API.

KEP-5278.title: Nominated node name for an expected pod placement
KEP-5278.summary: This KEP proposes reusing the existing `NominatedNodeName` field on Pods to convey the scheduler’s expected placement before the pod is actually bound. Exposing this information allows external components like the Cluster Autoscaler to make better decisions and enables the scheduler to resume binding work after restarts, reducing latency and preventing unnecessary scaling actions.

KEP-4816.title: DRA Prioritized List
KEP-4816.summary: The DRA Structured Parameters feature introduced device-specific ResourceClaims, but lacked a way to express preferences among multiple device types. This KEP adds a prioritized list of alternative device requests, allowing workloads to specify preferences and enabling the scheduler and autoscalers to select the best available devices, improving scheduleability of scarce resources like GPUs.

KEP-1923.title: Prefer Nominated Node
KEP-1923.summary: The PreferNominatedNode KEP changes the scheduler to evaluate a pod's nominated node first during the scheduling cycle, assigning the pod to that node if it still fits. This optimization reduces scheduling latency, especially in large clusters where preempted pods often can only be scheduled on their nominated node.

KEP-5471.title: Extended Toleration Operators for Threshold-Based Placement
KEP-5471.summary: This KEP extends core/v1 Toleration to support numeric comparison operators (Lt, Gt) for matching node taints, enabling threshold‑based placement such as SLA or reliability values. It provides a familiar, policy‑oriented mechanism that includes eviction semantics via NoExecute, allowing workloads to opt‑in to nodes meeting numeric criteria without modifying every pod's NodeAffinity.

KEP-268.title: Promote Pod Priority and Preemption to GA
KEP-268.summary: This KEP graduates Pod Priority and Preemption to General Availability by promoting the existing v1beta1 API to a stable v1 API in the scheduling.k8s.io group. It introduces the PriorityClass resource in the v1 version and updates the codebase and documentation to use the new stable API, ensuring stable, reliable scheduling of high‑priority Pods.

KEP-3902.title: Decouple TaintManager from NodeLifeCycleController
KEP-3902.summary: This KEP splits the existing NodeLifecycleController into two separate controllers: a NodeLifecycleController that only adds NoExecute taints to unhealthy nodes, and a new TaintEvictionController that handles pod eviction based on those taints. The separation improves code organization, maintainability, and allows custom implementations or disabling of taint‑based eviction.

KEP-4671.title: Gang Scheduling
KEP-4671.summary: This KEP introduces a new core resource, Workload, and a pod spec.workloadRef field to enable gang scheduling in kube-scheduler. By grouping pods into workload-defined PodGroups, the scheduler can wait until all pods in a group are ready before binding them, ensuring coordinated start for parallel applications.

KEP-382.title: Graduate TaintNodeByCondition to GA
KEP-382.summary: This KEP graduates the TaintNodeByCondition feature to GA, enabling the node lifecycle controller to automatically add taints based on node conditions. By using taints instead of condition predicates, the default scheduler can more reliably avoid scheduling pods onto unsuitable nodes.

KEP-2891.title: Simplified Scheduler Config
KEP-2891.summary: This KEP adds a new “MultiPoint” extension point to the kube-scheduler configuration, allowing a plugin to be enabled across all (or a subset of) scheduler extension points with a single config entry. It simplifies scheduler plugin configuration for cluster administrators while preserving the flexibility of the scheduling framework.

KEP-3243.title: Respect PodTopologySpread after rolling upgrades
KEP-3243.summary: This KEP adds a new field, `matchLabelKeys`, to the `TopologySpreadConstraint` in pod specifications. The field lets the scheduler consider only the values of specified label keys when calculating pod topology spread, enabling spreading to be scoped to a Deployment revision during rolling upgrades and eliminating the need for manual label management or external deschedulers.

KEP-1819.title: Scheduler Extender
KEP-1819.summary: The Scheduler Extender KEP adds the ability for the Kubernetes scheduler to call out to external HTTP/HTTPS endpoints for filter, prioritize, bind, and preempt phases, enabling custom scheduling logic without recompiling the scheduler. This extensibility allows external processes, written in any language, to influence pod placement and preemption decisions.

KEP-4247.title: Per-plugin callback functions for efficient requeueing in the scheduling queue
KEP-4247.summary: Introduces a per‑plugin QueueingHint callback that lets scheduler plugins suggest how a pod should be re‑queued, allowing pods to be retried only when they are likely to become schedulable and enabling plugins to skip backoff. This reduces unnecessary scheduling retries, improves throughput, and speeds up scheduling for workloads using dynamic resource allocation.

KEP-1258.title: Default Pod Topology Spread
KEP-1258.summary: This KEP adds a configurable default set of PodTopologySpread constraints that cluster operators can set at the cluster level. Pods without explicit topologySpreadConstraints will automatically receive these defaults, improving pod spreading without requiring authors to know the cluster topology.

KEP-3094.title: Take taints/tolerations into consideration when calculating PodTopologySpread skew
KEP-3094.summary: This KEP adds an optional feature that allows users to include or ignore node taints/tolerations when calculating PodTopologySpread skew. It introduces two new fields in the TopologySpreadConstraint API to explicitly define node inclusion policies, giving finer control over spread calculations and preventing unexpected pending pods on tainted nodes.

KEP-5229.title: Asynchronous API calls during scheduling
KEP-5229.summary: This KEP introduces a kube-scheduler-wide framework for making all API calls during scheduling asynchronous. By decoupling API calls from the scheduling cycle and handling them via a dedicated queue/cache component, it aims to improve scheduling performance and reduce latency.

KEP-986.title: Resource Quota Scope Selectors
KEP-986.summary: This KEP graduates the ResourceQuotaScopeSelectors feature to GA, allowing cluster administrators to define default ResourceQuotas with scope selectors that permit critical pods only in the kube-system namespace. By doing so, it removes the longstanding limitation that critical pods could only be created in kube-system, while retaining safety via admission control.

KEP-624.title: Scheduling Framework
KEP-624.summary: The Scheduling Framework KEP introduces a plugin-based architecture for the Kubernetes scheduler, providing multiple extensible extension points throughout the scheduling and binding cycles. By compiling plugins into the scheduler binary and configuring them via ComponentConfig, the core scheduler logic stays simpler while allowing custom and out‑of‑tree scheduler features to be added efficiently.

KEP-964.title: Extending RequestedToCapacityRatio Priority Function to support Resource Bin Packing of Extended Resources - @sudeshsh
KEP-964.summary: This KEP extends the RequestedToCapacityRatio priority function to support resource bin packing for both core and extended resources using user‑specified weights. It enables best‑fit scheduling, reducing fragmentation of scarce resources such as accelerators and improving pod placement efficiency.

KEP-2372.title: Resource Quota based on Node Labels
KEP-2372.summary: This KEP proposes extending the ResourceQuota API to allow quotas to be applied based on node label selectors, enabling administrators to restrict namespace resource consumption by hardware type, zone, or compliance requirements. It introduces a new spec field (podNodeSelector) and a new resource scope to tie node affinity/selector criteria to quota enforcement.

KEP-5142.title: Pop pod from backoffQ when activeQ is empty
KEP-5142.summary: This KEP enhances the kube-scheduler by allowing it to pop pods directly from the backoff queue when the active queue is empty, improving scheduling throughput and reducing idle time. It also ensures PreEnqueue plugins are invoked when pods enter the backoff queue, while preserving backoff behavior for error retries.

KEP-1451.title: Multi Scheduling Profiles
KEP-1451.summary: This KEP adds support for multiple scheduling profiles in the kube-scheduler component config, allowing a single scheduler binary to run different plugin configurations based on the pod's .spec.schedulerName. Operators can define distinct profiles, each with its own set of plugins and settings, enabling heterogeneous workloads to be scheduled with tailored behavior without running multiple scheduler instances.

KEP-3280.title: Guarantee PodDisruptionBudget When Preemption Happens
KEP-3280.summary: This KEP proposes adding a new field `allowDisruptionByPriorityGreaterThanOrEqual` to the PriorityClass API so that administrators can specify the minimum pod priority required to violate a PodDisruptionBudget during scheduler preemption. By making PDB guarantees configurable, the change improves high‑availability guarantees for critical workloads while preserving preemption semantics.

KEP-583.title: Coscheduling
KEP-583.summary: The Coscheduling KEP introduces a new PodGroup custom resource to enable gang scheduling of related pods, ensuring that a group of tasks only starts when sufficient resources are available for the defined minimum members. This solves deadlock scenarios for batch and machine learning workloads by allowing coordinated scheduling and provides extensions for resource reservation and lifecycle management via annotations and controllers.

KEP-3633.title: Introduce MatchLabelKeys and MismatchLabelKeys to PodAffinity and PodAntiAffinity
KEP-3633.summary: This KEP adds optional fields `matchLabelKeys` and `mismatchLabelKeys` to PodAffinityTerm, allowing users to restrict which Pods are considered when evaluating required or preferred PodAffinity and PodAntiAffinity rules. The change improves scheduling correctness during rolling updates and other scenarios where pods need to be grouped by specific label keys.

KEP-548.title: Graduate ScheduleDaemonSetPods to GA
KEP-548.summary: This KEP graduates the ScheduleDaemonSetPods feature to GA, making DaemonSet pod scheduling solely the responsibility of the default scheduler by attaching node affinity to DaemonSet pods. It removes the scheduling-related logic from the DaemonSet controller, simplifying the controller and reducing duplication of scheduling code.

KEP-2458.title: Preferred Fit Strategy
KEP-2458.summary: The KEP consolidates multiple resource‑fit scoring plugins (LeastAllocated, MostAllocated, RequestedToCapacityRatio) into a single configurable plugin (NodeResourcesFit) by introducing a ScoringStrategy field, simplifying scheduler configuration and paving the way for future strategies. This reduces configuration complexity and prepares the scheduler for pod‑level resource fit preferences.

KEP-5027.title: DRA: admin-controlled device attributes
KEP-5027.summary: This KEP introduces a new cluster‑scoped API type, ResourceSlicePatch, that lets privileged users (typically cluster administrators) override or extend device attributes and capacities published by DRA drivers. By applying patches based on CEL selectors or other criteria, the scheduler merges these admin‑controlled attributes with the driver‑provided ones, enabling admin‑controlled device taints and other adjustments without modifying driver code.

KEP-3022.title: Tuning the number of domains in PodTopologySpread
KEP-3022.summary: This KEP introduces a new optional field `minDomains` to the PodSpec TopologySpreadConstraint, allowing users to specify a minimum number of topology domains (e.g., nodes, zones) over which Pods must be spread when `whenUnsatisfiable=DoNotSchedule`. This helps ensure better distribution and can trigger cluster-autoscaler provisioning when insufficient domains exist.

KEP-5007.title: DRA Device Binding Conditions
KEP-5007.summary: This KEP introduces BindingConditions, a mechanism that defers Pod binding until external resources such as fabric-attached GPUs or FPGAs are confirmed ready. By extending the DRA APIs (ResourceSlice, DeviceRequestAllocationResult, and ResourceClaim) with condition fields, the scheduler can wait for readiness and avoid premature binding, improving reliability for asynchronous or failure‑prone devices.

KEP-5501.title: Reflect PreEnqueue rejections in Pod status
KEP-5501.summary: This KEP adds the ability for the kube-scheduler to reflect PreEnqueue plugin rejections in a Pod's status by setting a condition with a descriptive reason and message. The feature improves observability and debugging by providing users immediate feedback on why a Pod is not being scheduled, while leveraging asynchronous API calls to avoid impacting scheduler performance.

KEP-5004.title: DRA Extended Resource
KEP-5004.summary: This KEP adds support for advertising Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) devices as extended resources through a new DeviceClass field, enabling pods to request such devices using the familiar extended resource syntax. It also introduces a pod status field to track the special ResourceClaim created by the scheduler, allowing a gradual migration from device plugins to DRA without modifying existing applications.

KEP-5234.title: DRA ResourceSlice Mixins
KEP-5234.summary: This KEP introduces mixins to the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) ResourceSlice API, allowing drivers to define reusable metadata for devices and counter sets. By referencing mixins, duplication is reduced and more devices can be represented within a single ResourceSlice, improving scalability and efficiency.

KEP-895.title: Pod Topology Spread
KEP-895.summary: PodTopologySpread introduces TopologySpreadConstraint fields to pod specifications, enabling users to define hard or soft constraints that spread pods evenly across topology domains such as zones or nodes. This improves high availability and resource utilization by preventing pod concentration and providing controlled tolerance for unsatisfiable spreads.

KEP-2291.title: Presubmit config inside the tested repo
KEP-2291.summary: This KEP proposes adding the ability to define Prow presubmit jobs inside the same repository that contains the code being tested, via a prow.yaml file. It makes presubmit configuration versioned with the code, simplifying testing, branching, and collaboration while remaining optional and opt‑in.

KEP-3521.title: Pod Scheduling Readiness
KEP-3521.summary: This KEP adds a new .spec.schedulingGates field to the Pod API, enabling controllers or mutating webhooks to mark a Pod as not ready for scheduling until the gates are cleared. The scheduler will keep Pods with non‑nil schedulingGates in an internal unschedulable pool, reducing unnecessary scheduling cycles and improving overall scheduling throughput.

KEP-5468.title: Invariant Testing
KEP-5468.summary: The Invariant Testing KEP introduces a framework for running cluster-wide invariant checks after the entire e2e test suite completes. It adds sentinel tests and after-suite logic to enforce ownership, opt-in/out controls, and structured reporting, aiming to reduce flaky tests and improve observability of cluster-wide invariants without impacting conformance tests.

KEP-3041.title: NodeConformance and NodeFeature labels cleanup
KEP-3041.summary: This KEP proposes a cleanup and clarification of test labeling in the Kubernetes test suite, introducing explicit `[FeatureGate:]` and `[Environment:]` labels and redefining the semantics of existing `[Feature:]`, `[NodeFeature:]`, and `[NodeConformance]` labels. The changes aim to make test selection, skipping, and environments more consistent and easier to query without impacting the core API.

KEP-2420.title: Reducing Kubernetes Build Maintenance
KEP-2420.summary: This KEP proposes to eliminate the duplicate Bazel build system from the main Kubernetes repository, consolidating builds to the existing Make-based system. By removing Bazel tooling and related CI jobs, it reduces maintenance toil, simplifies Golang upgrades, and decreases friction for contributors and maintainers.

KEP-2539.title: Continuously Deploy K8s Prow
KEP-2539.summary: This KEP proposes automating the deployment of Kubernetes Prow by continuously merging autobump PRs on a regular schedule, eliminating manual approval and Slack notifications. It aims to reduce on‑call workload and streamline upgrades while relying on existing monitoring and alerting to catch any regressions.

KEP-2464.title: Kubetest2 CI Migration
KEP-2464.summary: This KEP proposes migrating Kubernetes release‑blocking and merge‑blocking CI jobs from the deprecated kubetest and scenario scripts to the newer kubetest2 tool. It outlines a phased approach—creating canary jobs, monitoring stability, and then making kubetest2 the default launcher—to reduce maintenance burden and enable deprecation of legacy testing infrastructure.

KEP-714.title: Breaking apart the Kubernetes test tarball
KEP-714.summary: This KEP proposes replacing the monolithic `kubernetes-test.tar.gz` release artifact with multiple platform‑specific test tarballs, mirroring the pattern used for client, node, and server tarballs. By breaking the test tarball into per‑platform binaries and a portable source tarball, the download size for users is reduced and it simplifies integration with Bazel and cross‑compilation workflows.

KEP-1933.title: Defend against accidental credential logging via static analysis interation into Prow.
KEP-1933.summary: This KEP proposes integrating the go-flow-levee taint propagation static analysis tool into Prow's presubmit testing to detect accidental logging of secrets in Kubernetes code. By catching secret logging early, it helps prevent credential exposure in logs and improves security hygiene.

KEP-2290.title: New label for trusted PR identification
KEP-2290.summary: The KEP introduces a new `ok-to-test` label that replaces scanning comment commands to identify trusted pull requests in the test-infra trigger plugin. By applying this label via the `/ok-to-test` command, the system simplifies trust determination, reduces API token usage, and prevents race conditions when starting test jobs.

KEP-3203.title: Auto-refreshing official CVE feed
KEP-3203.summary: This KEP introduces an automated process that periodically generates a machine‑readable JSON feed of official Kubernetes CVEs and publishes it to the website, enabling users to programmatically consume up‑to‑date vulnerability information. It adds a Prow job, GitHub issue labeling, and GCS storage to keep the CVE list refreshed without manual effort.

KEP-2763.title: Support Ambient Capabilities in Kubernetes.
KEP-2763.summary: This KEP adds support for Linux ambient capabilities in Kubernetes by introducing a new field in the Pod securityContext that allows users to specify capabilities that persist across execve without requiring root privileges. It enables non‑root containers to obtain necessary capabilities without modifying container images, improving security and usability across container runtimes such as containerd and CRI‑O.

KEP-1645.title: Multi-Cluster Services API
KEP-1645.summary: The Multi-Cluster Services API introduces a new set of CRDs (ServiceExport and ServiceImport) that enable Kubernetes services to be discovered and consumed across multiple clusters within a clusterset. It provides a minimal, extensible API for exporting services from one cluster and importing them in others, allowing multi‑cluster service consumption with behavior consistent with in‑cluster services.

KEP-5339.title: ClusterProfile credentials plugin
KEP-5339.summary: This KEP introduces a pluggable credentials provider mechanism for ClusterProfile resources, allowing controllers to obtain cluster credentials via external exec plugins. It adds a new credentialProviders field to ClusterProfile status, standardizing how credentials are defined and retrieved without embedding logic in controllers.

KEP-2149.title: ClusterID for ClusterSet Identification
