KEP-2149.summary: This KEP introduces a cluster‑scoped ClusterProperty custom resource to store cluster‑level metadata, providing a unique, immutable cluster ID and ClusterSet membership information for use in multi‑cluster services. By standardizing how cluster identifiers are recorded, it enables reliable cluster discovery, DNS disambiguation, and enrichment of logs and metrics across clusters in a ClusterSet.

KEP-4322.title: Cluster Profile API
KEP-4322.summary: The KEP proposes a universal ClusterProfile API to provide a standardized inventory of Kubernetes clusters for multi‑cluster management solutions. By defining a common interface for cluster discovery, status reporting, and properties, it enables tools such as schedulers, GitOps systems, and operations platforms to interact with clusters without being tied to specific implementations.

KEP-5313.title: Placement Decision API
KEP-5313.summary: The KEP introduces a vendor‑neutral, read‑only PlacementDecision API that standardizes the output of multicluster placement calculations. It provides a namespaced list of selected clusters, allowing any scheduler to emit decisions and any consumer to read them, reducing integration complexity across multicluster tools.

KEP-5679.title: Fallback for HPA on failure to retrieve metrics
KEP-5679.summary: This KEP adds an optional fallback configuration to the ExternalMetricSource used by the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, allowing a static replica count to be applied when external metric retrieval fails for a configurable duration. The feature improves reliability of autoscaling workloads that depend on out‑of‑cluster metrics by preventing stalls during provider outages.

KEP-5882.title: Deployment Pod Replacement Policy
KEP-5882.summary: This KEP introduces a new .spec.podReplacementPolicy field to Deployments, allowing users to control whether new pods are created only after terminating pods have fully terminated or immediately after termination starts. The feature provides consistent behavior across rollout strategies and scaling operations, helping to manage resource usage and scheduling predictability.

KEP-5966.title: etcd RangeStream
KEP-5966.summary: This KEP introduces a new server‑streaming etcd RPC called RangeStream that returns Range results in incremental chunks, reducing server‑side memory spikes and eliminating redundant count computation during client‑side pagination. By integrating the RPC into the kube‑apiserver (via a feature gate) and the watch cache, large list operations can be processed more efficiently, improving performance and scalability of Kubernetes control plane components.

KEP-5793.title: Manifest Based Admission Control Config
KEP-5793.summary: This KEP introduces manifest‑based admission control configuration, allowing kube‑apiserver to load admission webhook and policy objects from disk at startup and watch them for dynamic updates. By moving critical admission policies out of the Kubernetes API, it guarantees enforcement before the API server processes requests, prevents bypass through the API, and provides a bootstrapping security mechanism.

KEP-5541.title: Report Last Used Time On a PVC
KEP-5541.summary: This KEP adds an optional `UnusedSince` timestamp field to the `PersistentVolumeClaimStatus` to record when a PVC last transitioned to not being used by any Pod. The field is populated by the PVC protection controller when the last referencing Pod terminates, allowing administrators to identify and clean up stale PVCs. The feature is behind the `PersistentVolumeClaimUnusedSinceTime` feature gate.

KEP-5681.title: Conditional Authorization
KEP-5681.summary: Conditional Authorization extends the Kubernetes authorizer to return a set of conditions that must be satisfied by resource data (labels, fields) before a request can be allowed. It adds condition support to SubjectAccessReview APIs and introduces a new AuthorizationConditionsReview API, enabling fine‑grained, policy‑driven access control that spans authorization and admission while preserving backward compatibility.

KEP-5866.title: Server-side Sharded List and Watch
KEP-5866.summary: The KEP adds server‑side sharded LIST and WATCH support to the kube‑apiserver, letting clients specify a shard range so the API server filters events at the source. This reduces network traffic and client CPU/memory usage, enabling efficient horizontal scaling of controllers such as kube‑state‑metrics.

KEP-4563.title: EvictionRequest API
KEP-4563.summary: The EvictionRequest API introduces a declarative resource that enables cooperative pod termination, allowing applications and controllers to coordinate evictions before falling back to the existing eviction mechanism. This improves safety, observability, and flexibility for node draining, descheduling, and autoscaling scenarios, addressing limitations of current Eviction API and PodDisruptionBudgets.

KEP-5707.title: Deprecate Service.spec.externalIPs
KEP-5707.summary: This KEP deprecates the Service.spec.externalIPs field and removes its implementation in kube-proxy, introducing a feature gate (AllowServiceExternalIPs) to disable the functionality. The change improves cluster security by preventing unprivileged users from claiming arbitrary external IPs and encourages migration to safer alternatives like LoadBalancer services, Ingress, or Gateway API.

KEP-5758.title: Per-container ulimits configuration
KEP-5758.summary: This KEP introduces a `ulimits` field in the Container SecurityContext, enabling per‑container POSIX resource limit configuration such as nofile, nproc, and memlock. The change propagates through the CRI to container runtimes, integrates with node‑declared feature detection, and is gated by the Privileged level of the Pod Security Standards.

KEP-5677.title: DRA Resource Availability Visibility
KEP-5677.summary: The KEP introduces a new ResourcePoolStatusRequest API that lets users query the available capacity of device resource pools in a DRA-enabled cluster. By following the CSR pattern, the request is processed once by a controller in kube-controller-manager, populating status with per‑pool totals, allocations, and availability, thereby improving debugging, capacity planning, and cross‑namespace visibility.

KEP-5808.title: Native Histogram Support for Kubernetes Metrics
KEP-5808.summary: This KEP adds support for Prometheus Native Histograms to Kubernetes component metrics via a new feature gate, allowing components to expose both classic and native histogram formats simultaneously. The change reduces storage overhead and improves query performance while maintaining backward compatibility, enabling a gradual migration for users.

KEP-5304.title: DRA Device Attributes Downward API
KEP-5304.summary: The KEP adds a framework‑assisted way for Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) drivers to expose device attributes to containers via CDI‑mounted JSON files. Drivers populate a Metadata field in PrepareResult, and the kubelet plugin writes per‑request metadata files that are bind‑mounted into the pod, enabling workloads (e.g., KubeVirt, SR‑IOV) to discover device details without custom controllers or Downward API changes.

KEP-5547.title: Integrate Workload APIs with Job Controller
KEP-5547.summary: This KEP adds native integration between the Job controller and the Workload/PodGroup gang scheduling APIs. The Job controller will automatically create Workload and PodGroup objects for eligible parallel Jobs, enabling gang scheduling semantics without requiring external controllers.

KEP-3541.title: Add Recreate Update Strategy to StatefulSet
KEP-3541.summary: This KEP introduces a new Recreate update strategy for StatefulSets, allowing all pods to be deleted and recreated during an update, similar to Deployments' Recreate strategy. It provides a predictable way to recover from stuck pods without manual intervention, benefiting workloads that can tolerate downtime such as CI/CD pipelines and stateless applications using StatefulSets.

KEP-5729.title: DRA: ResourceClaim Support for Workloads
KEP-5729.summary: This KEP extends the Workload and PodGroup APIs to allow ResourceClaims and ResourceClaimTemplates to be associated with these higher‑level workload objects. By reserving a ResourceClaim for an entire PodGroup, it enables sharing DRA resources across many Pods, overcoming the 256‑entry limit and simplifying claim lifecycle management for large AI/ML workloads.

KEP-5732.title: Topology-aware workload scheduling
KEP-5732.summary: This KEP extends the Kubernetes Workload API with scheduling constraints that allow a PodGroup to specify topology and DRA requirements, enabling the kube-scheduler to place multi‑pod workloads within specific topological domains or shared DRA resources. By introducing Placement concepts and new scheduler framework plugin interfaces, it provides a native, high‑fidelity mechanism for topology‑aware workload scheduling.

KEP-5832.title: Decouple PodGroup API
KEP-5832.summary: This KEP decouples the PodGroup API from the Workload API by introducing PodGroup as a standalone runtime object in scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha2. It adds new fields to Workload and Pod specs to reference PodGroup templates and scheduling groups, enabling independent lifecycle, improved scalability, and clearer status ownership for gang scheduling.

KEP-5491.title: DRA: List Types for Attributes
KEP-5491.summary: This KEP adds support for list‑typed attributes in the DRA DeviceAttribute schema, allowing drivers to expose sets of values such as multiple PCIe roots or NUMA nodes. It also redefines the semantics of ResourceClaim matchAttribute and distinctAttribute constraints to operate on list intersections, while preserving backward compatibility with scalar attributes.

KEP-5554.title: In-place Update Pod Resources alognside Static CPU Manager Policy
KEP-5554.summary: This KEP extends the In‑place Resource Resize feature to work with pods that use the static CPU manager policy and have Guaranteed QoS. It enables safe CPU limit increases and decreases without restarting containers while preserving the original CPU allocation and NUMA affinity.

KEP-5710.title: Workload-aware preemption
KEP-5710.summary: This KEP extends the Workload and PodGroup APIs to define preemption units and pod group priorities, enabling the kube-scheduler to perform workload-aware preemption. By treating groups of tightly-coupled pods as a single preemption unit, it reduces disruptive partial preemptions and improves resource utilization for AI and multi-host workloads.

KEP-5825.title: CRI List Streaming
KEP-5825.summary: This KEP adds server‑side streaming RPCs to the Container Runtime Interface (CRI) for list operations, such as StreamContainers and StreamPodSandboxes, allowing results to be sent one item at a time and avoiding the 16 MiB gRPC message size limit. The change preserves existing unary List* APIs for backward compatibility while enabling nodes with large numbers of containers or pods to operate without RPC failures.

KEP-5517.title: DRA Node Allocatable Resources
KEP-5517.summary: This KEP adds a unified accounting model that integrates node allocatable resources managed via Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) with the kube-scheduler and kubelet. By synchronizing the standard NodeResourcesFit plugin and the DRA DynamicResources plugin, it prevents overcommitment and enables the kubelet to correctly calculate QoS, configure cgroups, and enforce resource isolation.
